WASHINGTON — The Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan would require a massive hike in annual costs in comparison to the average shipbuilding appropriations in recent years, according to a new report from the Congressional Budget Office.

Specifically, the Navy’s [shipbuilding plan released in May](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/04/omb-director-rebukes-shipbuilders-over-production-delays/) would average out to an annual cost of roughly $53.8 billion — totaling a 41 percent increase from the roughly $38.1 billion the Navy has secured annually in appropriations during the last half decade, the CBO report released Thursday said.

This estimate factors in costs stemming from refueling nuclear-powered ships, and procuring non-battle force ships such as used sealift ships, among other things — costs that are not factored into the Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan, even though such expenses are typically derived from shipbuilding funding, CBO said. As a result, those factors increase the CBO’s estimate of the Navy’s average annual shipbuilding costs by roughly $4.6 billion in comparison to the Navy’s shipbuilding plan. Altogether, this marks an unprecedented level of spending for shipbuilding.

“The cost of the Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan is high not only compared with recent funding but also by historical standards,” the report said. “Over the past decade, funding for ship construction has reached its highest levels since the Reagan Administration’s defense buildup in the 1980s. Since 2016, lawmakers have generally appropriated an average of $2.5 billion more per year for shipbuilding than the President has requested, partly because of concerns that the fleet is too small to perform all its missions.”

Accounting for only purchasing new ships in the recent shipbuilding plan, CBO estimates those ships would rack up to $1.47 trillion in 2026 dollars over 30 years. That’s an increase from the Navy’s estimate of $1.23 trillion over 30 years, per the report. CBO attributed these differences in new ship construction estimates to differences in “assumptions about the design and capabilities of some future ships.” Additionally, CBO acknowledged that it employed different estimating methods and accounted for growth of labor and material costs differently than the Navy.

The Navy’s [shipbuilding plan and budget request](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/05/navy-pushes-congress-to-back-constructing-auxiliary-ships-overseas/) seeks a total of $65.8 billion for shipbuilding alone for FY27.To advance the Trump administration’s Golden Fleet initiative, it calls for expanding the Navy’s inventory to 450 ships, including battle force ships, auxiliary ships, and unmanned vessels, by 2031.

“The pace of shipbuilding would be fastest in the next 10 years, reflecting the service’s desire to increase the size of the fleet as quickly as feasible,” the CBO report said. “It would slow from the mid-2030s to the mid-2040s; then construction would ramp up again in the late 2040s and 2050s to replace smaller ships, with a service life of 20 to 25 years, purchased in the first decade of the plan.”

content:
资料照片：2021年3月10日，民主党众议员阿米·贝拉在华盛顿国会山举行的众议院外交事务委员会听证会上发言。
众议院民主党人正在讨论下一届国会是否继续保留美国与中国共产党战略竞争特设委员会(简称中国问题特设委员会)。一些民主党人认为，众议院外交事务委员会及其下属的亚太小组委员会已经能够承担该委员会的部分监督和政策工作，没有必要维持一个单独的特设委员会。不过，也有民主党人主张保留这一委员会，继续发挥其现有职能。
众议院外交事务委员会亚太小组委员会首席民主党议员阿米·贝拉(Ami Bera)在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时表示，众议院现有委员会可以承担中国问题特设委员会的许多工作，而如果成立一个特设小组委员会，也可以与外委会现有的工作形成互补。
“如果决定设立一个特设小组委员会，我认为这将与我们在众议院外交事务委员会开展的工作形成互补,”贝拉众议员对美国之音说。
贝拉预计将在明年新一届国会中出任众议院外交事务委员会亚太小组委员会主席。
这位来自加利福尼亚州的民主党众议员还表示，即将出任众议院议长的民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯(Hakeem Jeffries)正在听取相关委员会人士的意见，再决定如何处理中国问题特设委员会的未来。
贝拉对美国之音说：“即将出任众议院议长的杰弗里斯正在听取相关委员会以及即将担任委员会主席的人士的意见。我相信，他会听取各方观点，并作出正确的决定。是的，还有很多工作需要做。”
贝拉说，明年执掌众议院外交事务委员会亚太小组委员会后，维护印太地区的和平与稳定将是他的首要政策目标之一。此外，人工智能发展带来的挑战，以及加强美国与地区盟友的合作，也将是重点议题。
“维护该地区的和平与稳定将是一个总体性的核心议题。随着人工智能技术迅速发展，我们必须明确需要建立哪些防护机制，以及如何与北京保持必要的沟通和政策框架，”贝拉说。
他还表示，美国需要维护和加强与日本、韩国的三边联盟关系，重建地区国家对美国承诺的信心，同时恢复并加强四方安全对话机制(QUAD)。
“此外，我们还需要维护美国、日本和韩国的三边联盟关系，恢复并巩固这些联盟，让相关国家和各方重拾信心。同时，恢复并加强四方安全对话机制(QUAD)也至关重要。所以，需要做的事情并不少”贝拉说。
据美国政治新闻网站Semafor报道，众议院外交事务委员会首席民主党成员、纽约州联邦众议员格雷戈里·米克斯(Gregory Meeks)的发言人表示，民主党将听从下一届众议院议长对中国问题特设委员会未来安排的决定。不过，这位发言人强调，无论委员会架构如何调整，众议院外委会都有能力监督政府对中国的政策。
杰弗里斯尚未明确表态是否支持保留中国问题特设委员会。他在11月17日的一场记者会上表示，民主党党团完成下一届国会领导层的遴选程序后，将就这一问题展开讨论。
“等我们完成组织程序后，最终会就这一问题展开讨论。组织程序的第一步当然是明天启动党内领导层选举，”杰弗里斯当时在记者会上说。
民主党在11月3日举行的中期选举中赢得众议院和参议院多数席位。第120届国会将于2027年1月3日开始任期，届时众议院全体议员将投票选举议长。
杰弗里斯获得党内提名后，仍未明确说明是否会保留中国问题特设委员会。该特设委员会于2023年1月成立，旨在跨党派推动美国国会就中国共产党带来的挑战形成共识，并制定保护美国人民、经济和价值观的行动方案。
随着民主党即将重新掌控众议院，中国问题特设委员会的存续及其未来职能，将成为新一届国会讨论美国对中国政策和国会监督机制时面临的问题之一。
目前担任众议院中国问题特设委员会主席的密歇根州共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)本月早些时候发表声明，呼吁下一届国会继续授权该委员会运作，让其“继续为美国人民开展跨党派工作”。
穆勒纳尔在声明中说：“近四年来，该特设委员会汇集了共和党和民主党议员，共同应对中国共产党对美国利益和价值观构成的严重威胁。我们与其他委员会以及两党政府部门合作，推动了多项重要政策调整，增强了美国实力，保护了美国人民。”
穆勒纳尔在接受美国之音采访时表示，他希望即将出任众议院议长的民主党领袖杰弗里斯能够认识到该委员会的价值。
“这一决定最终需要由民主党党团领导层作出，”穆勒纳尔对美国之音说，“议长或者说可能将成为议长的杰弗里斯在该委员会成立之初就参与其中，当时他与(时任议长)凯文·麦卡锡(Kevin McCarthy)并肩推动了委员会的成立。因此，他了解并认可该委员会的价值。不过，最终如何决定，仍需要由民主党党团内部讨论并作出决定。”
穆勒纳尔还表示，如果中国问题特设委员会在下届国会获得保留，他本人愿意继续参与委员会的工作。
“我确实认为，这是我们在国会能够开展的最重要的工作之一，其影响将延续数代人。因此，无论是从经济、人权还是国家安全的角度来看，保持对这场竞争的明确关注都至关重要，并确保美国在这场竞争中取得胜利，”穆勒纳尔说。
据美国政治新闻网站Politico报道，现任中国问题特设委员会首席民主党成员、加利福尼亚州联邦众议员罗·卡纳(Ro Khanna)也表示，希望下一届国会继续保留该委员会。
卡纳认为，中国问题特设委员会有望继续运作，但委员会的名称和具体职权范围可能发生调整。对于是否将其改为隶属于众议院外委会的下属小组委员会，卡纳表示，他预计该委员会仍将维持独立架构，不过民主党内部目前仍在就此进行讨论。
众院中国问题特设委员会调查后，几家美大型药企不再于新疆和中国军医院展开新临床试验

“日台友谊万岁”：离任特使片山告别
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
赖清德总统（右）在本月早些时候的仪式上，向即将离任的日本驻台最高代表片山一幸（左）授予台湾大绶星勋章。中央通讯社照片2026年11月18日
中新社台北11月23日电 即将离任的日本驻台首席代表片山一之周一告别台湾朋友，结束了在台的三年任期。
片山在 Facebook 上发帖纪念他在日台交流协会台北办事处的最后一天，他表示，自 2023 年 11 月抵达日本台湾关系以来，日台关系取得了重大进展。
片山举例说，日本和台湾在发生大地震和洪水等危机时继续相互支持。他列举了日本在2025年9月23日台风拉格莎期间堰塞湖泛滥造成严重破坏后花莲监测工作的捐款和援助，以及今年早些时候台湾在2026年熊本地震后向日本的捐款。
他说，其他成就包括取消对日本进口台湾红肉火龙果和杂交石斑鱼的禁令。
片山还表示，他很荣幸上周获得赖清德总统颁发的大绶光星勋章，以表彰他对双边关系的贡献。该勋章是台湾的最高荣誉之一，传统上授予外国高级官员。
他说：“我从包括总统在内的台湾各界所经历的热烈友谊和互动，是我在这里度过的最宝贵的财富。”他补充说，他的三年任期是他43年半外交生涯中最“有意义和充实的时期”。
他补充说：“日本与台湾的友谊万岁。台湾万岁。自由和民主万岁。”
东京和台北尚未宣布片山的继任者。
据日本媒体报道，日本前驻希腊大使伊藤晃一有望填补这一空缺。

'Long live Japan-Taiwan friendship': Departing envoy Katayama bids farewell

President Lai Ching-te (right) confers Kazuyuki Katayama (left), Japan's departing top representative to Taiwan, with Taiwan's Order of Brilliant Star with Grand Cordon in a ceremony earlier this month. CNA photo Nov. 18, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 23 (CNA) Kazuyuki Katayama, Japan's departing top representative to Taiwan, on Monday bid farewell to friends in Taiwan as he concluded his three-year tenure in the country.
In a Facebook post to mark his last day at the Japan-Taiwan Exchange Association's Taipei Office, Katayama said Japan-Taiwan relations had made significant progress since his arrival in November 2023.
For instance, Katayama said, Japan and Taiwan have continued to support each other in times of crisis, including major earthquakes and floods. He cited Japan's donation and assistance with monitoring efforts in Hualien following severe damage caused by overflow flooding from a barrier lake during Typhoon Ragasa on Sept. 23, 2025, as well as Taiwan's donation to Japan following the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake earlier this year.
Other achievements included the lifting of bans on imports of Taiwan's red-fleshed dragon fruit and hybrid grouper to Japan, he said.
Katayama also said he was honored to have received the Order of Brilliant Star with Grand Cordon from President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) last week in recognition of his contributions to bilateral ties. The decoration is among Taiwan's highest honors and is traditionally bestowed on senior foreign officials.
"The warm friendship and interactions I have experienced from all walks of life in Taiwan -- including from the president -- are the most precious treasures of my time here," he said, adding that his three-year tenure had been the most "meaningful and fulfilling period" of his 43-and-a-half-year diplomatic career.
"Long live Japan-Taiwan friendship. Long live Taiwan. Long live freedom and democracy," he added.
Tokyo and Taipei have not announced Katayama's successor.
According to Japanese media reports, former Japanese Ambassador to Greece Koichi Ito is expected to fill the vacancy.

title: Dispatch from 2032: After Chinese salvos fail to defeat Taiwan, Beijing is trapped in a war of attrition
zh_title: 2032年快讯：中国联军未能击败台湾，北京陷入消耗战
summary: 2032 年快讯：中国齐射未能击败台湾后，北京陷入消耗战 - 大西洋理事会的军舰和中国人民解放军 (PLA) 海军战斗机于 2018 年 4 月 12 日在南海参加军事展示。（路透社/斯金格，来自Reuters Connect）本文是斯考克罗夫特中心的系列文章“来自下一场战争的快讯”的一部分印度-太平洋安全倡议，其中我们的专家对世界下一场重大冲突在最有可能爆发的地区可能会是什么样子进行了假设：
content:
2032年快讯：中国的齐射未能击败台湾，北京陷入消耗战 - 大西洋理事会
2018 年 4 月 12 日，中国人民解放军 (PLA) 海军的军舰和战斗机参加在南海举行的军事展示。（路透社/斯金格，来自Reuters Connect）
本文是斯考克罗夫特中心印度-太平洋安全倡议系列“下一场战争的快报”的一部分，其中我们的专家对世界下一场重大冲突可能在最有可能爆发的地区印度-太平洋地区进行了假设。这些消息被称为虚构情报，或“FicInt”，在军队内部使用，让政策制定者为可能的未来做好准备。目的是防止下一场战争爆发。
2032 年，台北——中国第一批导弹和无人机在夜深人静时飞越台湾海峡。有些在咆哮的火焰喷射的推动下划过黑色的天空，而另一些则安静地、几乎看不见地以稳定的速度在黑暗的天空中嗡嗡作响。第一个被拦截导弹击中中国火柱摧毁，其他则在被激光闪光击中时爆炸。有些被小型拦截无人机撞到一边。一些人被自动炮和机枪的火幕击落，曳光弹在黑暗中摸索着目标，越来越多的条纹。
这些联合火力打击——中国对台战争中所宣称的第一次攻击——旨在摧毁台湾的防御，使其军事力量丧失能力，并粉碎台湾人的战斗意志。尽管这些齐射令人恐惧且令人印象深刻，但它们未能实现中国的目标。
一些袭击成功了，坠入港口、机场和军事基地，并向天空喷出滚滚火焰和浓烟。北起台北，南至高雄，台湾一次又一次遭到无情的打击。虽然台湾军事力量的来源是中国的目标，但许多平民也因这次袭击而被屠杀。世界领导人最初等着看台湾是否能够承受住这场冲击，或者是否会像许多分析人士预测的那样迅速崩溃。
但事实证明，台湾的多层防空和导弹防御系统“T-Dome”出乎意料地有效。尽管该公司在 2027 年首次投入运营时（即 2025 年宣布成立两年后）面临性能困难，但其许多自主系统的可靠性迅速成熟。随着中国入侵台湾领空和侵略性海上骚扰的行为逐年变得更加频繁和充满敌意，台湾的总统和指挥官们更加放心地相信 T-Dome 允许自主攻击其认定的敌对目标。
尽管中国在发动袭击之前发起了旨在破坏台湾指挥和控制系统的强大网络攻势，但台湾慷慨地使用了 Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 等前沿人工智能 (AI) 网络安全模型，发现并修补了几乎所有潜在的攻击向量，从而保持了 T-Dome 和其他系统的运行。对人工智能抱有如此大的信心的争议是不可避免的。战时的防御效果则不然。
T-Dome 证明了这些高风险决策的正确性，在第一轮拦截中拦截了 90% 的中国弹药。这为台湾指挥官赢得了宝贵的时间来分散兵力，使中国更难瞄准他们，采取预先计划

【原文 English Original】
Dispatch from 2032: After Chinese salvos fail to defeat Taiwan, Beijing is trapped in a war of attrition - Atlantic Council
Warships and fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy take part in a military display in the South China Sea on April 12, 2018. (REUTERS/Stringer via Reuters Connect)
This article is part of “Dispatches from the Next War,” a series from the Scowcroft Center’s Indo-Pacific Security Initiative in which our experts provide hypothetical accounts of what the world’s next major conflict could look like in the region where it’s most likely to break out: the Indo-Pacific. These dispatches are styled as fictional intelligence, or “FicInt,” which is used within the military to prepare policymakers for possible futures. The aim is to prevent the next war from ever unfolding.
TAIPEI, 2032—China’s first missiles and drones flew across the Taiwan Strait in the dead of night. Some coursed across the black sky propelled by growling jets of flame, while others quietly and near-invisibly hummed through the dark sky at a steady pace. The first were destroyed by interceptor missiles snaking into Chinese columns of fire, others exploded when hit by flashes of laser light. Some were knocked aside by tiny interceptor drones. A few were downed by curtains of autocannon and machine-gun fire, with the growing streaks of tracer bullets groping for targets in the dark.
These joint firepower strikes—the vaunted first attack of China’s war on Taiwan—were meant to smash Taiwan’s defenses, incapacitate its military force, and shatter the Taiwanese will to fight. While these salvoes were terrifying and impressive, they failed to achieve China’s objectives.
Some of the attacks got through, crashing into ports, airfields, and military bases, and sending plumes of flame and smoke into the sky. From Taipei in the north to Kaohsiung in the south, Taiwan was mercilessly hit again and again. While sources of Taiwanese military power were China’s target, many civilians were also slaughtered by the attack. World leaders initially waited to see whether Taiwan could withstand the onslaught or whether it would quickly fold as many analysts had predicted.
But the T-Dome, Taiwan’s multi-layered air- and missile-defense system, proved unexpectedly effective. While it faced performance difficulties when it first became operational in 2027, two years after its announcement in 2025, the reliability of many of its autonomous systems matured rapidly. As China’s incursions into Taiwan’s airspace and aggressive maritime harassment grew more frequent and hostile year after year, Taiwan’s presidents and commanders became more comfortable putting greater faith in the T-Dome’s permission to autonomously engage targets it identified as hostile.
And while China’s strikes were preceded by a robust cyber offensive aimed at disrupting Taiwan’s command-and-control systems, Taiwan’s generous use of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) cybersecurity models like Anthropic’s Claude Mythos had discovered and patched nearly every potential attack vector, keeping the T-Dome and other systems operational. The controversy about placing so much faith in AI was inevitable; the defensive results in wartime were not.
The T-Dome vindicated those high-risk decisions, intercepting 90 percent of Chinese munitions in the first barrage. This bought Taiwan’s commanders precious time to disperse their forces and make it more difficult for China to target them, take up preplanned fighting positions across their nation, and start fighting back.
Further, the survivability and resilience of many Taiwanese bases, stations, and command posts proved to be highly robust. Many were built underground and were well-protected by dozens of meters of earth and rock. Missile after missile and drone after drone slammed into the vicinity of these underground command posts. While some were disrupted, as antennas were toppled and wiring cut, most remained operational.
Notably, Taiwan’s air force was able to maintain aviation command and control from its underground airbase within Toad Mountain, contributing both to air defense and strike missions of its own. Above-ground targets in Taiwan, such as airfields and main supply routes, were initially cratered and some aircraft were destroyed. But Taiwanese engineers repaired airfields, roads, and bases with alacrity. As a result, such hits resulted only in temporary pauses in Taiwan’s operations and did not amount to debilitating knock-out blows.
With most of its forces intact, Taiwan counter-attacked, firing its own munitions at key targets across mainland China. Many of these were intercepted. But due to the superior quality and reliability of Taiwan’s munitions, and China’s years-long strategic emphasis on offensive rather than defensive capabilities, a disproportionate number of Taiwanese munitions hit their marks.
In addition, the United States, Japan, and other nations provided Taiwan with exquisite intelligence and provided non-attributable, non-kinetic cyber and space capabilities that greatly enhanced the hit-rate of Taiwan’s defensive counterstrikes. Consequently, Taiwan devastated targets such as the ports where China’s amphibious forces were assembling, crippling the invasion before it even got underway. Chinese aviation command-and-control nodes and over-the-horizon radars were also hammered, giving Taiwan’s air force greater freedom of maneuver than most analysts had ever predicted.
The effects on Taiwanese morale were immeasurable. As with the US military’s famous Doolittle Raid on Japan after Pearl Harbor, the physical damage Taiwan inflicted on China was less important than the political and psychological results of Taiwan’s demonstrated resilience. Taiwan was not helpless, and the People’s Republic of China was not an invincible juggernaut.
With the quick, decisive campaign China had envisioned to isolate and invade Taiwan thwarted, the joint firepower strikes pressed on. Days dragged into weeks. Taiwan began running dry on interceptors, cannons began to jam, and even lasers began to burn out. Taiwan was forced to absorb more direct hits from Chinese strikes, even as China’s own magazines ran low.
If the war were evaluated today based on targets hit, the assessment would find that China has a commanding lead. But even with Taiwan’s dwindling munitions, the forces still in the fight have proven disproportionately effective. As the United States painfully experienced during Operation Epic Fury in Iran, even a greatly diminished adversary can still hold the advantage if it fights asymmetrically and selectively. While short on missiles, Taiwan has maintained plenty of launchers and conducted carefully sequenced strikes layered with joint operations and allied intelligence support that continue to bloody China’s nose. China’s Eastern Theater Command has still refused to launch an invasion fleet across the strait, as the mere preservation of Taiwan’s stand-in forces held the amphibious force at risk, making the amphibious invasion appear infeasible.
China—and the world—also grossly underestimated Taiwanese resolve. Despite polling that showed Taiwanese willingness to fight as even higher than that of Ukrainians prior to the Russian invasion in 2022, many analysts were skeptical that Taiwan would hold fast under the pressure of a Chinese offensive. Such analysts had focused primarily on the correlation of forces and means between China and Taiwan, weighing their assessments on numeric comparisons of ships, jets, and missiles available to both sides. This, however, failed to account for qualitative differences in Chinese and Taiwanese systems and societies, or for fundamental human elements that have always characterized the conduct of war. While bombing alone was not China’s plan, China had been as yet unable to launch its amphibious invasion because it could not set the necessary conditions. Bombing alone has never produced capitulation, and it has not here in Taipei.
Moreover, China’s narrative warfare and United Front activities, its strategic co-opting of domestic groups, had also penetrated swaths of Taiwanese society and foreign discourse, influencing pre-war public commentary to give a dim view of Taiwanese will and an overinflated view of Chinese prowess. The extreme pro-unification wing of the Kuomintang, the Chinese Nationalist Party in Taiwan, aligned itself with Beijing before the war. A few American commentators had advocated strategic restraint, isolationism, and nativism, while some American politicians echoed these sentiments, leading many to presume Taiwan would surrender at the first blush with its enemy.
But as with the staunch resolve of Ukrainians, it appears the Taiwanese are prepared to fight for years if necessary to preserve the democracy and way of life they built after ending martial law in 1987. Under attack, as they have seen their people killed in the streets, the Taiwanese have bravely rallied, pro-unification extremists have been politically isolated, and public sentiment in favor of taidu, formal Taiwanese independence, has skyrocketed. Civil-defense initiatives and energy-diversification efforts, which had been maturing for years, have also mentally prepared the population and the entire society to be resilient despite the immediate imposition of incredible hardship across the country.
Beijing now faces a dilemma. Backing down could deal a fatal blow to the credibility of the Chinese Communist Party, while pressing on would mean doubling down on sunk costs and putting the government’s dream of national rejuvenation further out of reach. Caught in a trap of its own making, China has looked abroad to Russia and North Korea for other solutions, while the Central Military Commission has begun to consider limited nuclear strikes to turn the tide in China’s favor.
Magazine depth cuts both ways. Taiwan may run low on munitions first in a future conflict, but even Chinese inventories are not limitless. And because China cannot hit everything at once, it will likely have to focus on high-priority targets, yielding maneuver space for Taiwanese forces.
Range rings also cut both ways. Taiwan falls within the range of most Chinese strike capabilities. China, too, is within range of many of Taiwan’s strike capabilities. If Taiwan is attacked by China, Taiwan will strike back at targets in China—not just at munitions or forces entering Taiwanese territory.
The earth is the most reliable and affordable shield. Interceptors are necessary, but they can be expensive and can quickly run dry under constant barrage. While difficult to scale, subterranean fortifications reduce reliance on interceptors and mitigate China’s ability to effectively target Taiwan’s forces.
Regardless of when, why, and how China may start the fight, the result would likely be a protracted war with Taiwan. Beijing may intend—and pundits may predict—a quick surrender by Taipei, but this is unlikely. There are many “roads to war” and rationales Beijing will claim led to its aggression, and many ways the war might begin, including a quarantine, a blockade, or outright attack. Regardless, China is unlikely to win rapidly or easily, almost inevitably leading to a protracted and costly conflict—if Taiwan continues its defense and resilience efforts.
Even successful strikes rarely deliver knockout blows, and an active defense can prove resilient even under sustained strike campaigns. Defenders will disperse to preserve forces and capabilities, and can rapidly repair airfields, ports, and bases.
When nations are attacked, cohesion surges, even among politically divided states. Blood calls for blood, defenders rally to their flag, and the will to fight becomes stronger than ever.
Third parties are not easily intimidated into total non-participation in wars that impact them. When nations can pursue their interests and frustrate their adversaries at low risk, they will.

俄罗斯战机曾多次进入韩国防空识别区，但首尔针对此类飞行发出警告的情况却很少。 |彭博社
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
在多架俄罗斯战机进入韩国空中识别区后，韩国紧急出动战斗机，并短暂命令东海岸一座岛屿上的居民到地下寻求庇护，这是该地区一系列类似事件中的最新一起。
根据当地灾难门户网站上发布的警报信息，周二的空袭警报适用于居住在朝鲜半岛以东约 130 公里处的郁陵岛的约 9,000 人，该警报最初发布几分钟后就被解除。
韩国参谋长联席会议在一份声明中表示，俄罗斯战机进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）并飞近郁陵岛，促使韩国军方部署战斗机。
“飞机在我们采取军事措施后离开。没有侵犯韩国领空，”他们补充道。韩国防空识别区不是韩国的领空，而是飞机在接近时应表明身份的区域。
“俄罗斯军用飞机已经逼近郁陵岛，即将进入我们的领空。众所周知，鉴于军用飞机的高速飞行，我们预计可能会侵犯领空，并先发制人地发出警报，以保护我们的人民并确保他们的安全，”联合参谋长联席会议发言人张道永（Jang Do-young）在新闻发布会上说。
军方拒绝详细说明飞机飞离空域的距离有多近。
张说，俄罗斯战机曾多次进入韩国防空识别区，但韩国当局很少对此类飞行发出警告。
韩国国防部表示，计划召见俄罗斯武官以抗议这些航班。
这些航班是在俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京上周在亚太经济合作组织峰会期间与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平在深圳举行三边会议之后进行的。
上周，在会议召开之前，韩国、日本和台湾都抱怨俄罗斯飞机侵犯了它们的领空或防空区。
虽然最初的警报警告了俄罗斯飞机，敦促居民“疏散到地下设施或建筑物”，但后来的警报之一提到了朝鲜飞机，引发了混乱。当局后来澄清说，该消息是错误发布的。

South Korea scrambles jets as Russian warplanes enter air zone - The Japan Times
South Korea scrambles jets as Russian warplanes enter air zone
There have been multiple instances of Russian warplanes entering South Korea's air defense identification zone, but warnings by Seoul in response to such flights are rare. | BLOOMBERG
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly ordered residents of an island off its east coast to seek shelter underground after multiple Russian warplanes entered the country’s air identification zone, the latest in a string of similar incidents regionally.
An air raid warning Tuesday, which applied to the estimated 9,000 people who live on Ulleung Island, some 130 kilometers east of the Korean Peninsula, was lifted minutes after it was initially issued, according to alert messages posted on a local disaster portal.
The Russian jets entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone — or KADIZ — and flew near Ulleung Island, prompting the South Korean military to deploy its fighter jets, South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a statement.
“The aircraft left following our military measures. There was no violation of South Korean airspace,” they added. The KADIZ is not South Korea’s territorial airspace but is an area where aircraft are supposed to identify themselves as they approach.
“The Russian military aircraft had approached the Ulleung Island to the point where it was just short of entering our airspace. Given the high speed at which military aircraft travel, as you are all aware, we anticipated a potential airspace violation and issued the alert preemptively to protect our people and ensure their safety,” JCS spokesperson, Jang Do-young, told a briefing.
The military declined to elaborate on how close to the airspace the jets flew.
There have been multiple instances of Russian warplanes entering the KADIZ, but it is rare for South Korean authorities to issue a warning in response to such flights, Jang said.
South Korea plans to summon Russia’s military attache to protest the flights, the Defense Ministry said.
The flights come after Russian President Vladimir Putin held a trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping in Shenzhen last week, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
Last week, ahead of the meeting, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan all complained of Russian jets violating their airspace or air defense zones.
While the initial alert warned of Russian aircraft, urging residents to “evacuate to underground facilities or buildings,” one of the later alerts mentioned North Korean aircraft, stoking confusion. Authorities later clarified that the message had been issued by mistake.

随着国内股市飙升，日本债券跨曲线上涨 - 《日本时报》
随着国内股市飙升，日本债券跨曲线上涨
东京证券交易所的显示器显示，东京中央区的日经股票平均价格周二上午大幅上涨。 |集集
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
日本政府债券在三天假期后全线上涨，尽管国内股市因人工智能投资前景的担忧缓解而飙升，但涨幅仍保持不变。
基准 10 年期国债收益率领跌，下跌 7 个基点至 2.715%。五年期债务下降 5.5 个基点至 2.125%。
在黄仁勋重新领导英伟达缓解了人们对人工智能投资放缓的担忧后，225 期日经指数股价上涨了 5%。债券和股票的上涨表明，即使风险偏好有所恢复，日本国债仍保持坚挺。
新加坡 Lombard Odier 高级宏观策略师 Homin Lee 表示：“能源市场混乱的平静前景以及美联储 2027 年的政策路径可能是日本政府债券上午上涨的原因。”
法国巴黎银行资产管理公司高级债券策略师Ryutaro Kimura表示，虽然日本国债的空头回补似乎正在推低长期收益率，但人工智能相关股票的强劲反弹可能会缓解金融市场的避险情绪，从而使日本央行12月加息的可能性重新发挥作用。
木村补充道，尽管如此，国内主要机构投资者在评估英伟达的消息对人工智能相关的全球经济前景意味着什么时，似乎仍保持观望。
在今年早些时候收益率攀升至数十年高点后，随着投资者重新评估通胀前景、日本央行政策和政府债务需求，本月日本收益率大幅波动。投资者将关注周三举行的 40 年期政府债券拍卖，以更清楚地了解债券需求。

Japanese bonds rally across curve as domestic stocks surge - The Japan Times
Japanese bonds rally across curve as domestic stocks surge
A monitor at the Tokyo Stock Exchange displays the Nikkei Stock Average after a sharp rise on Tuesday morning in Tokyo's Chuo Ward. | JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Japanese government bonds rallied across the curve after a three-day holiday, with gains holding even as domestic equities surged on easing concerns over the outlook for artificial intelligence investment.
The benchmark 10-year yield led the moves, falling 7 basis points to 2.715%. Five-year debt fell 5.5 basis points to 2.125%.
The 225-issue Nikkei stock average rose as much as 5% after Jensen Huang’s return to lead Nvidia eased concerns about a slowdown in AI investment. The gains in bonds and stocks showed JGBs holding firm even as risk appetite recovered.
“The calming outlook on energy market disruptions and the U.S. Fed’s policy path in 2027 are the likely explanation for the positive session in the morning for Japanese government bonds,” said Homin Lee, senior macro strategist at Lombard Odier in Singapore.
While short-covering in JGBs appears to be driving long-end yields lower, a strong rebound in AI-related stocks could ease the risk-off mood in financial markets, bringing the possibility of a December rate hike by the Bank of Japan back into play, said Ryutaro Kimura, senior bond strategist at BNP Paribas Asset Management.
Still, major domestic institutional investors appear to be staying on the sidelines as they assess what the Nvidia news means for the global economic outlook in relation to AI, Kimura added.
Japanese yields have swung sharply this month as investors reassess the outlook for inflation, BOJ policy and demand for government debt, after yields climbed to multi-decade highs earlier this year. Investors will be looking to an auction of 40-year government debt on Wednesday for more clarity on bond demand.

邱垂正24日出席台北海洋大學舉辦的「印太戰略 vs. 全球南方：美中競合關係對台灣影響」研討會，他以「兩岸關係的現在與未來」為題發表演講。中央社記者廖文綺攝 115年11月24日
（中央社記者廖文綺台北24日電）陸委會主委邱垂正今天表示，中共自2022年以來不斷對台加強軍機艦擾台、外交打壓、跨境鎮壓與法律戰等複合性施壓，預計習近平第四任期將對台灣採取更具有侵略性的「未統先治」做法，可能更直接地改變現狀，未來兩岸管轄權之爭會越來越嚴重。
邱垂正今天出席台北海洋大學舉辦的「印太戰略 vs. 全球南方：美中競合關係對台灣影響」研討會，他以「兩岸關係的現在與未來」為題發表演講。
談到中國政治，邱垂正表示，習近平執政近15年以來，中共從集體領導轉向權力集中，再到定於一尊，並持續強化民族主義，夯實執政基礎。習近平以實現中華民族偉大復興作為執政正當性來源，完成統一台灣是其重要歷史任務，將對兩岸關係帶來更多風險。
經濟方面，邱垂正指出，目前中國經濟與其說是K型經濟，不如說更像「i型經濟」。他說，i的上面那一點就是「新質生產力」，包括新能源、人工智慧（AI）及機器人等產業，雖然維持雙位數成長，但僅占中國大陸GDP約9%，就業占比更只有1.3%，與整體經濟主體出現斷裂。
他續指，i底部的線則是主體經濟，如傳統產業、房地產、一般服務業、中小企業等，占就業及稅收約8至9成，但目前房地產低迷、內需與消費不振，民間投資也呈現衰退，「那一點是無法拉動主體經濟的」。不過台灣近年對中國大陸投資及出口比重下降，反映台商已調整全球布局，台灣也降低對中經濟依賴。
邱垂正也分析中國對台政策，中共自2022年起對台採取包括軍機艦擾台、外交打壓、社會滲透、經濟脅迫、跨境鎮壓與法律戰在內的複合性施壓，未來還可能進一步擴大。
邱垂正透露，曾有一位擔任過行政院院長的人，為了推動兩岸企業家峰會，向中共當局請示有沒有可能暫停軍機擾台，對方回覆「這是國策，沒辦法改變」。
邱垂正指出，未來兩岸管轄權之爭會越來越嚴重，從2020年開始，中共否認海峽中線；2022年軍機、艦艇、飛彈等越過海峽中線成為新常態；2024年否認離島禁限制水域；再到今年，中共聲稱對台海東部海域擁有主權與管轄權，對台行動可說是步步緊逼、改變現狀。
他研判，到習近平第四任期，將對台灣採取更具有侵略性、更有挑釁性的「未統先治」做法，過去中共透過複合性施壓間接改變現狀，但未來可能直接地改變現狀，包括內國化、行政與司法管轄權，以及對外交的打壓可能會更嚴峻。此外也會透過國民待遇、同城化來促統促融。
邱垂正強調，和平是要建立在實力之上，台灣具有三項無可取代的戰略重要性，包括第一島鏈戰略位置、已走出非紅格局的高科技供應鏈，以及自由民主的生活方式。他表示，政府將持續落實賴總統的和平四大支柱行動方案，強化自我防衛力量與全社會防衛韌性，並與各國共同維護台海和平穩定。（編輯：陳鎧妤）1151124

九合一大選倒數，台北市長蔣萬安（前左）24日起與國民黨各選區議員候選人啟動車掃，上午從松山、信義區出發拜票。中央社記者葉蓁芸攝 115年11月24日
（中央社記者葉蓁芸台北24日電）九合一大選倒數，尋求連任的台北市長蔣萬安今天起與國民黨各選區議員候選人展開車掃拜票，3天將跑遍6選區。針對近期車掃發生車禍等狀況，蔣萬安提醒民眾注意行車安全，也會請團隊留意。
選戰倒數4天，蔣萬安續拚陸戰，今天上午與國民黨議員候選人從松山、信義區開始車掃拜票，下午則將至中山、大同區，一連3天行經北市各選區，在最後階段全力催票。
蔣萬安上午在松信後援會前接受媒體聯訪，被問及近期車掃發生車禍、控燈等狀況，他表示，再次提醒所有支持者，打招呼時注意騎車、行車安全，他也會提醒團隊留意。
媒體詢問，先前曾傳出會從艱困選區開始車掃，第一站選擇松山、信義區是否因選情危急，且昨天與民眾黨議員個別車掃，恐引發藍營小雞不滿。蔣萬安說，車掃很早就規劃好，沒有特別考量，先前他也一一出席藍營候選人總部成立、掃街或站路口等活動。
九合一大選倒數，台北市長蔣萬安24日起與國民黨議員候選人啟動車掃，台北市議長戴錫欽（左2）、國民黨北市議員秦慧珠（右2）、詹為元（右1）、議員候選人李明璇（左3）及許原榮（左1）一同拜票。中央社記者葉蓁芸攝 115年11月24日
針對民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋將在市議會前舉辦選前之夜，且預告會安排許多驚喜，蔣萬安表示，尊重各陣營在選舉最後階段的規劃、安排；至於自己的選前之夜，他說，「讓我保密一下」。
媒體關切，蔣萬安、沈伯洋昨晚都開啟網路直播與支持者互動，空戰如何勝過沈伯洋。蔣萬安說，最後階段一切還是以走入基層、與市民面對面接觸為主，若接下來還有時間，就會規劃安排。
另外，蔣萬安21日在政見發表會提到將推動青年儲蓄支持，不過媒體報導指北市青年局未編列相關預算。蔣萬安指出，市府一直都在討論、研究與評估，這不只與單一局處相關，還需考量金融機構如何執行、市府整體預算等，一定會全力落實政見。
媒體問及，輝達董事會決定恢復黃仁勳的執行長職務。蔣萬安對此表示，北市府與輝達之間的合作不受影響，也都有高度默契。
國民黨北市議員秦慧珠近期發言疑讓藍營支持者不滿，也遭黃復興系統解除常委職務，外界關注蔣萬安與秦慧珠互動。
蔣萬安今天受訪後與秦慧珠握手，面對記者詢問是否支持蔣萬安，秦慧珠說：「我從頭到尾都支持蔣萬安。」2人隨後與台北市議長戴錫欽、國民黨北市議員詹為元、議員候選人李明璇及許原榮齊喊「蔣萬安凍蒜」、「議員全壘打」。（編輯：蕭博文）1151124

content:
2026年11月23日，中華民國陸委會副主委沈有忠（右）出席兩岸政策協會在台大校友會館舉辦的「APEC峰會後的美中競合：經貿博弈、台海情勢與戰略抉擇」座談會。（宋碧龍／大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月24日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）中華民國陸委會副主委沈有忠23日表示，中共利用亞太經濟合作會議（APEC）峰會及場邊會議，企圖營造「大國形象」，但成果乏善可陳，且言行不一。他研判中方後續對台政策將持續強化施壓、社會分化與強制促統作為。
陸委會副主委沈有忠23日出席「APEC峰會後的美中競合：經貿博弈、台海情勢與戰略抉擇」座談會。沈有忠強調，中華民國是主權完整的國家，與中華人民共和國（共產中國）互不隸屬，無論北京如何操作，都不會改變此一客觀事實。
「台灣將與美國等民主友盟保持密切聯繫、完整掌握狀況，確保我國家主權與自由民主的生活方式，並維持台海和平穩定的現狀。」他說。
沈有忠指出，美中戰略競爭始終是今年歷次「川習會」最重要的背景與結構性因素，本次APEC「川習會」旨在透過溝通對話，管控分歧、避免誤判造成的風險，但美中戰略競爭是在科技、經貿、地緣政治等不同層面的全局性競爭，不會因一兩次的會面有所改變。
此外，沈有忠說，今年6月的G7領袖峰會、11月的G7外長與歐盟代表會議、以及川普（特朗普）在參加APEC前，先赴菲律賓參加Quad峰會與東協-美國特別峰會，美方皆重申維持台灣海峽和平與穩定至關重要、反對任何以武力改變現狀的企圖。顯見台海和平穩定的現狀依然是包括台灣與美國在內、全球民主國家的共同利益。
沈有忠表示，中方利用舉辦APEC的機會，在場邊舉行美中俄三方峰會，利用主場優勢刻意凸顯中方精心設計的「大國形象」。而中方將三方峰會定位為「中俄美元首會晤」，並於會後發表「中俄美元首和平宣言」，企圖營造中共致力和平與穩定的形象。但事實上，中共在APEC正式舉辦前，不惜與俄羅斯加強在第一島鏈地區對日本、台灣和菲律賓的施壓。
沈有忠指出，「中共在APEC會議前出動大批軍機艦，而俄國軍機也於會前、會後持續侵擾日本領空及我國防空識別區，頗有中、俄聯合對外展現軍事協作、威嚇區域國家意味，與APEC的精神明顯衝突。」
「台灣與國際社會都會保持高度警惕，並致力於更多共同合作，確保區域的安全穩定與繁榮。此外，中方在APEC峰會的安排接待上，如針對日本首相高市早苗給予差別待遇，顯現其背後政治意涵凌駕於作為一個大國與東道主該有的氣度。」沈有忠說。
沈有忠強調，中共為在明年「二十一大」鞏固習近平持續掌權的正當性，勢將強化對台施壓與促統作為。當前刻意介入我即將舉行的地方選舉更是眾所周知、證據確鑿，研判中共將持續對台灣社會進行分化、破壞社會對選舉的信任，影響台灣選舉與民主的發展。
他說，無論中方如何刻意操作宣傳，都無法否認中華民國與中華人民共和國互不隸屬，中華人民共和國沒有一天治理過台灣的客觀事實。台灣的主流民意支持兩岸維持現狀，反對「一國兩制」及中共片面設定「一中原則」的「九二共識」作為對話的前提。
沈有忠重申，不願意與台灣民選政府對等對話的始終是中共，不願正視中華民國始終存在的也是中共，蓄意消滅中華民國國家主權、破壞台灣民主治理的仍然是中共。面對中共步步進逼的侵略，政府將堅守捍衛國家主權與自由民主的原則，不卑不亢、維持現狀。
最後，沈有忠說，政府也始終願意與北京當局在對等尊嚴、不預設前提下進行對話、化解分歧。未來，台灣將持續強化自我防衛力量，強化經濟與社會韌性，並與美國及國際民主友盟深化合作，共同守護台海與印太區域的和平穩定與繁榮。

title: The Jet That Always Shadows Air Force One When The President Travels Abroad
zh_title: 当总统出国旅行时，这架喷气式飞机总是尾随空军一号

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普最近对中国的访问引起了在线航班追踪器的特别关注。这在很大程度上是因为美国空军目前所有三架基于波音 747 的空军一号飞机——两架较旧的 VC-25A 和新的前卡塔尔 VC-25B“桥”喷气式飞机——都支持了这次旅行。另一架军用 747 飞机，即 E-4B 守夜人飞机，通常被称为“世界末日飞机”，也被发现跟踪该组织往返于亚洲。虽然这在网上引起了很多关注，包括来自国防网站的博客文章，但事实是这绝对是标准做法。 E-4B 只是总统离开该国时上演的大型空中物流芭蕾舞剧的另一部分，尽管是一个非常独特和害羞的部分。空军目前拥有四架 E-4B，也称为国家机载作战中心 (NAOC)，全部驻扎在内布拉斯加州的奥法特空军基地。其中三架飞机以 747-200 型号为基础，于 20 世纪 70 年代首次作为 E-4A 高级机载指挥所 (AACP) 投入使用。这些飞机随后在 20 世纪 80 年代达到了 E-4B NAOC 标准，并最终加入了直接改装为该配置的第四架飞机。多年来，这些喷气式飞机不断升级。
除了支持总统旅行外，守夜人飞机还定期在海外旅行期间运送国防部长（现在也称为战争部长）及其工作人员等。E-4B 守夜人喷气式飞机的库存图片。美国军方 11 月 16 日，搭载特朗普及其随行人员的 VC-25 飞机离开华盛顿特区郊外的安德鲁斯空军基地。大约在同一时间，一架 E-4B 被追踪到从奥法特起飞。特朗普首先对菲律宾进行了短暂访问，然后前往中国。飞机观察员有一个难得的机会看到所有三架 VC-25 停在马尼拉尼诺·阿基诺国际机场。美国空军：美国总统随行人员正在经安克雷奇飞往马尼拉的途中。 VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — 约翰尼·双子座(@Borrowed7Time) 2026 年 11 月 16 日 守夜人喷气式飞机分别飞往日本冲绳岛的嘉手纳空军基地。 E-4B NAOC 73-1676 在总统马尼拉之行期间停泊在嘉手纳。信用 RODN Kadena。 pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) 2026 年 11 月 17 日 今天早些时候，所有三架 VC-25 载着​​特朗普和美国代表团其他成员离开中国。当三人开始飞越日本本土时，E-4B 从嘉手纳起飞跟随他们。
美国总统返回美国 特朗普总统及其随行人员本周在结束各种会议后正在从中国返回美国的途中： VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B “TRUCK55” 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 正如开头提到的，在特朗普访问期间，E-4B 跟踪 VC-25 并在嘉手纳进行前沿部署先去菲律宾，然后去中国，这并不奇怪。这是美国总统出国旅行的标准操作程序。在特朗普五月份访华期间，飞行追踪器特别发现了类似的飞机队列。 HANK99 又名“末日飞机”(E-4B NAOC) 从内布拉斯加州奥法特空军基地飞往美国

【原文 English Original】
U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent visit to China has drawn particular attention from online flight trackers. This is in no small part due to the fact that all three of the U.S. Air Force’s current Boeing 747-based Air Force One aircraft – the two older VC-25As and the new ex-Qatari VC-25B “Bridge” jet – have supported the trip. Another militarized 747, an E-4B Nightwatch , commonly referred to as a ‘doomsday plane,’ was also spotted shadowing the group to and from Asia. While this drew a lot of attention online, including blog posts from defense-focused sites, the reality is this is absolutely standard practice. The E-4B is just another part, albeit a very unique and shy one, of the massive aerial logistics ballet that occurs whenever the President leaves the country. The Air Force currently has four E-4Bs, also known as National Airborne Operations Centers (NAOC), all based at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Based on the 747-200 model, three of these planes first entered service in the 1970s as E-4A Advanced Airborne Command Posts (AACP). Those aircraft were subsequently brought up to the E-4B NAOC standard in the 1980s, and were eventually joined by a fourth example converted straight to that configuration. The jets have been continuously upgraded over the years. In addition to supporting presidential travel, the Nightwatch aircraft also regularly transport the Secretary of Defense (now also referred to as the Secretary of War) and their staff during overseas trips, among other roles. A stock picture of an E-4B Nightwatch jet. US Military The VC-25s carrying Trump and the rest of his entourage left Andrews Air Force Base just outside Washington, D.C., on November 16. An E-4B was tracked heading out from Offutt at around the same time. Trump headed first for a brief visit to the Philippines before traveling on to China. Plane spotters had a rare opportunity to see all three VC-25s parked together at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila. USAF: POTUS entourage en route to Manila via Anchorage. VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — Johnny Gemini (@Borrowed7Time) November 16, 2026 The Nightwatch jet headed separately to Kadena Air Base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. E-4B NAOC 73-1676 bedding down at Kadena during the presidential trip to Manilla. credit RODN Kadena. pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) November 17, 2026 All three VC-25s left China carrying Trump and the rest of the U.S. delegation earlier today. As the trio began to pass over Japan’s home islands, the E-4B took off from Kadena to follow them. POTUS Returning to the US President Trump and his entourage are en-route back to the US from China after various meetings this week: VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B "TRUCK55" 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) November 19, 2026 As mentioned at the start, the E-4B shadowing the VC-25s and being forward-deployed in Kadena during Trump’s visit to the Philippines and then China is no surprise. This is standard operating procedure for when the President of the United States travels abroad. Flight trackers notably caught a similar procession of aircraft during Trump’s trip to China back in May. HANK99 aka “The Doomsday Plane” (E-4B NAOC) is airborne from Offutt AFB, Nebraska to shadow POTUS on his trip to China. https://t.co/BBsq1tkC1E pic.twitter.com/Z3zpxBX9zy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) May 12, 2026 While the E-4Bs are nowhere near as luxurious as the VC-25As or the new VC-25B, they are just as capable of serving as airborne command posts, if not more so in many respects . They are unofficially referred to as ‘doomsday planes’ because they are specifically configured to provide the president and other senior military officials with a flying headquarters they can use for any and all duties, including directing nuclear strikes during the most serious crises. They are hardened against electromagnetic pulses caused by nuclear detonations and have the ability to stay airborne for days. Their very existence, at least one being on alert at all times to support the National Command Authority , is a critical component that underpins America’s nuclear deterrent. Even if an adversary destroys much of the country, an E-4 can remain airborne to order the counter-attack. With all this in mind, the E-4B fleet is key to so-called continuity of government plans , which are in place to make sure key elements of the federal government remain functional following an attack or a similarly serious contingency. As a prime example, President George W. Bush rode on one of the VC-25A Air Force One aircraft in the immediate wake of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but there were discussions about transferring him to a Nightwatch jet . Bush ultimately decided against making the change, but an E-4B was still scrambled and orbited over Washington, D.C., for a time. This is hardly the only time a president has made use of an E-4B, or one of its predecessors, as well as command ships, as TWZ has examined in the past . September 11th, 2001 – Boeing E-4B NAOC callsign ADDIS77 scrambled from Andrews AFB. While ATC was calling them “VENUS” which is a typical callsign used at Andrews, you can hear the urgency of the pilot wanting to get airborne. The E-4 orbited over Washington DC for a while… pic.twitter.com/K61yeFY3kZ — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 The aircraft got airborne assuming for safety reasons (safer in air than on the ground) and if needed would have flown to pickup the President or next in the line of succession (Continuity of government). — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 Within this broader context, E-4Bs have been a key feature of overseas presidential travel for decades now, although they are the least visible of the presidential aerial armada. This massive airlift and logistics effort includes bringing in multiple examples of the presidential motorcade , Marine One helicopters , and various force protection assets . This involves many sorties by C-17 and C-5 cargo aircraft that cover many thousands of miles each. The videos below from Trump’s visit this week to the Philippines give a sense of just one portion of these options, albeit the most visible one, the vertical airlift component. US President Trump landing at Luneta. Impressive to see the extent of securing the safety of the most important human being on the planet. pic.twitter.com/gIXewN6Yz3 — Emil (@13thFool) November 18, 2026 Beyond its strategic command and control mission, having an E-4B positioned in the region the president is visiting during overseas trips offers a critical option for refuge and escape, as well as an additional backup aircraft to Air Force One, should any emergencies arise. The exact parameters for where the Nightwatch aircraft go are unknown, but would be based on what suitable airports are available and what potential threats and contingencies could arise. They are never seen at the same locations as Air Force One and are always separated by a distance of dozens of miles, at least, in friendly countries — close enough to be accessed by Marine One in an emergency — or generally in a region for more sensitive locales where such close proximity basing isn’t an option. It moves in shadow of AF1 everywhere it goes overseas, usually lands at another airport nearby. This is standard procedure going back decades. We see it every single overseas trip. Beyond it's strategic and COG function it acts as a refuge/escape if something really bad happens… https://t.co/nPhxPJOKMk — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) November 19, 2026 E-4Bs do not need to be airborne to act as command and control platforms and secure communications relay nodes, either. This further feeds into their continuity of government role. These are capabilities that can also be made available, if required, to assist the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) during major natural disasters or to help serve as command posts and communications nodes in other emergencies. The changing character of the Air Force One fleet could put new emphasis on the E-4Bs, as well as the replacement E-4C Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC) jets the Air Force is now in the process of acquiring. Trump’s trip back from China has notably underscored a significant difference between the VC-25As and the new VC-25B Bridge aircraft, which is that the latter lacks aerial refueling capability. Two fully-outfitted VC-25Bs that Boeing is still in the process of converting for the Air Force will also not be capable of refueling in flight. The E-4Bs can refuel in flight, and the E-4Cs will be able to do so, as well. Coming back from China heading to DC, the new VC-25B Bridge Air Force One does not need to refuel in Alaska but the old VC-25As do. Tracking via @ADSBex pic.twitter.com/zhcdCaIRyy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) November 19, 2026 TWZ has previously explored the Air Force’s decision to axe the aerial refueling requirement for the VC-25B in detail. The ostensible logic is that the VC-25Bs are based on newer 747-8i aircraft with more capable and fuel-efficient engines than the aging 747-200-based VC-25As. The new aircraft are, as a result, capable of longer unrefueled flights, though maximum range requirements were also watered down . At the same time, in-flight refueling allows the VC-25As ( as well as the E-4Bs ) to remain aloft for days at a time. This, in turn, could be critical in a major crisis where access to secure airfields might be limited, if not completely unavailable, for a prolonged period of time. An E-4B links up with a KC-135 aerial refueling tanker. USAF The  VC-25B Bridge jet has prompted a whole new array of operational security questions, which TWZ was calling attention to even before the decision was formally made to outfit it for presidential use. The circumstances of Trump’s return from the NATO summit in Turkey in July had prompted a further flurry of reports about whether the modified, Qatari-gifted jet lacked sufficient defensive features and other capabilities in line with the existing VC-25As. The President had flown to Turkey on the Bridge jet, but was reportedly covertly moved between other aircraft on the way back. This was said to have been done as a security precaution amid then-escalating fighting with Iran . A stock picture of the VC-25B Bridge aircraft seen at the time of its official unveiling. USAF President Trump subsequently downplayed the series of events, but said that the Bridge aircraft would be sent to have its capabilities “maxed out.” The White House confirmed that the jet would receive “additional upgrades and enhancements,” but did not elaborate. It is unclear how the aircraft’s configuration has changed in the ensuing months. It is worth noting here that the upgrades in question would have to be limited to defensive systems. The Bridge aircraft could also have entered service without certain communications and networking capabilities found on the VC-25As. Another way to mitigate any such limitations could be to have a VC-25A or an E-4B operating closely enough to establish a line-of-sight data connection relatively quickly so it can leverage the better-equipped aircraft’s communications systems if needed. As an aside, Trump arrived in China aboard the Bridge aircraft and was seen boarding it to head back to the United States. Reporters onboard had their phones taken away during the return flight for still unexplained security reasons. Fox News has reported that the president is aiming to set a record for the longest continuous flight for an Air Force One aircraft. At the time of writing, its unclear whether the president has touched back down anywhere publicly since leaving Shenzhen. Air Force One is about to take off. Press has had their phones confiscated for security reasons. pic.twitter.com/2UkCDekUma — Andrew Leyden (@PenguinSix) November 19, 2026 NOW: Air Force One is setting a new endurance record on the way home from China. In an exclusive chat with @aishahhasnie , President Trump says his trip back to Washington will be the longest continuous flight in Air Force One history. President Trump says he will discuss the… pic.twitter.com/xn25uSkzYZ — Fox News (@FoxNews) November 19, 2026 Where the E-4B is now is also unclear, but it was last tracked continuing along a path shadowing behind Air Force One, where one would expect to see it. Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

content:
Fundraiser by Aydin Anwar : Uyghur Students in Egypt
Aydin Anwar is organizing this fundraiser.
Help save Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt from deportation to China, where they will face detention, persecution, torture, lengthy prison sentences, and perhaps even death.
Hundreds of Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt with resident permits are currently being rounded up to be deported to China, where they will be subject to persecution, imprisonment, torture, and death sentences. Their crime? Being Uyghur and studying Islam. #SaveUyghurStudents
In its attempt to "crackdown on Islamic extremism", China has significantly tightened its security measures and prohibition of religious practice in East Turkestan (aka Xinjiang, occupied by China). Chinese authorities are now seeking the return of thousands of innocent Uyghur students abroad in "wide sweeps" to extend this crackdown.
It has been reported that all airports in Egypts are preventing Uyghurs from leaving the country. Some Uyghur students have already been deported, and the remaining are either in detention awaiting deportation or in hiding within Egypt’s borders. Several that we know managed to escape to Turkey, but are currently homeless or in extreme financial hardship.
Therefore the funds we collect will go to providing shelter, food and other support to the Uyghurs who have already managed to flee Egypt. It will also go to provide those in hiding with necessities (e.g. food, room, board) while we work with nonprofit human rights organizations to pressure Egypt and China to stop the deportations and detentions.
The funds will be collected through Uyghur Youth Campaign, a 501(c) nonprofit based in the US, and will (for now) be directly delivered to the Uyghur students who fled to Turkey by one of its members, Aydin Anwar, who has been in Istanbul. She is connected with these refugees through Munevver Ozuygur, an Uyghur activist based in Zeytinburnu, Istanbul.
Please donate and help spread awareness. Do not remain silent as these young men and women are sent off to be detained, tortured, imprisoned and perhaps even killed in China. They need our help.

content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

title: China’s fourth aircraft carrier, bigger than others and nuclear-powered, nears completion
