summary: 台湾新北市——分析人士称，中国的第四艘航空母舰是一艘迄今为止被称为 004 型的巨型舰艇，最早将于明年面世，其尺寸将比前几艘航母更大，并且配备核动力，在发生任何冲突时可以比平常更快地起飞飞机。这可能会增加日本和美国等已经对中国军队保持高度戒备的国家的压力。智库国防优先事项亚洲项目主任表示，目前正在北方港口城市大连建造的这艘航母部署后可容纳 75 至 90 架飞机。一个
content:
台湾新北市——分析人士称，中国的第四艘航空母舰是一艘迄今为止被称为 004 型的巨型舰艇，最早将于明年面世，其尺寸将比前几艘航母更大，并且配备核动力，在发生任何冲突时可以比平常更快地起飞飞机。这可能会增加日本和美国等已经对中国军队保持高度戒备的国家的压力。智库国防优先事项亚洲项目主任表示，目前正在北方港口城市大连建造的这艘航母部署后可容纳 75 至 90 架飞机。据智库战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 称，截至 10 月，该船的船体从未完工的船头到船尾长约 322 米，宽约 46 米。 CSIS 称 004 型“比中国海军任何其他级别的水面战舰都要大得多”。新加坡南洋理工大学高级研究员科林·许 (Collin Koh) 表示，该航母的航拍照片显示“基本船体形式”已经建成，这预示着 2027 年发射的良好前景。他说，部署需要五到十年的时间。相关军事专家表示，自2025年政治争端以来，中国已在日本附近的海军存在“正常化”，考虑到其规模，包括海岸警卫队船只和海军军舰在内的庞大中国舰队可能已经瞄准了台湾的海上邻国日本。
Koh表示，这些规格将使004型航母比目前中国舰队中最大的一艘——中国的福建号航母“略大”。台北战略与兵棋推演研究委员会主席亚历山大·黄(Alexander Huang)表示，目前获得的有关004型航母的信息——可能会以中国现有的三艘航母等省份的名字重新命名——从电子设备、吨位和飞机运载能力方面将这艘航母归类为“超级航母”。 Koh说，机载核动力将为飞机提供比中国现有的电磁飞机发射系统更多的推进力。他表示，这将消除航母上对发电机的需求，同时允许更快的起飞（不影响有效载荷）和快速的战斗周转以加油。 “这似乎标志着某种战略目标，”高在谈到核能力时说道。 “它不仅仅会沿着你的海岸移动。它似乎标志着某种全球野心。”康奈尔大学专门研究军事历史和国防政策的教授大卫·西尔贝表示，核动力将使航母“基本上具有无限的续航力”，并允许在全球部署，而无需常规动力航母所需的加油机支持。黄说，第四艘航母可能会部署到中国北方，因为其他三艘航母都在南方。
他说，在这种情况下，中国可以“利用这四种方式中的一种来始终在某个地方开展活动”。黄补充道，004型航母可能用于训练、维护以及作战。分析人士表示，中国的第四艘航母使其更接近与美国海军的竞争。西尔贝说，它的尺寸将与美国尼米兹级和福特级航母相当，这意味着它可以搭载多达 100 架飞机。 “这使得它比以前只能运载 50 架左右的航母具有更强的攻击力，”他说。美国海军拥有 11 艘航母，全部为核动力。高说，即使规模小于美国舰队，拥有核动力航母的中国海军也可以对美国构成挑战。美国海军在关岛保留基地

【原文 English Original】
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan — China’s fourth aircraft carrier, a gigantic vessel known so far as just Type 004, will come out as early as next year bigger than its predecessors and with nuclear power that can launch planes faster than usual in case of any conflict, analysts say. And it’s tipped to add pressure on countries, such as Japan and the United States, that already keep a high alert for the Chinese military. The carrier being built now in the northern port city Dalian could accommodate 75 to 90 planes once deployed, the Asia program director at the think tank Defence Priorities has said. As of October, the vessel’s hull measured about 322 meters in length from the unfinished bow to stern with a width of approximately 46 meters, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), also a think tank. CSIS called Type 004 “far larger than any other class of surface combatant” in China’s navy. Aerial photos of the carrier show the “basic hull form” already built, auguring well for a 2027 launch, said Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. Deployment would take five to 10 years, he said. Related China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025 Given its scale, the massive Chinese flotilla that included coast guard vessels alongside navy warships may have had Taiwan’s maritime neighbor Japan in its sights, military experts say. The specs would make Type 004 “slightly larger” than China’s Fujian aircraft carrier, currently the biggest one in its fleet, Koh said. Information available today about the Type 004 – likely to be renamed after a Chinese province like the existing three – classify the vessel as a “supercarrier” in terms of electronics, tonnage and aircraft carrying capacity, said Alexander Huang, chairman of the Council of Strategic and Wargaming Studies in Taipei. Nuclear power on board would offer the aircraft more propulsion than China’s existing electromagnetic aircraft launch system, Koh said. He said that would eliminate the need for power generators on board the carrier while allowing faster takeoffs – without payload compromises – and quick combat turnarounds for refueling. “It seems to signal a certain strategic objective,” Koh said of the nuclear capability. “It’s not just going to move along your coast. It seems to signal a certain global ambition.” Nuclear power will give the carrier “essentially unlimited endurance” and allow for global deployment without the kind of tanker support a conventionally powered carrier needs, said David Silbey, a Cornell University professor specializing in military history and defense policy. The fourth carrier may get posted to northern China because the other three are in the south, Huang said. In that scenario, he said, China could “use one of the four to always operate somewhere.” Type 004 may be used for training and maintenance as well as operations, Huang added. China’s fourth carrier gets it closer to rivaling the U.S. navy, analysts said. It will compare in size to the Nimitz and Ford class U.S. carriers, which means it can carry as many as 100 aircraft, Silbey said. “That gives it much more striking power than previous carriers, which could only carry around 50,” he said. The U.S. navy has 11 carriers, all nuclear powered. Even if smaller than the U.S. fleet, a Chinese navy with nuclear-powered carriers can mount a challenge to the United States, Koh said. The U.S. navy maintains bases in Guam, Hawaii and Japan plus treaty alliances with Japan and the Philippines. The U.S. and China have long seen each other as rival superpowers. Experts have said China sent an especially large number of its naval deployments near Japan’s southernmost islands and nearby waters since a political rift that erupted in November 2025 over a remark by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The Philippines is embroiled in a maritime sovereignty dispute with China. China plans to build more carriers over the next decade for a “blue water capability that they’ve never really had before,” Silbey said. “In the Pacific, it means that they can go after American assets that are out of range of their other assets.”

title: Naval District Washington personnel sharpen crisis response skills during CNIC N73, SOTG c
zh_title: 华盛顿海军区人员在 CNIC N73、SOTG c 期间提高危机应对技能
summary: 华盛顿——来自华盛顿海军区 (NDW) 的 45 名人员参加了海军设施司令部 (CNIC) 指挥官事件管理小组/危机行动小组成员课程，这是 11 月 18 日至 19 日举行的为期两天的虚拟培训。 CNIC 为来自 NDW、中大西洋海军区、日本海军区、东南海军区和西南海军区 5 个地区 21 个基地的 120 多名学员进行了培训。该课程为分配到安装事件管理团队和区域危机行动团队的人员提供了共同的基础。 CNIC IMT/C
content:
华盛顿——来自华盛顿海军区 (NDW) 的 45 名人员参加了海军设施司令部 (CNIC) 指挥官事件管理小组/危机行动小组成员课程，这是 11 月 18 日至 19 日举行的为期两天的虚拟培训。

CNIC 为来自 NDW、中大西洋海军区、日本海军区、东南海军区和西南海军区 5 个地区 21 个基地的 120 多名学员进行了培训。该课程为分配到安装事件管理团队和区域危机行动团队的人员提供了共同的基础。

CNIC IMT/CAT 会员课程 CIN S-540-1040/CDP 25B1 是后续现场紧急行动中心/事件管理团队培训师课程的先决条件。讲师介绍了事件指挥系统、国家事件管理系统、作战中心程序、指挥官意图、通用作战图开发以及指挥、控制、通信、计算机和情报套件 (C4IS) 工具。

对于 NDW，培训帮助人员了解自己的角色并在紧急情况下协调信息、行动和建议。
NDW 地区应急管理项目总监 Greg Powe 表示：“事件管理团队/危机行动团队成员课程帮助华盛顿海军区 CAT 成员建立一个管理紧急情况的通用操作框架：了解他们的角色、保持态势感知、跨组织协调以及为指挥官提供及时的决策支持。”

Powe 表示，每个 NDW 设施都会派 IMT 成员参与，帮助建立整个地区的深度。

鲍威说：“我希望团队能够从本课程中获得的最大收获是在压力下作为危机行动团队的一部分发挥作用的实际能力，将快速发生的紧急情况转化为有组织的信息、协调一致的行动以及向领导层和支持合作伙伴提供的明确建议。”

讲师们强调，危机管理需要在紧急情况发生之前就进行深思熟虑的计划。

“应急管理不应该是一场临时游戏；而是一场规划游戏，”CNIC 海岸运营培训小组的课程讲师道格·比斯利 (Doug Beasley) 说。 “我们希望人们坐下来，了解他们的威胁是什么，他们的弱点是什么，他们如何相互合作，经历爬行、行走、跑步阶段，并确保他们知道他们需要知道的事情。”
虚拟形式允许参与者探索共同的挑战，包括标准化事件指挥系统原则如何应用于当地计划、危险、指挥关系和互助协议。
 以安装为主导的演习、熟悉紧急行动中心以及后续的现场团队课程使人员能够根据当地情况应用企业基础。

对于安装级别人员，该课程提供了有关专业部门如何融入更广泛的事件管理框架的背景信息。

“这让我对危机应对有了更全面的了解，”华盛顿海军支持活动舰队和家庭支持中心综合初级预防劳动力主管丽贝卡·劳埃德 (Rebecca Lloyd) 说。 “我曾在现实世界的紧急家庭援助中心担任临床角色，这次培训让我了解了危机应对行动的其他关键部分。”

劳埃德表示，该课程强调了了解其他团队的角色和保持良好关系的重要性。

【原文 English Original】
WASHINGTON — Forty-five personnel from across Naval District Washington (NDW) participated in the Commander, Navy Installations Command (CNIC) Incident Management Team/Crisis Action Team Member Course, a two-day virtual training held Nov. 18-19.

CNIC conducted the training for more than 120 participants from 21 installations across five regions: NDW, Navy Region Mid-Atlantic, Navy Region Japan, Navy Region Southeast and Navy Region Southwest. The course provided a common foundation for personnel assigned to installation Incident Management Teams and regional Crisis Action Teams.

The CNIC IMT/CAT Member Course, CIN S-540-1040/CDP 25B1, is a prerequisite for the follow-on, on-site Emergency Operations Center/Incident Management Team trainer course. Instructors covered the Incident Command System, National Incident Management System, operations center procedures, commander's intent, common operating picture development and Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence Suite (C4IS) tools.

For NDW, the training helps personnel understand their roles and coordinate information, actions and recommendations during an emergency.

“The Incident Management Team/Crisis Action Team Member Course helps Naval District Washington CAT members build a common operating framework for managing emergencies: understanding their roles, maintaining situational awareness, coordinating across organizations, and providing timely, decision-ready support to commanders,” said Greg Powe, NDW region emergency management program director.

Powe said each NDW installation sent IMT members to participate, helping build depth across the region.

“The biggest takeaways I hope the team can gain from this course is a practical ability to function as part of a Crisis Action Team under pressure, converting a fast-moving emergency into organized information, coordinated actions, and clear recommendations for leadership and supported partners,” Powe said.

Instructors stressed that crisis management requires deliberate planning long before an emergency occurs.

“Emergency management shouldn't be a pickup game; it’s a planning game,” said Doug Beasley, a course instructor with the CNIC Shore Operations Training Group. “We want people to sit down, understand what their threats, their vulnerabilities are, how they can work with each other, go through that crawl, walk, run phase, and make sure that they know the things that they need to know.”

The virtual format allowed participants to explore shared challenges, including how standardized Incident Command System principles apply to local plans, hazards, command relationships and mutual-aid agreements.
 Installation-led drills, Emergency Operations Center familiarization and the follow-on on-site team course enable personnel to apply the enterprise foundation in local conditions.

For installation-level personnel, the course provided context on how specialized departments integrate into the broader incident management framework.

“It gave me a better whole picture view of crisis response,” said Rebecca Lloyd, supervisor, Integrated Primary Prevention Workforce, Fleet and Family Support Center, Naval Support Activity Washington. “I have participated in a real-world Emergency Family Assistance Center in a clinical role, and this training allowed me to see the other critical parts of crisis response operations.”

Lloyd said the course reinforced the importance of understanding the roles of other teams and maintaining strong relationships with tenant commands.

“No two crisis responses are the same, and the importance of not making assumptions and strictly going off past training scenarios and standard operating procedures was a major lesson,” Lloyd said.
 The virtual IMT/CAT Member Course convenes approximately 22 times annually. It establishes individual proficiency before participants advance to local drills, tabletop exercises and team-level operations center training.

By investing in continuous emergency management training, NDW strengthens its ability to support personnel, preserve critical infrastructure, and maintain mission readiness across the National Capital Region.
 For more NDW information, please visit http://www.facebook.com/NavDistWash, http://www.instagram.com/navdistwash and the NDW website at http://www.cnic.navy.mil/regions/ndw.html.

（中央社記者廖文綺台北23日電）首次美中俄三方峰會19日落幕，學者認為，未來再度舉行的可能性不大。此外，在三方峰會前，俄羅斯轟炸機穿越日本、台灣周邊空域，俄國軍事行動及中共在第一島鏈周邊的布局，都可能牽動台海安全，值得持續關注。
兩岸政策協會今天舉辦「APEC峰會後的美中競合：經貿博弈、台海情勢與戰略抉擇」座談會，多位學者與會。
淡江大學國際事務與戰略研究所助理教授馬準威表示，美中俄三方會晤顯示未來可能形成三極體系的趨勢，他指出，三方會晤在談聯合國改革時，完全忽略過去五強中的兩強，也就是英、法，形成三強鼎立的格局。不過馬準威認為，美中俄三方會晤未來繼續進行的可能性不大，這需要在對三方都有利的情況下才會發生。
馬準威在回答中央社提問時指出，這次會晤之所以能夠促成，是中國需要對內外塑造強大形象，俄國則想停掉俄烏戰爭，扭轉國內經濟局勢；而美國則在美伊戰爭中「找不到台階下」，尤其在美國期中選舉後，美國總統川普停火壓力更大，因此需要與伊朗關係友好的中俄協助。「但未來不見得同時存在對三方有利的條件，所以它可能不見得是一個常態」。
馬準威在座談會上還提到，這次三方會晤談到削減核武，他認為「這是一種理想主義」，擁核大國之間彼此有所猜忌，後續不見得這麼樂觀。
馬準威認為，這次三方會晤最值得關注的是美伊戰爭與俄烏戰爭。他認為中美俄之間對於結束俄烏戰爭有一定程度的默契，但變數在於烏克蘭接受程度。接下來G20各國會面時，歐洲國家的態度，可能會牽動美俄之間對於俄烏戰爭解決問題的方向。
淡江大學國際事務與戰略研究所副教授林穎佑則從台灣安全角度看待美中俄戰略互動。日前2架俄羅斯Tu-95熊式戰略轟炸機穿越日本、台灣周邊空域。他指出，俄羅斯此次行動恰逢亞太經濟合作會議（APEC）期間、美中俄會晤前夕，此次飛行意味著俄國有能力將軍力投射至南海，證明俄羅斯在印太區域擁有話語權。
他強調，俄羅斯的任何行動都可能會影響到第一島鏈各國的防衛計劃，值得台灣關注。例如俄羅斯介入第一島鏈，可能使日本回歸冷戰時期的防衛，把重心放在北海道與北方四島，削弱日本在西南諸島的防衛計畫。這也是中共軍事考量之一，可能藉由跟北韓、俄羅斯的合作去牽制日韓對台海的介入。
林穎佑指出，這兩年另一個軍事熱點在南海。尤其菲律賓與美國近期有許多軍事互動；而中共遼寧號經過菲律賓突破相關島鏈，以及其他軍事行動，都顯示中共持續經營南海。
他強調，台海安全不只是台灣周遭的海空域，更會連線到第一島鏈周遭甚至以外的國家，也不是只有在台海周遭出現威脅，才對台灣有直接的國家安全威脅，第一島鏈與印太區域發生的事件都需要關注與思考。（編輯：朱建陵）1151123

summary: 日本汽车供应商加入防卫建设海峡时报 从马力到火力，日本吸引汽车供应商参与大规模军备建设 立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的发展 政府希望利用现有的工业供应链将加速日本的安全转型，同时加强其防御能力，抵御来自核武器邻国的威胁。发布于 2026 年 11 月 24 日下午 12:17 更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日下午 01:19 随着中国竞争削弱汽车制造，日本正在推动汽车供应商参与国防工作。 Aster 现在为 Anduril 生产无人机发动机，并且
content:
日本汽车供应商加入防卫建设海峡时报
从马力到火力，日本吸引汽车供应商大规模军备建设
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
日本政府希望，利用现有的工业供应链将加速日本的安全转型，加强其防御能力，抵御来自核武器邻国的威胁。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 24 日 12:17
更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日 1:19
由于中国的竞争削弱了汽车制造业，日本正在推动汽车供应商参与国防工作。 Aster 现在为 Anduril 生产无人机电机，国防销售达到收入的 10%。
在美国的支持下，东京希望加快针对中国、俄罗斯和朝鲜的重新军备。 ATLA 正在将供应商与军火公司联系起来，并为无人机技术提供资金。
小型零部件制造商首先采取行动，而丰田、本田和日产则对声誉和与中​​国的关系保持谨慎。日本想要更多无人机，但国内产量仍然很低。
日本横手——多年来，日本制造商 Aster 通过为丰田汽车供应零部件赚钱。
但随着该国汽车工业在激烈的中国竞争中举步维艰，Aster 在国防技术领域找到了新的利基市场。
其电动机为美国军事技术公司 Anduril 制造的无人机提供动力，自 2025 年进入该行业以来，国防工作收入已增长至十分之一。
“无人机是一项更好的业务，”首席执行官本乡武信(Takenobu Hongo)在谈到Aster对国防承包的拥护时说道，长期以来，这个几十年来和平主义塑造的国家的公民一直对国防承包持谨慎态度。 “目前，对我们来说，汽车电机的利润并不高。”
根据对包括政府官员、公司高管和首相高市早苗内阁顾问在内的九人的采访，东京鼓励日本众多汽车供应商加入该国自二战以来最大规模的军事集结，Aster 的战略重点是其举措的一部分。
高市政府希望，利用现有的工业供应链将加速日本的安全转型，加强其防御能力，抵御来自核邻国中国、俄罗斯和朝鲜的威胁。
重新军备的努力得到了东京主要安全伙伴美国的支持，美国正在敦促盟国增加武装部队支出。
此次集结还为日本曾经世界领先的汽车业提供了一条重要的多元化途径。日本汽车制造商协会的数据显示，到 2025 年，日本工厂的汽车产量将比十年前减少近 90 万辆。
路透社首次报道了该行业刚刚进军国防部门的详细信息，以及负责监督国防部采购的采购、技术和物流局 (ATLA) 如何为其提供支持。
一名机构官员和四名高管表示，该部门一直在评估 Aster 等供应商，将它们与军火公司配对，并提供新的资金来源。
高市内阁顾问 Koko Kato 在帮助引导行业转型方面也发挥了作用。她说，如果国防和汽车之间存在协同作用，汽车制造商“应该抓住机会”。
加藤告诉路透社，她在二月份监督了一项单独的贸易部计划的修改，旨在帮助汽车供应商多元化进入国防和其他行业。
ATLA 在回答路透社问题时表示，它是帮助寻求进入市场的公司的联络点。

【原文 English Original】
Japan auto suppliers join defence build-up | The Straits Times
From horsepower to firepower, Japan draws auto suppliers into major arms build-up
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The government hopes that tapping existing industrial supply chains will speed up Japan’s security transformation as it bolsters its defences against threats from its nuclear-armed neighbours.
Published Nov 24, 2026, 12:17 PM
Updated Nov 24, 2026, 01:19 PM
Japan is pushing auto suppliers into defence work as Chinese competition weakens carmaking. Aster now makes drone motors for Anduril, and defence sales reached 10% of revenue.
Tokyo, backed by the US, wants to speed up rearmament against China, Russia and North Korea. ATLA is linking suppliers with arms firms and funding drone technology.
Small parts makers are moving first, while Toyota, Honda and Nissan stay cautious over reputation and China ties. Japan wants more drones, but domestic output is still very low.
YOKOTE, Japan – For years, Japanese manufacturer Aster made its money supplying parts for Toyota vehicles.
But as the country’s auto industry struggles in the face of fierce Chinese competition, Aster has found a new niche in defence technology.
Its electric motors power drones built by US military technology company Anduril, and defence work has grown to a tenth of revenue since it entered the sector in 2025.
“Drones are a much better business,” chief executive Takenobu Hongo said of Aster’s embrace of defence contracting, which has long been viewed warily by citizens of a country shaped by decades of pacifism. “At the moment, for us, automotive motors aren’t very profitable.”
Aster’s pivot is part of a move by Tokyo to encourage Japan’s many auto suppliers to join the country’s biggest military build-up since World War II, according to interviews with nine people, including government officials, company executives and an adviser to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s Cabinet.
Takaichi’s government hopes that tapping existing industrial supply chains will speed up Japan’s security transformation as it bolsters its defences against threats from nuclear-armed neighbours China, Russia and North Korea.
The rearmament efforts are backed by Tokyo’s chief security partner, the United States, which is pressing allies to increase spending on armed forces.
The build-up also offers an important diversification avenue to Japan’s once world-leading auto industry. The country’s factories built nearly 900,000 fewer vehicles in 2025 than a decade earlier, according to the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association.
Reuters is reporting for the first time details of the industry’s nascent push into the defence sector and how it is supported by the Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA), which oversees defence ministry procurement.
The department has been evaluating suppliers like Aster, pairing them with arms firms and offering new funding streams, an agency official and four executives said.
An adviser to Takaichi’s Cabinet, Koko Kato, has also played a role in helping steer the industry’s transformation. If there is a synergy between defence and autos, carmakers “should take the opportunity”, she said.
Kato told Reuters she oversaw changes in February to a separate trade ministry programme aimed at helping auto suppliers diversify into defence and other industries.
ATLA said in response to Reuters questions that it serves as a point of contact to help companies seeking to enter the defence industry and that it will continue to work with other government departments to encourage new entrants.
Takaichi’s office did not respond to questions.

Here’s how Japan can curb rising home prices: Tax foreign buyers more
Takaichi’s government has pledged to lay out a new security strategy by year-end, including a road map for bolstering an arms industry that was initially dismantled after Japan’s World War II defeat.
The plan builds on Japan’s legacy as a manufacturing powerhouse. Despite its auto industry’s recent decline, Japan is still the world’s third-largest vehicle-producing nation.
The industry manufactures more than eight million vehicles a year and supports one in 10 jobs, with some 70,000 companies making an enormous array of components.
Skills prized in auto manufacturing, such as precision and electronics manufacturing, as well as quality control, are relevant to arms production, said Pontus Haggstrom, a Japan-based adviser to the auto industry and former chief executive of Stellantis Japan.
The industry “also knows how to produce complex products reliably and at scale”, he added.
The case for Japan to draw on domestic manufacturing has also grown as American arms makers struggle to replenish arsenals depleted by conflicts in the Middle East and Europe.
Tokyo was the destination for about a tenth of US weapon exports in 2021-2025, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.
“Customers tell us their traditional suppliers don’t have the capacity,” said Hiroko Suzuki, the CEO of car-engine component maker Kyowa Industrial, which has received a growing number of orders for prototype drone engines.
While Kyowa has long made missile-related components, the defence sideline now comprises 10% of annual sales, up from 3% in spring 2025.
Some auto suppliers are also eyeing opportunities to sell to US and European military contractors.
ATLA has been holding events in Tokyo to connect Japanese suppliers with potential Western clients. Some 48 Japanese companies from various industries took part in a September event, twice as many as 2025, the procurement agency said.
ATLA, which in October launched a funding programme for the development and testing of new military technology, has encouraged some auto suppliers to produce components for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
The agency has said it is willing to provide millions of dollars in support to projects that advance to prototype development.
Ishikawa Energy Research’s gasoline engine-powered drone flies during a demonstration near its factory in Japan on Nov 6.
The upcoming national security strategy is expected to outline plans to arm Japan with fleets of attack and interceptor drones of the kind that have reshaped warfare elsewhere.
But domestic industrial production is tiny: The country exported just over 1,100 drones in 2025, compared with the roughly 123,000 UAVs sold to overseas clients by neighbouring Taiwan, according to trade figures compiled by Taiwan’s Research Institute for Democracy, Society and Emerging Technology.
While fiscal constraints are likely to force Tokyo to rethink some existing orders for missiles and aircraft, such is Japan’s need for UAVs that drone-related spending will likely be ringfenced, according to an official familiar with budget plans.
Toru Tokushige, CEO of Japanese dronemaker Terra Drone, said ATLA officials recently introduced him to Kaaz, a maker of racing car parts that has developed a small gasoline-powered aircraft engine. Tapping auto suppliers could significantly increase Japan’s drone-building capacity, he said.
A spokesperson for Kaaz said that it has consulted with ATLA and is actively pursuing the development of engines for military drones.
Ishikawa Energy Research, a drone start-up that attended ATLA’s September forum, is also seeking military applications for its aircraft.
Employees of Ishikawa Energy Research work on an assembly line producing petrol engine-powered drones at the company's factory in Ota on Nov 6.
The firm’s UAVs are used mainly for agricultural purposes such as crop spraying, founder Mitsuru Ishikawa told Reuters. But the former Honda engineer said his petrol-powered drones could also transport heavier defence equipment or conduct longer-range military reconnaissance missions than more common battery-powered models.
The firm, which is based in the industrial town of Ota, has already tapped into the sprawling local auto supply chain that feeds carmaker Subaru, with more than 50% of the components in its drones coming from auto suppliers.
Ishikawa does not think those firms will object to his military ambitions, in part because Subaru, which is better known globally for its sporty cars, already has a major defence arm.
The company has built military aircraft, including attack helicopters, for Japan’s Self-Defense Forces for decades.
Subaru expects defence-related demand to grow and intends to capture those business opportunities, a spokesperson said, declining to give specific forecasts.
Mitsuru Ishikawa, founder of Ishikawa Energy Research, does not think firms will object to his military ambitions, in part because Subaru, which is better known globally for its sporty cars, already has a major defence arm.
The auto industry’s shift to defence contracting is for now largely limited to smaller parts makers, according to five officials and analysts.
Japan’s big three automakers – Toyota, Honda and Nissan – have shown little appetite for a defence tilt. They still have substantive businesses in China, which has criticised Japan’s arms build-up.
They have also long been wary of the reputational risks that come with the defence sector.
“The company’s basic position at this point is that we will not do anything related to defence,” senior Toyota executive Hiroyuki Ueda said at a results briefing earlier in November.
Nissan declined to comment on potential defence work, while Honda said in response to questions that it has no specific plans to enter the sector.
That hesitancy also filters down to their closest suppliers.
Mitsubishi Electric chief financial officer Kenichiro Fujimoto told Reuters that some auto parts makers it had approached for a new military drone venture had declined to participate. The suppliers, which Fujimoto did not name, were worried about upsetting their main customers, he said.
Aster’s Hongo was also wary that some of his company’s roughly 100 staff might object when he gathered them at his factory in the northern Japanese town of Yokote in November 2025 to announce that Anduril wanted to use their motors.
Instead, the 71-year-old executive received a warm reception. “Everyone was more like: ‘Wow, that’s impressive!’” he said of the meeting.
The commercial opportunities in defence, as well as growing public concern about Japan’s security challenges, would lure many more companies, Hongo predicted.
“In Japan now, there are very few people who think this is somebody else’s problem,” he said. REUTERS

summary: 关于台湾地方选举的五个事实和问题|海峡时报 关于台湾地方选举的五个事实和问题 立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展 发布于 2026 年 11 月 24 日上午 11:57 更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日上午 11:57 11 月 24 日 - 台湾将于周六举行地方选举，这是总统大选前对执政的民进党 (DPP) 和主要反对党国民党 (KMT) 的支持率的关键考验以及 2028 年初的议会民意调查。以下是有关选举的五个事实和问题： 每四年举行一次的选举选择城市
content:
关于台湾地方选举的五个事实和问题|海峡时报
关于台湾地方选举的五个事实和问题
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发布于 2026 年 11 月 24 日上午 11:57
更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日 11:57
11 月 24 日 - 台湾将于周六举行地方选举，这是在 2028 年初总统和议会选举之前对执政的民进党 (DPP) 和主要反对党国民党 (KMT) 的支持率的关键考验。
以下是有关选举的五个事实和问题：
每四年举行一次选举，选举所有22个市县的市长和县长。
市和县议员以及其他一些较低级别的官员（包括区长）也将被选举产生。
近2000万选民有资格选举11051名各级政府官员。
周六晚上早些时候结果应该会很清楚。
主要问题是什么？中国问题是否已列入议程？
竞选活动的重点是交通和环境等当地问题，而不是台湾与中国的有争议的关系，中国将这个民主统治的岛屿视为自己的领土。
市长、县长和议员并不直接对中国政策负责。
在反对派的推动下，还将举行一场关于核电的公投，问题是“你是否支持政府利用核能振兴经济并废除‘无核家园’能源政策？”
台湾政府已表示对重启核电站持开放态度，最后一座核电站将于 2025 年关闭。
2022 年最后一次地方选举发生了什么？
国民党击败了民进党，赢得了14个市县，而民进党则赢得了5个。台湾人民党赢得了两场胜利，还有一个独立党赢得了胜利。
周六值得观看的主要比赛有哪些？
两党都把精力集中在富裕、人口众多的“六市”，即台湾最多的六个城市。
值得关注的主要竞争是台北市长选举，现任国民党议员蒋万安面临着民进党议员沉彪马的挑战，沉彪马是一名学者出身的立法者，也是中国虚假信息专家。
其他值得关注的城市包括台湾人口最多的城市新北，目前由国民党控制，以及南部的民进党传统据点高雄，国民党正在那里大力竞选。
法律禁止在选举前 10 天内报道民意调查。
这次投票对 2028 年选举意味着什么？
周六投票结束后，将认真开始决定总统候选人，从而提供政党支持的最新概况。尽管赖清德总统几乎肯定会参加宪法规定的第二届也是最后一届任期，但国民党尚未确认其候选人。
国民党的领跑者可能是前记者、现任台中市市长的卢秀彦。
台北市市长蒋介石是一匹黑马，尽管假设国民党在 2028 年选举中失利，但人们普遍认为他是 2032 年的可能候选人。路透社

Five facts and questions about Taiwan's local elections | The Straits Times
Five facts and questions about Taiwan's local elections
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 24, 2026, 11:57 AM
Updated Nov 24, 2026, 11:57 AM
Nov 24 - Taiwan holds local elections on Saturday, a key test of support for both the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the main opposition Kuomintang (KMT) party ahead of presidential and parliamentary polls in early 2028.
Here are five facts and questions about the elections:
The elections, held every four years, choose city mayors and county magistrates in all 22 cities and counties.
City and county councillors will also be elected along with some other lower level officials, including borough chiefs.
Nearly 20 million voters are eligible to elect 11,051 officials at various levels of government.
The results should be clear by early Saturday evening.
WHAT ARE THE MAIN ISSUES AND IS CHINA ON THE AGENDA?
Campaigning has focused on local issues such as transport and the environment, rather than Taiwan's contested relations with China, which views the democratically-ruled island as its own territory.
Mayors, county magistrates and councillors are not directly responsible for China policy.
There will also be a referendum, pushed by the opposition, on nuclear power, asking the question "Do you support the government revitalising the economy with nuclear energy and abolishing the 'nuclear-free homeland' energy policy?"
Taiwan's government has already signalled it is open to restarting nuclear power plants, the last of which shut in 2025.
WHAT HAPPENED AT THE LAST LOCAL ELECTION IN 2022?
The KMT thrashed the DPP, winning 14 cities and counties to the DPP's five. The Taiwan People's Party won two, and an independent one.
WHAT ARE THE KEY RACES TO WATCH ON SATURDAY?
Both parties have concentrated efforts in the wealthy and populous "six municipalities", or Taiwan's six most cities.
The main race to watch is for the Taipei mayorship, where the incumbent Chiang Wan-an from the KMT is facing a challenge from the DPP's Puma Shen, an academic-turned-lawmaker and an expert on Chinese disinformation.
Other cities to watch are Taiwan's most populous city, New Taipei, which is now held by the KMT, and traditional DPP stronghold Kaohsiung in the south, where the KMT is campaigning hard.
Reporting on opinion polls is banned by law in the 10 days before the election.
WHAT WILL THIS VOTE MEAN FOR THE 2028 ELECTION?
Manoeuvring to decide presidential candidates will begin in earnest once Saturday's vote is done, giving an updated snapshot of party support. While President Lai Ching-te will almost certainly stand for his constitutionally limited second and last term, the KMT has not confirmed its candidate.
The likely front runner for the KMT is former journalist Lu Shiow-yen, current mayor of the central city of Taichung.
A dark horse is Taipei mayor Chiang, though he is more generally considered the likely candidate for 2032, assuming the KMT loses the 2028 election. REUTERS

content:
台湾选举与中国无关，但北京有很多话要说 |海峡时报
台湾选举与中国无关，但北京有很多话要说
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发布于 2026 年 11 月 24 日上午 11:57
更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日 1:42
台北，11 月 24 日 - 周六的台湾市长和县长选举与中国无关，但执政党提名台北市长——一位因“分裂国家”罪名被中国警方通缉的议员——引发了北京方面的一系列谴责。
中国将台湾视为自己的领土，但并不统治这个民主岛屿，称执政的民进党台北候选人沉普马是一个“叛徒”，他正在渲染中国威胁，以欺骗人们投票给他。
10月，台北检方起诉四人，称他们在沉家外停放的一辆摩托车上安装了监控装置，并对两名香港人发出了逮捕令，称他们是该计划的幕后黑手。
同月，中国主要官方广播机构中央电视台称，沉通过“打反对中国牌”和利用谈论外部干预选举的“小伎俩”来“欺骗性”拉选票。
中国上个月对他父亲在中国的企业实施了制裁，进一步加强了对沉的制裁。
台北一再指责北京在地方选举前加强行动，包括军事活动、网络攻击和信息战。
台湾最高中国政策制定者邱垂正对路透社表示：“多年来，中国共产党将其对台政策与台湾选举的结果挂钩，使得选前干预不可避免。”
陆委会主任邱说，这种干涉“只会适得其反，加深台湾人民对中共政权的不满”。
中国台湾事务办公室没有回应置评请求。它长期以来一直否认干涉台湾选举的指控。
沉本人并没有将中国作为其竞选的主要焦点，而是将注意力集中在城市更新等问题上。
民进党此前只在陈水扁的领导下执掌过台北一次，时间是1994年至1998年。他后来成为民进党在台湾的第一任总统。
沉先生吸引了被称为“洋流”的热情支持基础，最初是由关心中国的选民推动的，后来又因沉先生以政策为重的竞选活动而得到加强，沉先生在竞选活动中详细描述了如果他获胜将做什么。
他的对手、现任市长蒋万安来自主要反对党国民党，该党历来主张与中国保持密切关系。该公司董事长郑丽媛今年早些时候在北京会见了中国国家主席习近平。
蒋介石因一年一度的台北-上海城市论坛而为中国所熟知。在竞选期间，他也基本上没有谈论与中国的关系，而是关注水安全等问题，以及英伟达如何在他的领导下签署在台北建立新总部的协议。
“顽固的台独分裂分子”
两名民进党高级官员告诉路透社，沉阳利用了亲台湾的认同感，成为反抗中国的象征——这令许多人感到惊讶，甚至在他自己的党内也是如此。
一位不愿透露姓名的官员表示：“他唤醒了新的亲台精神。”

Taiwan's elections not about China, but Beijing has a lot to say | The Straits Times
Taiwan's elections not about China, but Beijing has a lot to say
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 24, 2026, 11:57 AM
Updated Nov 24, 2026, 01:42 PM
TAIPEI, Nov 24 - Taiwan's mayoral and county chief elections on Saturday are not directly about China, but the ruling party's nomination for Taipei mayor — a lawmaker wanted by Chinese police for "separatism" — has sent Beijing into a flurry of denunciations.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory but does not govern the democratic island, says the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Taipei candidate Puma Shen is a "traitor" who is playing up the China threat to trick people into voting for him.
In October, Taipei prosecutors indicted four people for putting monitoring devices on a scooter parked outside Shen's home, issuing arrest warrants for two people from Hong Kong it said were behind the scheme.
The same month, China's main state broadcaster CCTV said Shen was "deceptively" seeking votes by "playing the oppose China card" and using "little tricks" by talking about external interference in the election.
China last month imposed sanctions on his father's business in China, adding to those already on Shen.
Taipei has repeatedly accused Beijing of stepping up operations ahead of local elections including military activity, cyberattacks and information warfare.
"For years, the Chinese Communist Party has tied its Taiwan policy to the outcome of Taiwan's elections, making pre-election interference inevitable," Taiwan's top China policy maker, Chiu Chui-cheng, told Reuters.
Such interference "will only backfire and deepen resentment among the people of Taiwan toward the Chinese Communist regime," said Chiu, who heads the Mainland Affairs Council.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to requests for comment. It has long rejected accusations it interferes in Taiwanese elections.
Shen himself has not made China a major focus of his campaign, instead concentrating on issues like urban renewal.
The DPP has only run Taipei once before, under Chen Shui-bian from 1994 to 1998. He later went on to become the DPP's first president of Taiwan.
Shen has attracted a passionate support base known as the "Ocean Current," initially driven by voters concerned about China and later strengthened by Shen's policy-heavy campaigning, in which he described in detail what he would do if he won.
His opponent, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an, is from the main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT), which traditionally favours close ties with China. Its chairwoman, Cheng Li-wun, met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing earlier this year.
Chiang is well-known to China thanks to the annual Taipei-Shanghai city forum. He also has largely held off talking about relations with China during the campaign, focusing on issues like water safety and how under his leadership Nvidia signed a deal to build a new headquarters in Taipei.
'DIEHARD TAIWAN INDEPENDENCE SEPARATIST'
Two senior DPP officials told Reuters that Shen had tapped into a sense of pro-Taiwan identity and become a symbol of defiance against China — to the surprise of many, even within his own party.
"He has awakened a renewed pro-Taiwan spirit," said one of the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Shen was put on the list of obstinate "Taiwan independence" separatists by China's Taiwan Affairs Office in October, 2024, which also sanctioned the Kuma Academy he co-founded, which runs civil defence courses to prepare people to deal with a possible attack from Beijing.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office last year called him a "diehard Taiwan independence separatist in every sense of the word", saying people like him are "traitors to the Chinese nation and criminals".
Shen told Reuters earlier this month that China did not like his previous work about trying to bring greater global attention to disinformation.
"We try to tell other countries, hey, you need to be aware of this Chinese influence operation in your country," he said.
Chiang's campaign team said he did not have time to accept an interview.
It previously told Reuters that "no outside force should exert political pressure on Taiwan's democratic elections" and it opposed any "domestic or outside forces that use any means to intervene in, interfere with, or influence voters' voting intentions".
Reporting on opinion polls is banned by law in the 10 days before the election. REUTERS

Trump to meet NATO chief ​Mark Rutte on Wednesday, White House says

Published Nov 24, 2026, 11:52 AM
Updated Nov 24, 2026, 11:52 AM
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 - US President Donald Trump will meet NATO chief Mark Rutte on Wednesday in Florida, the White House said on Monday, with the meeting coming after the Republican leader met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week in Asia.
• The White House said Trump and Rutte will meet late in the afternoon on Wednesday in Palm Beach, Florida.
• Trump, who has been critical of America's Western allies, cast both Putin and Xi as his "friend" when he met them last week at a summit.
• Trump's meeting with Putin triggered a backlash among both European allies and Trump's Democratic opponents at home.
• Rutte, who has repeatedly tried to soothe tensions within NATO and keep Trump onside, said it was normal for major nuclear powers to meet.
• Rutte's meeting with Trump also comes as Europe has pushed to be included in US-backed talks to end Russia's war in Ukraine.
• Trump has often criticized Washington's Western and democratic allies over issues like NATO spending, trade tariffs and what he casts as their inadequate support for Washington during the US-Israeli war on Iran.
• Trump was open to security guarantees for Ukraine based on the NATO alliance's Article 5 mutual defense agreement, and that Russia had grown "comfortable" with that, US special envoy and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said last week as he sought to reassure allies.
• Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who has been criticized by Trump, has said Europe had to be included in peace talks. REUTERS

（中央社記者陳俊華台北24日電）選戰倒數4天，民進黨立法院黨團書記長范雲今天表示，根據國安單位、陸委會資料，中共介選樣態包括非法資金挹注，資助特定候選人或政治團體，還有落地招待廉價旅遊、廉價機票動員返台投票等。黨團呼籲，民眾要有能力辨識這些手法，再做出選擇。
范雲、黨團副幹事長陳培瑜上午舉行輿情回應記者會。陳培瑜指出，中共介選已發展出新策略，關於「交通」的包括，第1，「串聯協力團體」，中國國台辦、地方台辦，透過旅遊、航空業者，提供台商及其家人返鄉機票優惠及補助，希望動員台商回台投票，並指定支持特定候選人。
陳培瑜表示，第2，如果補助吸引力不夠，甚至「贈送免費機票」，透過願配合的中配團體，調查投票意願、盤點清單，再由專人發放來回機票；第3，「提供交通優惠」，刻意調降回台投票機票價格，提供機場貴賓室、機場接駁等，讓大家覺得回台投票沒什麼成本。
陳培瑜說，第4，「預留返台機位」，當航班、機位不夠時，確實會降低返鄉投票意願，於是中國利用可控制的國家航空公司，預留很多返台機位。最後第5，「協調海空疏運」，在金門、馬祖有小三通，透過小三通可回台灣投票，這事情在過去也屢屢發生。
陳培瑜表示，當中國用這些手段且指定要投給特定候選人時，就代表這些候選人未來在政策上可能會配合中國操作，不論是里長、代表、議員等，都是民眾要考慮的，要先有能力辨識這些手段，才問自己要做出什麼選擇。
范雲說，中共介選樣態包括非法資金挹注，資助特定候選人或政治團體，提供其選舉所需資源，例如民眾黨桃園市議員候選人周曉芸案，就是非法資金挹注的問題。另外，還有落地招待廉價旅遊、廉價機票動員返台投票等。
范雲指出，假訊息與認知操作、網路入侵竊取選舉情資部分，國際有許多智庫報告指出，台灣是中共網路入侵、攻擊的第一大受害者。「經濟利誘差別待遇」是選擇性開放特定縣市農產品輸中，綁定經貿利益，讓選民、小農受影響。
范雲表示，「點名懲戒，威嚇候選人及支持者」、「共機擾台架次新高」，也是威嚇選民的方式，想讓大家覺得若支持某黨候選人，可能會帶來更多的軍事威脅。這些都是國安單位、陸委會整理的中共介選方式。（編輯：萬淑彰）1151124

SINGAPORE - Surging electric truck sales in China resulting from higher oil prices are driving demand for lithium, an unexpected bright spot for the battery metal that has been dragged down by market worries of oversupply.
Electric truck sales in China, the biggest market for EVs and the dominant producer of batteries powering them, hit 600 000 in the first 10 months of the year, up 45%, accounting for 30% of sales across truck sizes, according to BofA Global Research.
Growth is strongest for heavy trucks, which have the largest batteries containing the most lithium, with sales up 68% to 262 000 units.
While still small compared with car exports, Chinese heavy electric truck exports more than doubled to 16 823 in the four months after US-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, data from China's General Administration of Customs showed. About half went to South and Southeast Asia, where higher fuel costs strengthened demand for electric vehicles.
Electric trucks globally will use nearly 7% of lithium supply this year and 12% by 2030 — which would be equivalent to demand from up to 11.5-million battery electric cars, YJ Lee, a fund manager at Singapore-based Arcane Green Metal Fund who invests in lithium projects, told Reuters.
China's Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL), the world's largest manufacturer of EV and energy storage system batteries, described commercial vehicles as a growth area.
"Following passenger vehicles and energy storage, the next major opportunity lies in the electrification of commercial road transport, especially heavy-duty trucks," CATL said in response to Reuters queries.
UK-based consultancy SFA Oxford has raised its 2026 forecast for lithium demand from heavy-duty EVs by 95% in the last year, said Lakshya Gupta, senior market analyst.
Still, lithium prices remain weighed down by uncertain demand from energy storage systems. Prices have nearly halved since touching in May their highest level since September 2023, with earlier optimism tempered by patchy installation rates in China and slowing domestic EV sales.
Lithium futures on China's Guangzhou Futures Exchange (GFEX) have fallen as traders bet on a surplus and buyers held off on stocking in anticipation prices would fall further, analysts said.
Expectations for a surplus intensified as new mines and restarts of idled operations added supply after the price rally earlier this year.
The lithium market is notoriously volatile and has been buffeted this year by policy shocks, including Zimbabwe's export curbs and licensing delays at a major Chinese mine, and by speculative trading on the GFEX.
Chinese buyers are unwilling to "catch the falling knife" in a declining market, Fastmarkets' senior lithium analyst Connor Watts said.
"The Chinese utility and commercial vehicle industry isn't large enough to be singularly supporting lithium prices at this moment," he added.

content:
香港大埔宏福苑去年11月26日发生致命大火，造成168人罹难，港府星期二（11月24日）宣布再推出两项新生活支援补助，其中每名遇难者家属获得20万港元。图为灾后的大埔宏福苑。 （香港中通社）
香港大埔宏福苑去年11月26日发生致命大火，造成168人罹难。港府宣布再推出两项新生活支援补助，其中每名遇难者家属获得20万港元（3万2932新元）。
据香港政府公报，香港特区政府星期二（11月24日）宣布在大埔宏福苑援助基金（援助基金）下推出两项新生活支援补助。
援助基金将向每名宏福苑单位的业主发放30万港元补助。补助将分两期发放，第一期的15万港元于今年12月底与第三期的租金补助一同发放；第二期的15万港元于2027年6月底与第四期的租金补助一同发放。
上述补助提供予所有宏福苑业主。如业主已出售或将出售业权予政府，补助将发放予单位业权出售前的业主。
援助基金会也向罹难者家属发放补助。每名罹难者家属获发20万港元，补助将于今年12月底起一笔过全数发放。
上述补助透过社会福利署的“一户一社工”机制发放，业主以及罹难者家属无需另行作出申请。
另据香港《星岛日报》报道，香港民政及青年事务局局长麦美娟受访时，首次公开48亿港元援助基金的来源和去向。
她说，除了政府拨出的3亿港元启动资金外，社会各界共捐出约45亿港元，涉及逾29.9万宗捐款。按宗数计算，1万港元以下捐款约29万宗，占整体约97%；5万港元以下捐款则达29.6万宗，占99%，这批小额捐款合共约4.3亿元。
据介绍，基金近40亿港元均来自100万港元或以上的大额捐款，占公众捐款额逾八成。捐助者包括履行企业社会责任的香港企业、华侨组织，以及透过中国人民银行于去年11月28日开通的绿色通道或驻港机构捐款的大陆企业。
至于支出分布，麦美娟称，基金约28亿港元用于支援政府收购业权工作，其余约20亿港元则全数用于支援居民生活，包括火灾后即时推出的13项措施，涵盖每户10万港元生活津贴、业主及租户搬迁补助、学生与外佣及屋苑工友2万港元“应急钱”，以及租金补助等，再加上今次两项新生活支援补助。

title: Trump, Xi agreed that military AI decisions should involve humans, Bessent says
zh_title: 贝森特表示，特朗普和习近平一致认为军事人工智能决策应让人类参与

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。贝森特表示：“我认为，特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与情报情报机构做出的任何军事决策，并且不应允许情报情报机构在重大军事行动中自主行事，这一点非常重要。”贝森特指的是特朗普政府对该技术的首选术语“超级智能”。贝森特表示，美中就该技术的军事使用达成的协议需要人类参与和其他保障措施，不会受到两国人工智能霸主竞争的影响。他补充说，美国人工智能实验室需要保持其技术领先地位，作为抵御网络攻击中使用的“危险”中国人工智能模型的最佳防御手段。贝森特说：“但是，当双方都同意不应该在无人参与的情况下发起任何重大军事行动时，这与竞争无关。”
他表示，涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名与他有恋情的中国公民的间谍指控并未在特习双边会晤中提及。贝森特表示，在特朗普采取他所谓的“非常强硬的路线”后，英伟达的第二级人工智能芯片 H200 仍然是中国可以通过许可购买的最先进的芯片。 “我认为我们看到的是中国人在 H200 上的订单很少，因为他们试图构建自己的芯片堆栈，而且我认为他们可能落后了很多年，”他补充道。英伟达丑闻发生后，贝森特淡化了财政部长和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在人工智能芯片限制问题上所表达的分歧，称特朗普政府官员“都致力于遵循特朗普总统的指示”。美国商务部周一采取措施，进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，包括中国实体可以租用计算能力的海外数据中心使用的芯片。 “我认为我们将会看到适当的芯片限制已经到位，并且远程访问已经被限制，”他说。

【原文 English Original】
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday. Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump’s trip to Asia. “I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology, “super intelligence.” Bessent said that the U.S.-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries’ competition for AI supremacy. He added that U.S. AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against “dangerous” Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks. “But there’s nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved,” Bessent said. He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting. Bessent said that Nvidia’s second-tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a “very firm line.” “I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind,” he added. Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were “all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.” The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power. “I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed,” he said.

Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，尤其是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

title: 涉嫌受贿 中共西安市委原书记方红卫被提起公诉
summary: 面对涉嫌受贿指控的中共陕西西安市委原书记方红卫，被提起公诉。 （互联网） 面对涉嫌受贿指控的中共陕西省委原常委、西安市委原书记方红卫，被提起公诉。 中国最高人民检察院星期二（11月24日）在微信公众号通报，方红卫涉嫌受贿一案，由国家监察委员会调查终结，移送检察机关审查起诉。最高人民检察院以涉嫌受贿罪对方红卫作出逮捕决定，并指定由甘肃省兰州市人民检察院审查起诉。兰州市人民检察院已向兰州市中级人民法院提起公诉。 根据通报，检察机关起诉指控方红卫利用担任陕西汽车集团有限责任公司董事
content:
面对涉嫌受贿指控的中共陕西西安市委原书记方红卫，被提起公诉。 （互联网）
面对涉嫌受贿指控的中共陕西省委原常委、西安市委原书记方红卫，被提起公诉。
中国最高人民检察院星期二（11月24日）在微信公众号通报，方红卫涉嫌受贿一案，由国家监察委员会调查终结，移送检察机关审查起诉。最高人民检察院以涉嫌受贿罪对方红卫作出逮捕决定，并指定由甘肃省兰州市人民检察院审查起诉。兰州市人民检察院已向兰州市中级人民法院提起公诉。
根据通报，检察机关起诉指控方红卫利用担任陕西汽车集团有限责任公司董事、总经理，党委常委、董事长，党委书记、董事长，陕西汽车控股集团有限公司党委书记、董事长，陕西重型汽车有限公司副董事长、总经理，陕西省汉中市委副书记、市长，市委书记，陕西省委常委、西安市委书记等职务上的便利，为他人谋取利益，非法收受他人财物，数额特别巨大，“依法应当以受贿罪追究其刑事责任”。
公开资料显示，今年60岁的方红卫是陕西富平人，研究生学历，工学博士学位，高级经济师。1989年从清华大学毕业后，他在陕西汽车制造总厂、陕汽集团任职长达26年。
方红卫在2015年出任宝鸡市委常委、副市长，其后多次履新，担任过渭南副市长、汉中市长、汉中市委书记。他在2021年11月任陕西省委常委、西安市委书记。
方红卫去年11月官宣被查。香港《明报》曾引述西安消息人士报道，在官宣被查前两天，方红卫当天原定调研西安市宗教工作，并拟对行程作公开报道，以就外界指他“神隐”出事辟谣。不过，方红卫在半路就被中共中央纪委人员拦下带走。
报道也引述一名在当地经商的外省企业家称，方红卫不仅本人涉贪，还纵容、默许亲属利用他的影响力谋取私利。 “当地商界都知道，方红卫妻子、妹妹‘胃口很大’。”
官方后来在今年7月通报，方红卫严重违纪违法被开除党籍和公职，并指方红卫对组织不忠诚不老实，履行全面从严治党主体责任不力，干扰巡视工作，对抗组织审查，搞迷信活动；违规拥有非上市公司股份，利用职权和职务影响为亲属谋取利益，纵容、默许配偶利用本人职务影响谋取私利；家风不正，对家人失管失教。

这对中国来说也是一个巨大的胜利。” （观看）关于空中交通管制：“这是有 50 年历史的设备，必须更换……上届政府花费了数十亿美元，然后他们试图将其连接起来，但没有成功；” “它不仅不起作用，而且还让它倒退。所以，我们希望它能得到修复，我们希望它能够正确修复……当它完成后，我们将拥有世界上最好的系统。” （观看）关于最近的技术中断：“一切都很好。这些都是个人事件……我也认为媒体对此很感兴趣。如果这些事情发生在两年前、三年前，在极其无能和腐败的拜登政府，没有人会提到它……如果有人对我们这样做并且我们发现了这件事，他们知道我会受到什么影响。没有人会和我们一起玩游戏。” （观看）关于伊朗：“他们想要达成协议，但我想要一项可以持久的协议……如果我们有一位糟糕的总统，一位软弱的总统，我想要一项能够取代总统的协议……无论如何，我们都会完成它。” （观看）关于在新国会中与民主党人合作：“民主党人对我的评价非常惊人。没有人会相信……他们想要做交易。我拥有否决权……我有一种感觉，这将是令人难以置信的富有成效的两年。
因为他们会向我发送一份有关医疗保健的法案，我会说不行，我会否决它，然后他们会给我打电话……然后我们就坐下来。” （观看）关于超级智能：“昨晚我整晚都和习主席在一起，在晚宴上坐在他旁边，就在他的右手边，我们整个晚上都在说话，我们谈论了这个问题，他对我们在这方面做得如此出色感到惊讶。我们正在领导中国，我们正在领导全世界。” （观看）关于伊朗脏弹阴谋的报道：“有迹象表明伊朗正在关注天然气，他们正在关注生物——生物武器，不是很好——以及其他东西，我们会看到......这些都是令人讨厌的人......听着，如果我

Key moments: On China and President Xi: “The relationship that I have with China is a great one. You know, it’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship. You saw the seating last night. You saw the greeting yesterday… This is a great President, one of the great Presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody — and not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people… the soldiers, the whole thing. It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.” ( Watch ) On air traffic control: “This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed… They spent billions of dollars, the previous Administration, and then they tried to hook it up and it didn’t work; not only didn’t it work, it set it back. So, we want it fixed, and we want it fixed right… When it’s finished, we will have the best system anywhere in the world.” ( Watch ) On recent tech outages: “Everything’s good. These are individual events… I also think that the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would have happened two years ago, three years ago in the Biden Administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would have mentioned it… If anybody did that to us and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me. Nobody’s going to play games with us.” ( Watch ) On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting… If we have a bad President, a weak President, I want a deal that will supersede the President… One way or the other, we’ll finish it off.” ( Watch ) On working with Democrats in the new Congress: “I’ve been called by Democrats at a level that’s pretty amazing. Nobody would even believe it… They want to make deals. I have the veto power… I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years. Because they’ll send me a bill on healthcare, and I’ll say no way, and I’ll veto it, and then they’ll call me… and we’ll sit down.” ( Watch ) On Super Intelligence : “I was with President Xi all night last night, sitting next to him at the dinner, right on his right-hand side, and we spoke the whole evening, and we talked about that, and he’s amazed at how well we’ve done with that. We’re leading China, we’re leading the whole world.” ( Watch ) On reports of an Iranian dirty bomb plot: “There is indication that Iran is looking at gas and they’re looking at the bio — the biological weapons, not nice — and other things, and we’ll see… These are nasty people… Look, if it does happen, we wipe them out.” ( Watch ) On Obama driving China and Russia together: “The relationship should have never been allowed to happen. You know, they were natural enemies, but because of Obama, not Biden, it was Obama before, he drove them together because of energy. … All my life I read you never want to have Russia and China team up… What can I tell you? They both like Trump.” ( Watch ) The post ICYMI: President Trump Talks China, Iran, Super Intelligence, and the Path Ahead in Exclusive Interview from Shenzhen appeared first on The White House .

（中央社記者劉建邦台北24日電）民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋今天被問及有網友提到親友離世前還在拉票，也有住院的99歲阿嬤希望出院投給沈伯洋。沈伯洋說，感受到民主重要性，相信大家想投票的意志會留在世間。
沈伯洋競選團隊上午在中正、萬華區舉辦首場傳統型車掃活動，民進黨台北市黨部主委吳沛憶及中正萬華區議員及議員參選人陪同。沈伯洋在車隊出發前接受聯訪時做出以上回應。
媒體提問時提到，「小水滴」透過網路積極拉票，有網友提到住院中的99歲阿嬤希望投票當天出院才能投給沈伯洋，也有網友分享親友離世前還在幫沈拉票。
沈伯洋回應，看到阿嬤因身體狀況住院仍一直想投票，讓大家知道每票都是如此重要，就像昨天在內湖1名支持者提到朋友生前還在幫他拉票，他有寫一段話給對方。
沈伯洋說，「人生當然會有很多遺憾，但大家想要投票的意志，相信也都會留在這個世間，讓大家感受到民主的重量和重要性」，希望大家不要放棄手中選票，「不管支持誰，28日一起出來投票」。
此外，媒體詢問有關夏莉絲幼兒園不當對待案家長在社群平台發文的看法。沈伯洋指出，如他之前提到，明明一件事能快速被處理卻拖拖拉拉，直到議題已燒成如此，還在選前時才開始有進度。
沈伯洋表示，沒人希望市政都要等選前才能被討論或被解決，他非常能感受到此案父母的擔憂及立場，希望不管最後此案結果如何，他會一直陪伴家屬到最後階段，確保孩童在台北市是能夠被保護。（編輯：蕭博文）1151124

zh_title: 神秘的MQ-25类似黄貂鱼的中国无人机出现在鲜为人知的飞行测试中心
summary: 卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的宽视野卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日位于浦城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初在浦城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现后引起了人们的关注。
content:
卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的一张广角卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初引起了人们的关注，因为它在中国西北部陕西省蒲城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现，可通过苹果地图查看。无人机出现在跑道上的单独图像也可以通过必应地图获得。 TWZ 随后从 Vantor 获得了浦城的图像，显​​示了相关无人驾驶飞机。真是一个惊喜！苹果地图上发现三架无人机出现在蒲城。 CH-7、九天和类似MQ-25的无人机。 pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 18 日再次出现在 bing 地图上！这次它出现在跑道上 pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 除了不明飞行器之外，今年 4 月从蒲城拍摄的图像还揭示了似乎是 CH-7 隐形飞翼无人机和重型喷气动力九天母舰无人机的例子。 2026 年 4 月 23 日，一架 CH-7 停泊在蒲城。
卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的九天无人机母舰。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 与不明飞行器最明显的比较是波音的 MQ-25 Stingray。 MQ-25是一种舰载无人飞机，主要为美国海军飞机提供空中加油，扩大舰载机联队的航程和操作灵活性。它还为未来无人海军航空能力奠定了基础。范托称，就尺寸而言，这架身份不明的中国无人机翼展约为66英尺，长度为49英尺。相比之下，MQ-25 的翼展约为 75 英尺，长度约为 51 英尺。 MQ-25 黄貂鱼。波音公司的这款中国无人机似乎具有相似的总体设计类别，但现阶段存在一些值得注意的重要差异。最引人注目的之一是前机身。与MQ-25不同，MQ-25的前部具有相对扁平的铲状外观，中国飞机似乎有一个更传统的锥形机头。也许这可以包含一个容纳雷达设备的锥形天线罩。这个理论，而且它只是一个理论，可以通过机头与黄色底漆机身的不同颜色来支持。进气量也不同。
与 MQ-25 相关的异国情调的齐平进气道不同，中国设计有一个更传统的背部进气道，看起来呈锯齿状，有助于雷达信号和/或分成两个通道。另一种可能性是飞机有两个发动机，尽管基于明显的分叉进气道，这仍然是推测性的。左侧浦城图像中的无人机和 MQ-25 的并排视图，提供了它们入口的比较视图。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor/Boeing 尾部配置也可能很独特，具有横向展开的 V 型尾翼，如 MQ-25，但可能采用可见控制面，而不是全移动水平尾翼设计。综合起来，这些功能

【原文 English Original】
Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center appeared first on TWZ .
