title: Ground View Pakistan: The smelter before the mine
zh_title: 巴基斯坦地面景观：矿井前的冶炼厂
summary: 在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。 “在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区
content:
在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。谢里夫说：“在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区。”这一举措反映出巴基斯坦希望从矿产财富中获取更多就业机会、技能和出口收入。但由于只有山达克 (Saindak) 一家铜矿生产厂，其旗舰 Reko Diq 项目仍在等待商业生产，该国面临着更紧迫的挑战：在投入数十亿美元建设加工基础设施之前建立可靠的矿山产出。巴基斯坦联邦规划、发展和特别倡议部长阿赫桑·伊克巴尔表示，政府现在要求投资者提交完整的价值链提案，而不是仅仅关注开采和原材料出口的计划。这一要求给探险家带来了特殊的挑战。铜冶炼厂是围绕特定精矿设计的，包括其品位、杂质和预期产量。
如果没有明确的矿产资源和可靠的生产，开发商就无法做出贷款人要求的原料承诺。Milbank 律师事务所能源和基础设施合伙人穆尼布·侯赛因 (Munib Hussain) 表示，合同原料是此类项目融资的主要要求之一。区别很重要。 2025 年 4 月，我认为仅靠采矿并不能实现关键的矿产独立性，因此应优先考虑对加工的投资。这一论点涉及美国，美国现有的矿藏和数十年的生产为下游投资奠定了基础。巴基斯坦正处于早期阶段，全球铜市场呈现出不同的经济现实。冶炼经济 随着中国的新设施与印度、中亚和非洲不断扩大的业务展开竞争，铜冶炼厂正面临产能过剩的困境。处理和精炼费用方面的压力显而易见，矿工向冶炼厂支付费用，将精矿转化为精炼金属。安托法加斯塔和中国冶炼厂同意 2026 年基准为每吨 0 美元和每磅 0 美分，低于 2025 年每吨 21.25 美元和前一年的 80 美元。现货费用已降至零以下，标准普尔全球普氏能源资讯 (S&P Global Platts) 1 月份的评估值为每吨负 47.40 美元。这些负费用意味着加工商实际上正在向矿工支付费用以确保精矿。
Wood Mackenzie 副总裁兼金属和采矿咨询主管帕特里克·巴恩斯 (Patrick Barnes) 在论坛上表示：“现在是建设冶炼厂的非常艰难的时期。”印度说明了其中的商业风险。阿达尼 (Adani) 价值 12 亿美元的卡奇铜冶炼厂每年需要约 160 万吨精矿才能满负荷运营。彭博社报道的进口记录显示，该公司在 2024 年 2 月至 2026 年 2 月期间获得了所需原料的四分之一以上。有关高杂质精矿相关运营不稳定的报道加剧了人们的担忧，尽管阿达尼对这些说法提出了异议。在其他地方，嘉能可关闭了位于菲尔州的帕萨尔冶炼厂

【原文 English Original】
Pakistan’s ambition to build a domestic copper processing industry risks putting smelters ahead of mines at a time when global refining capacity already exceeds available concentrate supplies.  Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reinforced that ambition at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad, pledging to end exports of unprocessed minerals and calling for Reko Diq and other projects in the southwest to support refineries, smelters and factories producing cables and conductors.  “Mine in Pakistan, process in Pakistan, manufacture in Pakistan and then export to the rest of the world,” Sharif said.  The push reflects a desire to capture more jobs, skills and export revenue from Pakistan’s mineral wealth. But with only one producing copper operation, at Saindak, and its flagship Reko Diq project still awaiting commercial production, the country faces a more immediate challenge: establishing reliable mine output before committing billions to processing infrastructure.  Ahsan Iqbal, Pakistan’s federal minister of planning, development and special initiatives, said the government now asks investors to submit complete value-chain proposals rather than plans focused solely on extraction and raw-material exports.  That requirement creates a particular challenge for explorers. Copper smelters are designed around specific concentrates, including their grades, impurities and expected volumes. Without defined mineral resources and dependable production, developers cannot establish the feedstock commitments lenders require.  Munib Hussain, an energy and infrastructure partner at law firm Milbank, said contracted feedstock ranks among the principal requirements for financing such projects.  The distinction is important. In April 2025, I argued that mining alone would not deliver critical minerals independence and that investment in processing should take priority.  That argument concerned the United States, where established mineral deposits and decades of production provided a foundation for downstream investment. Pakistan is at an earlier stage, and the global copper market presents a different economic reality.  Smelting economics  Copper smelters are struggling with excess capacity as new facilities in China compete with expanding operations in India, Central Asia and Africa.  The pressure is evident in treatment and refining charges, which miners pay smelters to convert concentrate into refined metal.  Antofagasta and Chinese smelters agreed to a 2026 benchmark of $0 per tonne and zero cents per pound, down from $21.25 per tonne in 2025 and $80 the previous year. Spot charges have fallen below zero, with S&P Global Platts assessing them at minus $47.40 per tonne in January.  Those negative charges mean processors are effectively paying miners to secure concentrate.  “It’s a very tough time to build a smelter,” Patrick Barnes, vice-president and head of metals and mining consulting at Wood Mackenzie, said at the forum.  India illustrates the commercial risks. Adani’s $1.2-billion Kutch Copper smelter requires approximately 1.6 million tonnes of concentrate annually to operate at full capacity. Import records reported by Bloomberg indicate it secured just over a quarter of its required feedstock between February 2024 and February 2026.  Reports of operating instability linked to high-impurity concentrate have added to concerns, although Adani has disputed those accounts.  Elsewhere, Glencore has closed its Pasar smelter in the Philippines, while Australia has intervened to support the Mount Isa smelter in Queensland.  Even countries that have developed mines before building processing facilities remain exposed to supply disruptions.  Indonesia delayed its copper concentrate export restrictions until production at Grasberg, one of the world’s largest copper mines, could adequately supply domestic smelters. Freeport also had to demonstrate that sufficient concentrate had been reserved for its Manyar facility.  But a September 2025 mud rush at Grasberg forced Freeport to declare force majeure, leaving Indonesian processors short of material.  For Pakistan, these examples strengthen the commercial case for Reko Diq’s existing development plan.  The project is designed to export copper concentrate by rail to Port Qasim for shipment through the Pakistan International Bulk Terminal. Although that approach falls short of the government’s downstream ambitions, it positions Pakistan to benefit from the current shortage of concentrate rather than compete in an oversupplied smelting market.  Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said Reko Diq’s first year of commercial production had been expected to generate $2.8 billion in exports, equivalent to roughly 10% of Pakistan’s current goods exports.  For an economy repeatedly constrained by balance-of-payments crises, that potential foreign exchange revenue is significant.  The opportunity also extends to Western supply chains. American and allied processors need dependable mineral supplies, making Pakistan’s emerging mining industry potentially more valuable as a concentrate exporter than as another entrant into copper smelting.  Domestic processing could still make economic sense for smaller, specialized operations targeting minerals with genuine refining bottlenecks and committed buyers. Antimony is one example, with at least one Pakistani processor pursuing refining capacity linked to prospective US offtake.  Exploration incentives  Pakistan’s taxation policies present another obstacle to establishing the mining industry needed to support future processing.  Waleed Ahmed Vohra, founder and chief executive of Pakistani explorer Ark Metals, said customs duties and taxes consume close to 30% of his exploration budget because the emerging industry depends heavily on imported equipment and foreign technical services.  “I really feel bad when I have to raise a hundred dollars and give 30 dollars to the government,” Vohra said.  Rather than seeking permanent exemptions, he proposes deferring those obligations until commercial production begins, allowing companies to invest more capital in exploration while preserving the government’s eventual tax revenue.  “Defer now to prosper tomorrow,” he said.  Aurangzeb acknowledged the industry’s concerns and said the government would consider changes to taxation and other policies, particularly measures supporting exporters. He pointed to the removal of super taxes in this year’s budget.  But he also emphasized Pakistan’s limited fiscal flexibility, warning that a tax-to-GDP ratio below 10% would be unsustainable. The country has only recently moved into double digits.  That creates a policy dilemma. Export-oriented tax relief provides little immediate benefit to explorers that may spend years defining deposits before generating revenue.  Deferral could bridge that gap without permanently eliminating government receipts, although it would postpone collections and leave the treasury exposed if projects never reach production.  Current incentives nevertheless favour processing.  At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif announced the province’s first dedicated mineral processing zone at an industrial estate in Khushab, offering industrial land at nominal rent for 15 years alongside customs duty concessions.  Federal relief for explorers, including a reported 30-year sales tax exemption covering exploration and development, remains under consideration.  The contrast is striking: processing investors are receiving concrete incentives while explorers are still seeking comparable support.  Government officials appear increasingly aware of the sequencing challenge. Barnes said discussions at the forum showed that policymakers had carefully examined the conditions necessary to make domestic smelting commercially viable.  “They understand that until there’s a mining industry here, smelting is not really on the table,” he said. “If they get two, three, four mines that are producing, options start to open up for them.”  Pakistan does not need to abandon its processing ambitions. It needs to distinguish between commodities where domestic refining addresses a genuine supply-chain shortage and copper, where existing smelters are already competing for scarce material.  The immediate priority is to make exploration more attractive, establish dependable production and build an export industry capable of financing future downstream investment.  A domestic copper smelter may eventually make sense. Its economic justification will be stronger once Pakistan has several producing mines and the concentrate supply to sustain it.  For now, the furnace can wait for the rock.  * Erik Groves is a contributing analyst for MINING.COM and Corporate Strategy and In-House Counsel at Morgan Companies. He will attend and provide coverage of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad on November 12 and 13. zh_title: 精心策划东山再起：俄罗斯的非洲政策对欧洲意味着什么
summary: 2026 年 10 月 29 日星期四，领导人在莫斯科举行的俄罗斯-非洲峰会期间合影留念。（Anastasia Barashkova//美联社泳池照片）|图片联盟/Anastasia Barashkova/Pool 路透社来自美联社 |阿纳斯塔西娅·巴拉什科娃 (Anastasia Barashkova) 十月下旬，非洲领导人抵达莫斯科，参加第三次俄罗斯-非洲峰会以及看似无休无止的外交会议。传达的信息很明确：俄罗斯希望恢复与非洲的接触。克里姆林宫试图将俄罗斯描绘成一个重返非洲大陆的全球大国，继承了苏联支持非洲反殖民主义的遗产。
content:
2026 年 10 月 29 日星期四，领导人在莫斯科举行的俄罗斯-非洲峰会期间合影留念。（Anastasia Barashkova//美联社泳池照片）|图片联盟/Anastasia Barashkova/Pool 路透社来自美联社 |阿纳斯塔西娅·巴拉什科娃 (Anastasia Barashkova) 十月下旬，非洲领导人抵达莫斯科，参加第三次俄罗斯-非洲峰会以及看似无休无止的外交会议。传达的信息很明确：俄罗斯希望恢复与非洲的接触。克里姆林宫试图将俄罗斯描绘成一个重返非洲大陆的全球大国，继承了苏联支持非洲反殖民运动的遗产。在 11 月 19 日与习近平和唐纳德·特朗普会面之前，弗拉基米尔·普京还利用这次峰会推进了另一个地缘政治野心：让俄罗斯拥有与苏联曾经享有的相同的全球地位。普京正在寻找一个“新雅尔塔”，在这个新雅尔塔中，他可以以斯大林的角色与另外两个大国就势力范围进行讨价还价。俄罗斯接待非洲领导人，普京在最近的公开露面中看似不经意地提及苏联在国际关系中的作用，以及他的大规模宣传工作，都反映出总统试图将自己描绘成一位有权重新绘制世界政治版图的政治家。然而，尽管莫斯科声称自己具有独特性，但“非洲+1”峰会却是司空见惯的。
欧洲各国政府以及亚洲和中东地区的其他大国经常召开类似的集会来讨好非洲大陆。为了加强其在非洲的地位，欧洲人应该更加直言不讳地表达自己的利益，并为非洲国家提供俄罗斯以外的替代方案。莫斯科扩大其非洲官僚机构 2023 年举行的第二次俄罗斯-非洲峰会因给非洲带来的好处甚少而受到批评。普京的回应是责成众多俄罗斯政府机构和国家支持的行动者与非洲建立更牢固的关系。到 2026 年，这些努力除其他外，已召开了两次部长级会议，旨在加强政府机构之间的联系；在外交部设立新的非洲伙伴关系司；以及统一俄罗斯党的“为了民族自由！”运动和议会倡议将俄罗斯和非洲政党纳入更广泛的反殖民网络。克里姆林宫还举办青年聚会和媒体论坛，以宣传俄罗斯对全球秩序的看法。这些举措与俄罗斯在非洲的军事存在并存，后者仍然是俄罗斯在非洲大陆最重要的影响力来源。然而，乌克兰战争暴露了莫斯科经济和金融资源的局限性。尽管非洲国家正在根据国家发展目标实现伙伴关系多元化，但普京未能实现他在 2019 年设定的五年内与非洲贸易额翻番至 400 亿美元左右的目标。
他现在的目标是到 2030 年达到 500 亿美元。到 2025 年，俄罗斯与非洲的货物贸易总额将达到 270 亿美元，大致相当于其与哈萨克斯坦的贸易额，而欧盟与非洲的货物贸易额则达到 3560 亿欧元。而且，俄罗斯在非洲外国直接投资流入存量中所占比例不足1%，远远落后于中国、美国和欧盟。农业提供了更多有形收益。 2026年上半年，俄罗斯对非洲的农产品出口额达到29亿美元，比2025年同期增长35%。然而，俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争正在扰乱乌克兰的粮食出口。这与寻求可靠供应返回的非洲政府产生了摩擦

【原文 English Original】
Leaders pose for a family photo during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Anastasia Barashkova//Pool Photo via AP) | picture alliance / Anastasia Barashkova/Pool Reuters via AP | Anastasia Barashkova In late October, African leaders arrived in Moscow for the third Russia-Africa summit and a seemingly endless procession of diplomatic meetings. The message was clear: Russia wants to renew its engagement with Africa. The Kremlin seeks to portray Russia as a global power returning to the African continent, carrying the Soviet legacy of support for Africa’s anti-colonial movements. Vladimir Putin also used the summit to advance another geopolitical ambition ahead of the November 19th meeting with Xi Jinping and Donald Trump: for Russia to have the same global standing once enjoyed by the Soviet Union. Putin is searching for a “new Yalta” in which he, in Stalin’s role, can bargain with two other great powers over spheres of influence. Russia’s hosting of African leaders and Putin’s seemingly offhand references to the Soviet Union’s role in international relations during recent public appearances, as well as his massive publicity efforts , reflect the president’s attempt to portray himself as a statesman with the authority to redraw the world’s political map. For all Moscow’s claims of uniqueness , however, “Africa+1” summits are commonplace. European governments and other powers across Asia and the Middle East often convene similar gatherings to court the continent. To strengthen their standing in Africa, Europeans should be more vocal about their interests and offer African countries an alternative to Russia. Moscow expands its Africa bureaucracy The second Russia-Africa summit in 2023 drew criticism for delivering little benefit to Africa. Putin responded by tasking numerous Russian government agencies and state-backed actors to build stronger ties with Africa. By 2026 these efforts had amounted, among other things, to two ministerial conferences that aimed to strengthen ties between government agencies; the establishment of a new Department for Partnership with Africa in the foreign ministry; and United Russia’s “ For the Freedom of Nations!” movement and parliamentary initiatives to bring Russian and African parties into a wider anti-colonial network. The Kremlin also hosted youth gatherings and media forums to promote Russia’s view of the global order . These initiatives sit alongside Russia’s military presence in Africa, which remains its most consequential source of influence on the continent. However, the war in Ukraine has exposed the limits of Moscow’s economic and financial resources. While African countries are diversifying their partnerships based on national development objectives, Putin missed the target he set in 2019 to double trade with Africa to around $40bn in five years. He is now aiming for $50bn by 2030. Russia’s goods trade with Africa totalled $27bn in 2025, roughly matching its trade with Kazakhstan , while EU-Africa goods trade reached €356bn . Moreover, Russia accounts for less than 1% of Africa’s inward foreign direct investment stock, far behind China, the US and the EU . Agriculture offers more tangible gains. Russian agricultural exports to Africa reached $2.9bn in the first half of 2026, up 35% in value on the same period in 2025. However, Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting Ukrainian grain exports. This creates friction with African governments seeking the return of reliable supplies via the Black Sea. From trade to sovereignty Moscow has limited prospects of competing economically on the African continent. It is therefore increasingly framing partnerships with African countries ideologically while simultaneously pursuing more pragmatic cooperation in selected sectors, such as technology and agriculture. Putin’s speeches, final declarations and business programmes at the 2019, 2023 and 2026 Russia-Africa summits demonstrate this attempt. Putin’s references to military security and terrorism fell even more sharply in his speeches and almost halved in the final declarations. By 2026, references to sovereignty had gained prominence in both programmes and declarations, highlighting the core of Russia’s Africa strategy and tapping into existing anti- French and European sentiment , especially in West Africa. Putin is also placing greater emphasis on colonialism and multipolarity, grounding Russia’s claim to relevance in its vision of a multipolar world , of which the Kremlin is a champion. Russia is also drawing institutions such as universities and media organisations into its Africa policy, tasking them with facilitating cultural cooperation between Russia and Africa. Such organisations can form part of Russia’s wider disinformation campaigns. Between 2019 and 2026, Putin’s speeches nearly doubled their references to education and the Russian language, while the business programmes used them almost twice as often. The use of information-related terms, such as “media” and “informational agenda”, also more than doubled, largely through new media-forum sessions bringing together Russian and African journalists and media executives as a separate part of the third summit. Russia’s more selective and pragmatic agenda also includes energy, which regained prominence in the programmes and declarations between 2023 and 2026, drawing on Russia’s expertise in nuclear power . And, as part of Russia’s drive for pragmatic cooperation, the country also pursues seemingly uncontroversial themes such as its 2026 declaration on civilian AI . However, this offers African partners little immediate help. Many have more pressing industrial and economic needs. Pendulum partnership African governments choose partners pragmatically, based on their ability to deliver socio-economic growth, industrialisation and job creation Moscow’s bureaucratic expansion and stronger ideological approach are struggling to resonate with its potential partners in Africa. African governments choose partners pragmatically, based on their ability to deliver socio-economic growth, industrialisation and job creation. Even so, most of Moscow’s core partnerships in Africa continue to rest on security cooperation. For example, Russia has deployed forces in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, and in the Central African Republic (CAR), Libya and Equatorial Guinea. It has also formalised defence cooperation with Togo and continues to pursue a military base in Sudan. The share of African speakers from these eight states at the three Russia-Africa summits rose from 5% in 2019 to 23% in 2026. Speakers from Russia’s BRICS+ partners, Egypt and Ethiopia, brought this up to 30% in 2026. Elsewhere, some African countries’ ties with Moscow fluctuate depending on changes of government and their renewed attempts to diversify partnerships. Ghana’s president John Mahama led his country’s 2026 summit delegation, which saw six Ghanaian speakers in the business programme. Russia and Ghana also reached an agreement on bauxite mining and alumina refining, and Russia has committed to help develop Ghana’s first nuclear power plant. Yet, despite Mahama’s ties to Russia (he studied in the Soviet Union), the speech data show that Ghana retains a pragmatic approach. Mahama’s renewed engagement with Russia perhaps reflects a search for partnerships that best serve Ghana’s national interests. Putin used ideological vocabulary more than twice as often in 2026 as in 2019, while his use of economic terms remained largely static. Among Moscow’s security partners, ideological language held roughly steady between 2023 and 2026, while references to trade, energy and investment doubled. Egypt’s emphasis changed little. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi used ideological terms as often as Putin in 2019, but by 2026 Putin used them 75% more often than Sisi. African leaders outside the core group of eight security partners plus Egypt and Ethiopia used ideological terms 25% less frequently between 2023 and 2026, while the use of pragmatic vocabulary rose by more than a third. Some countries are scaling back their cooperation with Russia amid limited economic returns and tensions over the war in Ukraine. For example, in 2026, South Africa sent its foreign ministry’s director-general and Nigeria a junior foreign minister , replacing the presidents who attended in 2019. Their business programme speaker counts fell from 14 to five and from seven to three, respectively. An opening for Europe Insights from confidential conversations between ECFR’s Africa programme and African policymakers suggest that the continent’s governments and leaders appreciate a more pragmatic approach from European partners. This involves Europeans acknowledging the legacy of European colonialism in Africa, but also realising that in a fragmented global order Africa has options to choose from. Europe would benefit from identifying where Russian political actors are working at cross-purposes and leveraging this fragmentation in diplomatic negotiations with African partners. For example, the former Wagner chief Yevgeny Prigozhin welcomed the Niger coup in 2023, while Russia’s foreign ministry backed ECOWAS in restoring constitutional order. In the CAR, his son Pavel Prigozhin has held on to Wagner’s operations despite the Russian defence ministry’s efforts to absorb them. As Moscow gives its bureaucratic players a bigger role in Africa, such tensions are likely to grow. The Russia-Africa Action Plan for 2027-2029 contains 236 measures, including joint drone, fertiliser and vaccine production, and cooperation between the African Union and the Russia-led Collective Security Treaty Organisation. But these priorities, and Russia’s bilateral agreements with African countries, can undermine one another: Rosatom requires deep cooperation with Accra to develop the planned nuclear power plant in Ghana, for example, but Russia’s coercive recruitment of Ghanaians for its war against Ukraine risks eroding bilateral trust. Even Mahama, who praised Moscow’s support for Africa’s anti-colonial struggles, has challenged Putin over the practice . Where Moscow’s competing interests undermine its summit promises, Europe can build trust by backing projects that African partners themselves prioritise. An example is the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), for which the EU provided technical and financial support. Despite facing some difficulties, the AfCFTA highlights where European and African strategic interests align—and where Europeans can help Africans reach their objectives, without setting the terms. Europeans also need to understand that, for African partners, pursuing a narrative in which Europe “counters” other actors such as Russia may not land well. Although Africa has considerable growth and market potential, the continent does not want to be approached as an international bargaining field. European governments should instead sharpen their own offer and advance investments in areas such as education and training, technology and engineering. Forums such as the AU-EU Senior Officials Meeting in Addis Ababa are essential for Europe to stay aligned with African priorities, while the participation of high-level European leaders, such as German president Frank-Walter Steinmeier at the upcoming German-African Business Summit in Ghana, signals how seriously they take cooperation. * African partners are not going to wait for European countries to take more responsibility in their approach to economic and trade negotiations. Europeans must ground any partnerships with African countries in reliability—a quality that Russian cooperation has yet to achieve. Both Europe and Africa share a strong belief in multilateralism, political dialogue and collective action. This dialogue, if transformed into a pragmatic, well-coordinated approach , would set Europeans apart from the transactional and extractive approaches of other global players. Source

三边会谈 + 气候呼吁 + 间谍事件 Linda_Heyer Thu, 11/19/2026 - 14:46 picture league / Win McNamee/Pool Getty Images AsiaPac via AP Download (pdf - 720.16 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Nov 19, 2026 11 分钟阅读 三边会谈 + 气候呼吁 + 间谍事件 头条新闻 普京习近平按自己的方式主持峰会，特朗普成为众人瞩目的焦点 美中俄深圳峰会对俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京来说是一次外交胜利，但习近平成为了更大的赢家，他成功主持了一场可能让中国在深圳举办的亚太经合组织峰会黯然失色的会议。对于因俄罗斯近五年的侵略乌克兰战争而被西方孤立的普京来说，这次会议提供了一个轻松的机会来展现一位在国际外交最高层仍然受欢迎的领导人的形象。对习近平来说，中国对两位不可预测的客人的精心舞台管理得到了回报，峰会既没有像莫斯科所希望的那样就乌克兰问题达成“雅尔塔式”协议，也没有像美国总统唐纳德·特朗普所建议的那样让北京参与削减核武器谈判。
根据俄罗斯政府会后发布的联合声明，三位领导人确实同意“就减少核风险和防止核扩散进行对话”，但这不应损害北京的既定立场，即美国和俄罗斯必须在中国加入任何谈判之前大幅削减其更庞大的核武库。习近平、普京和特朗普还承诺改革联合国，并同意增加石油产量。也许对维护基于规则的国际秩序的西方国家来说最痛苦的是，该声明还表示，国家官员的豁免权是“根本性的”，国际刑事法院不得滥用其权力，该法院于 2023 年对普京发出了逮捕令。后一点将加剧欧洲的担忧，即美国总统在几个问题上与北京和莫斯科更加一致。但乌克兰的未来并未出现在官方结论中，这一事实使欧洲免于陷入更糟糕的境地。在莫斯科本身提高了对三边会议的期望后，普京似乎急于挽回乌克兰问题上缺乏进展的面子，并强调他已与习近平和特朗普分别讨论了这场战争。深圳的情况也没有暗示平等国家的新“G3”。在他们第 50 次面对面会面时，习近平再次称普京为“老朋友”，但没有像接待特朗普那样到机场接待他。
周四，习近平与特朗普的双边会晤和午餐会持续了很长时间，以至于普京不得不等待三边会议开始。“最重要的事情可能是三边会议最终举行了。习近平让普京得到了他所寻求的关注，同时为特朗普保留了红地毯待遇。通过这样做，他成功地举办了一场可能有风险的会议。”  伊娃·塞沃特 (Eva Seiwert)，MERICS 高级分析师 更多相关主题：为什么习近平可能有自己的理由避免美俄中峰会 – MERICS 伊娃·塞沃特 (Eva Seiwert) 的评论 媒体报道和来源：中国外交部（CN）：习近平会见俄罗斯总统普京 BBC：普京称俄罗斯、美国和中国对全球和平负有“共同责任” 路透社：直播：特朗普、习近平和普京举行了前所未有的三边会谈，重点关注乌克兰和核武器METRIX 1,042,590,000,000 这是中国2026年前10个月的贸易顺差，以美元计算。顺差突破1万亿美元三月

Trilateral talks + Climate call-out + Espionage affair Linda_Heyer Thu, 11/19/2026 - 14:46 picture alliance / Win McNamee/Pool Getty Images AsiaPac via AP Download (pdf - 720.16 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Nov 19, 2026 11 min read Trilateral talks + Climate call-out + Espionage affair Top story Putin gets the spotlight and Trump the red carpet as Xi runs the summit on his terms The US-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen was a diplomatic win for Russian President Vladimir Putin, but Xi Jinping emerged as the bigger winner, successfully managing a meeting that risked overshadowing the APEC summit China was hosting in the same city. For Putin, isolated by the West over Russia’s near five-year war of aggression against Ukraine, the meeting offered an easy opportunity to project the image of a leader still welcome at the highest level of international diplomacy. For Xi, China’s careful stage management of two unpredictable guests paid off, with the summit neither producing a “Yalta-style” agreement on Ukraine, as Moscow had favored, nor binding Beijing into nuclear-arms reduction talks, as US President Donald Trump had suggested.  The three leaders did agree to “engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation,” according to a joint statement released by the Russian government after the meeting, but this should not undermine Beijing’s established position that the US and Russia must make substantial reductions to their much larger arsenals before China joins any talks. Xi, Putin and Trump also committed to reforming the UN and agreed to increase oil production. Perhaps most painfully for Western countries that uphold the rules-based international order, the statement also said immunity for state officials was “fundamental” and that the International Criminal Court, which issued an arrest warrant for Putin in 2023, must not abuse its authority.  This latter point will reinforce European concerns that the US president is more aligned with Beijing and Moscow on several issues. But the fact that the future of Ukraine did not feature in the official conclusions spared Europe from worse. After Moscow itself had raised expectations for the trilateral, Putin appeared keen to save face over this lack of progress on Ukraine, stressing that he had discussed the war separately with Xi and Trump. The optics in Shenzhen also did not suggest a new “G3” of equal countries.  Xi once again called Putin his “old friend” at what was their 50th in-person meeting, but did not receive him at the airport as he did Trump. Xi’s bilateral meeting and lunch with Trump on Thursday ran so long that Putin was left waiting for the trilateral to begin.  "The most significant thing may have been that the trilateral took place at all. Xi gave Putin the spotlight he sought, while reserving the red-carpet treatment for Trump. In doing so, he successfully managed a potentially risky meeting.”  Eva Seiwert , Senior Analyst, MERICS More on the topic: Why Xi may have his own reasons to avert a US-Russia-China summit – MERICS Comment by Eva Seiwert Media coverage and sources: Chinese MFA (CN): 习近平会见俄罗斯总统普京   BBC: Putin says Russia, US, and China share 'joint responsibility' for global peace Reuters: Live: Trump, Xi and Putin hold unprecedented trilateral talks, with Ukraine and nuclear arms in focus METRIX 1,042,590,000,000 This is China’s trade surplus in the first ten months of 2026, in US dollars. The surplus broke the USD 1 trillion mark in October, one month earlier than in 2025, putting it on track to exceed last year’s record annual surplus of USD 1.2 trillion. A surge in foreign demand for electric vehicles, technology and AI-related products has seen exports outpace imports, even though the latter are themselves growing rapidly. Exports of computer parts were up 235 percent, those of semiconductors up 110.8 percent, and those of vehicles up 52.2 percent. (Source: General Administration of Customs )  GRAPHIC OF THE WEEK China exported 41 billion USD more goods to Germany between January and October 2026 than it imported from Europe’s largest economy – almost twice the trade surplus recorded in the same period last year. As the latest issue of the SOAPBOX newsletter on China reported, citing Chinese customs data, this increase accounted for nearly one third of the 69 billion USD increase in China’s trade surplus with the EU as a whole.  China’s surplus with Germany grew almost five times as fast as the 22 percent rise in its surplus with the rest of the EU, which reached USD 270 billion. This highlights Germany’s deep economic ties with China – and its resulting exposure to Chinese competition. As China sells more higher-value products abroad and increasingly sources components domestically, Germany faces a big double squeeze: rising imports and falling exports.  SOAPBOX is a weekly newsletter on EU-China trade relations compiled by Rafael Buendia Jimenez and Ilaria Perla. You can subscribe to the newsletter for free here . TOPICS China uses COP31 to showcase Europe’s dilemma on climate and trade China’s clear position at November’s UN climate change conference in Türkiye stood in stark contrast to Europe’s growing dilemma between its climate ambitions, defensive trade policy toward China and growing reluctance to commit more financing for developing countries dealing with global warming.  Before COP 31, Beijing had emphasized the need to discuss “old issues” of insufficient climate financing and “new challenges” of unilateralism and protectionism, which were harming “collective efforts to address climate change.” But in the end, it was the African Group that proposed putting climate-related trade and climate finance on the agenda. Their contention that Europe’s additional levy on carbon-intensive imports is unfair to Africa reinforced China's argument that European protectionism is undermining global climate cooperation. The EU objected to these proposals, which included the tripling of finance pledges, but did not block the Climate Finance Work Programme – a process to work out how developed countries meet their climate finance obligations to developing nations – as a separate agenda item.  The bloc is under pressure to fill a US-sized financing gap after US President Donald Trump’s withdrawal from the Paris agreement. Domestic opposition to a larger pledge is growing, as the EU is already one of the largest donors worldwide. Europe’s reluctance to step up, together with a lack of high-level European leaders at the conference stands in a stark contrast to China’s dominant cleantech offer to the world.  "The EU faces a dilemma: decarbonization is needed to fight climate change, but Chinese cleantech dominance and exports to the EU are a geoeconomics challenge. As the EU grapples with this, China’s proposed solution – more Chinese cleantech and more climate funding from developed countries – is gaining momentum.” Johanna Krebs , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources : Xinhua (CN): 以“双碳”为牵引加快全面绿色转型——生态环境部介绍我国应对气候变化工作成效 Down to Earth: COP31 Adopts Climate Finance Work Programme Amid Tensions Over Adaptation Funding and Trade Carbon Brief: COP31: Agenda adopted! - Conversations / Policy   Carbon Brief: Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit Euronews: ‘More than just a photo opportunity’: Why are key EU leaders skipping the COP31 Leaders’ Summit? Nvidia’s espionage drama could backfire on Chinese AI ambitions Revelations that the chief executive of US chipmaker Nvidia, Jensen Huang, had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy could deal another blow to China’s AI industry, which is already grappling with an economic slowdown and Beijing’s push for labs to switch to less powerful domestic hardware such as chips designed by Huawei. The US government is openly split between advocates of continued commercial engagement and national-security hawks who want to cut off Chinese access to US AI technology. But pressure from lawmakers in Washington for tighter controls is mounting – and Congress could ultimately override any presidential veto of legislation covering foreign trade. China’s AI stocks, already caught in China’s broader market correction, have slumped again. Huang has not just been Nvidia’s guiding light since co-founding the company in 1993, but he also successfully lobbied US officials, including President Donald Trump, over the last two years to relax chip export controls. US lawmakers now want to crack down on smuggling networks that supply China with the most advanced US-designed AI chips and on schemes that give Chinese companies remote cloud access to powerful chips via data centers located in third countries. The Commerce Department will also soon require companies to obtain licenses for advanced semiconductor exports, re-exports and transfers to data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Data centers anywhere in the world will need permission to service Chinese companies.  "China's AI future is deeply tied to policy decisions made in Washington, which the networks and choices of a few tech CEOs can shape in fundamental ways. Huang was one of the most influential advocates of maintaining the flow of US AI chips to China. But the espionage allegations will make that position much harder to defend – and leave China’s AI industry with even fewer options.” Rebecca Arcesati , Head of Program (Co-Lead) Science, Technology and Innovation, MERICS Media coverage and sources: The New York Times: The Fall of Jensen Huang Reuters: US to curb China's access to AI chips as Trump heads to Asia Bloomberg: Nvidia Stops Selling AI chips to China Despite US Approval Xi tightens his grip on local party committees – in good time for a fourth term Xi Jinping’s third term as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) ends in the second half of 2027, but it looks like he is not going anywhere. The CCP’s Central Committee on November 7, 2026, issued revised regulations on the work of local party committees for the first time since 2015. The new rules are meant to improve decision-making by cadres in provinces, cities and counties to make sure central directives are implemented. Maintaining a strong chain of command from the center down to the local level is of paramount importance to the CCP’s ability to meet its goals – and to securing Xi’s position at the apex of the party, making a fourth term increasingly likely. Xi and the other then 22 members of the Politburo had announced the review of the regulation in March. They require officials to shoulder “political responsibility” for ensuring that the Central Committee’s policies are effectively implemented. Contradicting the leadership’s directives, engaging in local protectionism, pursuing prestige projects designed to demonstrate political achievements and improperly increasing local government hidden debt are expressly forbidden. Local party committee members are subject to “lifelong accountability” for rule violations and decision-making errors. Although permanent responsibility already applies to environmental and certain major administrative decisions, this is a significant extension of the mechanism. "The ideologies of Marx, Lenin and Mao have been removed from the regulations, while Xi’s status as ‘core leader’ has been codified. His latest instructions and speeches are now the first item on the agenda at local party meetings. Xi wants to put cadres’ feet to the fire and make sure they get the job done the way he wants it. He looks like a leader who expects to keep a close eye on them for a while yet.”  Alexander Davey , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources: SCMP: Communist Party lays down the internal discipline law for local leader s Xinhua (CN): 《 中国共产党地方委员会工作条例 》 (Regulations on the Work of Local Committees of the Chinese Communist Party) Communist Party Member Network (CN): 《 中国共产党地方委员会工作条例 (2015) 》 (Archived version of the previous 2015 regulations) Lianhe Zaobao Singapore (CN): Revised work regulations of local party committees bans "vanity" projects and "prestige" projects China successfully targets rich to boost income-tax revenue China appears to be having considerable success in taxing its richer residents more. Revenues from personal income tax surged 90 percent in October 2026 from a year earlier, after tax authorities in July introduced rules requiring Chinese residents to pay tax on assets transferred into offshore trusts and on income generated by them. Taxpayers – mostly the country’s ultra-rich – had until late October to comply, effectively closing a loophole used to protect assets from the Chinese state. Tax revenue linked to offshore trusts reached CNY 160 billion in the first ten months of 2026, which suggests personal income-tax revenue from January to October 2026 is likely to have already exceeded the 2025 full-year total of CNY 1.62 trillion (about EUR 221 billion).  China’s overall tax revenue has been rising over the past year, spurred in particular by securities trading. But with China’s AI bubble deflating and share prices falling, the additional personal income tax revenue from offshore trusts is a welcome boost to state finances. Personal income tax accounts for only a portion of total tax revenue. At 9 percent, it carries less weight than value-added tax, which accounts for 39 percent of revenues, or corporate income tax, which accounts for 23 percent. But the increased flow of revenues from taxing offshore trust assets and income will provide additional fiscal room by offsetting declines in land-tax and consumption-tax revenue.  “The surge in personal income tax takings is the latest sign of China’s push to expand its tax base and strengthen public revenues. The recent focus on taxing offshore trusts, most of which are owned by high-net-worth individuals, also opens up other opportunities. It allows authorities to exercise greater oversight over capital outflows and potentially redistribute wealth more evenly.” Sophia Pradels , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources: Xinhua (CN): 离岸信托收益征税平稳有序推进 (Offshore Trust Income Taxation Is Progressing Smoothly and Orderly) Yicai: China’s Personal Income Tax Haul Nearly Doubles in October on Offshore Trust Windfall Financial Times: China warns of ‘severe’ punishment for offshore trust tax evaders MERICS CHINA DIGEST China's economy falters as factory output, retail sales undershoot expectations (Reuters) Chinese retail sales grew just 0.4% year-on-year in October, down from 1.1% in September, while industrial production growth slowed to 4.8%.  (26/11/16) China's Singles Day sales rise 4.8% to USD 1.78 trillion; AI takes larger role (Reuters) China's Singles Day shopping generated CNY 1.78 trillion in revenues, but annual sales growth slowed to 4.8% from 14.2% in 2025 despite weeks of promotions. (26/11/12) China’s passenger car sales fall 27% as exports rise 69% (Caixin) Domestic passenger car retail sales fell 27.1% year-on-year in October to 1.64 million vehicles, while exports rose 68.5% to 928,000.  (26/11/10) China's October new bank loans shrink for third time this year (The Standard) New yuan loans fell by CNY 100 billion in October, marking the third monthly contraction this year, the PBOC said in its quarterly monetary policy. title: Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government
zh_title: 艾丽丝·黄与上海商界和政府的不正当关系
summary: 内容摘要：黄仁勋间谍丑闻核心人物、Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 通过上海金融界建立了自己的商业网络。她与因财务不当行为而受到制裁的所谓丈夫康伟和后来涉嫌欺诈和贿赂的谷国平等人物有联系。报道称，美国情报部门认为她是中华人民共和国情报部门的合作伙伴。根据开源研究，目前尚不清楚 Alice Huang 在国家安全部 (MSS) 中的确切角色是什么
content:
内容摘要：黄仁勋间谍丑闻核心人物、Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 通过上海金融界建立了自己的商业网络。她与因财务不当行为而受到制裁的所谓丈夫康伟和后来涉嫌欺诈和贿赂的谷国平等人物有联系。报道称，美国情报部门认为她是中华人民共和国情报部门的合作伙伴。根据开源研究，目前尚不清楚 Alice Huang 在国家安全部 (MSS) 中的确切角色是什么；然而，当她结识黄仁勋时，她的兴趣和事工的兴趣很可能是一致的。黄和康利用他们的游戏业务扩展到半导体和数据中心，并在此过程中成为 Nvidia 的客户。随后，黄仁勋接管了香港游戏公司第七大道在新加坡的国际子公司第七大道国际，并通过马来西亚子公司购买了英伟达芯片。美国当局怀疑这些芯片随后被转运到中国。皇康网络与中国地方政府建立了联系。持有顾国平旗下斐讯公司股份的上海松江区投资机构，在顾国平的犯罪活动导致斐讯公司倒闭后，将股份出售给其网络中的一家公司。
科技巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 联合创始人兼首席执行官 (CEO) 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 垮台的核心人物是一位名叫黄乐 (Huang Le) 的女性，又名 Alice Huang。媒体报道称，黄女士是英伟达在东南亚最大的客户之一、新加坡计算公司 Megaspeed 的前高管，她与黄仁勋有染。 Megaspeed 涉嫌将受美国出口管制限制的 Nvidia 芯片走私到中华人民共和国（PRC）。报道还称，美国情报部门认为黄女士已被中华人民共和国国家安全部 (MSS) 拉拢（《纽约时报》[NYT]，10 月 29 日；《华盛顿邮报》，11 月 15 日）。 [1] 北京很快否认了这些指控，但一些亲美人士认为中国的知识分子则更加持怀疑态度。他们认为当前的丑闻是特朗普政府内部以及特朗普与“深层政府”之间的内讧的结果（腾讯新闻；X/@Wuuesanren；X/@WoodenHarp，11月10日）。一位上海商人在接受采访时也表达了类似的观点，称黄女士的网络采用了复杂的、多层的公司结构来掩盖最终控制者是谁，并称这种策略是“上海滩从同治皇帝时候就玩的东西了”，指的是19世纪下半叶的早期现代化时期（作者访谈，11月10日）。他相信女士。
黄女士的目的只是将芯片走私到中国。黄出身于上海金融界，她与随后被判犯有金融犯罪的人物的关系表明，她的个人资料应该引起更多的危险信号。她的网络以一家投资公司上海和熙投资管理为中心，该公司是由她所谓的恋人、商人康伟创立的（英国《金融时报》，11 月 10 日）。该网络中的其他主要人物包括黄瑜，英国《金融时报》将其描述为黄女士的妹妹；顾国平

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the heart of the Jensen Huang spy scandal, built her business network through the world of Shanghai finance. She is linked to figures such as Kang Wei, her alleged husband who has been sanctioned for financial misconduct, and Gu Guoping, who was later implicated in fraud and bribery. Reporting indicates that U.S. intelligence considers her a cooptee of People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence services. It remains unclear what Alice Huang’s exact role was for the Ministry of State Security (MSS) based on open-source research; however, it is likely that her interests and that of the ministry converged around the time when she became acquainted with Jensen Huang. Huang and Kang used their gaming business to expand into semiconductors and data centers, becoming an Nvidia customer in the process. Huang then took over Hong Kong-based gaming company 7Road’s international subsidiary based in Singapore, 7Road International, and purchased Nvidia chips through a Malaysian affiliate. U.S. authorities suspect the chips were then transshipped to the PRC. The Huang-Kang network cultivated ties with local governments in the PRC. The investment arm of Shanghai’s Songjiang District, which owned a stake in Gu Guoping’s Phicomm, sold the stake to a company in their network after Phicomm failed in the wake of Gu’s criminal activity. At the center of the downfall of Jensen Huang, the co-founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of technology giant Nvidia, is a woman identified as Huang Le (黄乐), also known as Alice Huang. Media reporting alleges that Ms. Huang, a former executive of one of Nvidia’s largest customers in Southeast Asia, the Singapore-based computing company Megaspeed, had an affair with Jensen Huang. Megaspeed has been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips covered by U.S. export control restrictions into the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Reports have also said that U.S. intelligence considered Ms. Huang to have been coopted by the PRC’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) ( New York Times [NYT] , October 29; Washington Post , November 15).  [1] Beijing has been quick to deny these allegations, but some pro-U.S. Chinese intellectuals are more skeptical. They view the current scandal as a consequence of infighting within the Trump administration and between Trump and the “deep state” ( Tencent News ; X/@Wuyuesanren ; X/@WoodenHarp , November 10). In an interview, a Shanghai businessman expressed a similar view, saying that Ms. Huang’s network used an elaborate, multilayered corporate structure to conceal who ultimately controlled it, calling this tactic “the sort of thing Shanghai has been doing since the time of the Tongzhi Emperor” (上海滩从同治皇帝时候就玩的东西了), referring to the period of early modernization in the second half of the 19th century (Author interview, November 10). He believed Ms. Huang’s purpose was simply to smuggle chips into the PRC. Ms. Huang emerged from the world of Shanghai finance, where her connections to figures who have subsequently been found guilty of financial crime suggest that her profile should have raised more red flags. Her network centered on an investment firm, Hexi Investment Management (上海和熙投资管理), which was founded by one her alleged romantic partners, the businessman Kang Wei (康伟) ( Financial Times , November 10). Other major figures in this network include Huang Yu (黄瑜), whom the Financial Times describes as Ms. Huang’s sister; and Gu Guoping (顾国平), the founder of communications company Phicomm (斐讯技术) ( Financial Times , November 10; Caixin , November 10).  [2] Ms. Huang co-founded Shanghai Yunxi (上海韵禧) in 2016, and Huang Yu took over the following year ( The Time Weekly , November 9). (Source: Author’s research) Gaming Served as Gateway to Data Centers For Ms. Huang, as for Nvidia, the gaming industry provided a route into the compute business. PRC game publishers often set up foreign entities to serve overseas markets, providing a legitimate reason to import graphics processors and expand data center capacity. Huang became involved with 7Road Holdings (第七大道), a Hong Kong-listed game developer, after it had acquired a portfolio of gaming businesses held by an entity wholly owned by her and registered in the British Virgin Islands ( Caizhongshe , November 11). A circular announcing the acquisition identified a company owned by Kang Wei, Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), as a “party acting in concert” (一致行动人) with Ms. Huang. It also listed among the portfolio’s operating entities in the PRC a company previously owned by a subsidiary of Century Huatong (世紀華通), another firm with ties to Kang and Huang ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [3] With Ms. Huang now behind the scenes, Yunxi expanded her business network into the semiconductor and data center industries through cooperation with 7Road starting in 2022. A 7Road subsidiary committed renminbi (RMB) 330 million ($49 million) to a limited partnership managed by Yunxi whose sole asset was a 5.29 percent stake in a Shanghai-based semiconductor wafer manufacturer ( Hong Kong Exchange , May 24, 2022). 7Road also expanded into the data center and cloud computing businesses in 2019, offering cloud services for gaming and the possibility of third-party data center services in a cooperation framework ( Hong Kong Exchange , December 30, 2019; Hong Kong Exchange , May 9, 2021). A 7Road subsidiary involved in Huang’s gaming portfolio later became a vehicle for 7Road’s cloud computing business, buying graphics processors and servers ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [4] In 2022, it raised RMB 150 million ($24 million at the time) through a sale-and-lease-back of equipment that included 9,800 graphics processors ( Hong Kong Exchange , March 15, 2022). Kang had planned to pitch major technology companies, including Tencent and Alibaba, as tenants (Author interview, November 16).  [6] When Ms. Huang took over 7Road International—7Road’s Singapore-based subsidiary—in 2023, its move into overseas data center operation was in some ways a natural next step. reported control transfers in May-Jul. 2016"}]} Notes [1] A cooptee is an MSS collaborator, whom the ministry uses for operational support—typically in exchange for favors. They can help make introductions, serve as a go-between for the MSS and a source, provide excuses for sources to travel to the PRC, or otherwise assist the MSS in its operations. The MSS may also approach these people because of the access, business, or other ability that they have to support operations ( National Interest , June 11, 2017). [2] In November 2014, CITIC Securities (中信证券) bought a 3.8 percent stake in a technology firm under a stock return swap with Hexi, helping Gu gain control of the listed company ( CSRC , May 12, 2017). Ms. Huang worked in securities financing at CITIC at the time. The deal may have brought her into contact with Kang a year before she joined Hexi ( Hexi Investment , March 17, 2017). [3] In 2014, Hexi subscribed for shares in Century Huatong connected to its acquisitions of Tianyou Software (天游软件) and Wuxi SevenCool (无锡七酷网络). In 2017, Wuxi SevenCool sold the gaming company Hangzhou Shengfeng (杭州盛锋) to Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), whose ultimate controller is Kang (CNINF, March 9, 2014 , March 7, 2017 ). [4] The name of this firm, Shanghai Lingsu (上海凌素), closely resembles another firm within Ms. Huang’s business network, Shanghai Lingsuda (上海领素达), which invests primarily in smart mobility and ride-hailing platforms (see the Interactive Map) ( CAIC , August 16, 2023; Hong Kong Exchange , December 23, 2024). Yunxi also entered the ownership chain of a data center holding company, also based in Shanghai, and in 2025 changed its own registered name to Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group (上海珑腾智算数据集团) ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 13, 2023; Times Weekly , November 9). In Shanghai business circles, it is common to register a series of companies with names that share the same Chinese characters or use different characters with the same pronunciation. Other businesspeople can then easily tell who actually controls a company from its name alone. [5] Kang had previously used companies he controlled, including Hexi, to take over three major Phicomm shareholding vehicles ( Sina Finance , August 10, 2018). [6] Such data centers under Kang’s control, with refurbishment nearing completion, would very likely use Nvidia chips smuggled into the PRC through Huang’s Megaspeed. [7] The business tactic of offering one’s spouse to another man reaches even much further back. During the Warring States period, Zichu (子楚), a prince of Qin (秦), took an interest in Zhao Ji (赵姬), the consort of the merchant Lu Buwei (吕不韦). Lu, considering how much he had already bet on Zichu to be the next King of Qin, offered Zhao Ji, who was already pregnant, to him. After Zichu became king of Qin, Lu was appointed chancellor and wielded power over the Qin court ( Records of the Grand Historian , accessed November 11). A historical conspiracy theory even held that Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), first emperor of ancient China, was Lu and Zhao Ji’s son. In the early 2010s, PRC financial media and business books often portrayed Lu Buwei as a merchant who knew how to bet on real power (through whatever means), fueling an interest in him among businessmen of the era (see Fortune China , March 23, 2011). That was precisely when Kang rose to prominence in business. The post Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government appeared first on Jamestown .

这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章中的第二部分。起初，必要性是欧洲商业与中华人民共和国之间伙伴关系之母。在瑞士商学院，电梯制造商辛德勒的例子仍然是一个主题研究。 1979年，这家瑞士公司成为早期与中国的合资伙伴，尽管它与怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson）有联系，怡和洋行是一家与19世纪鸦片贸易有关的香港贸易公司。原因是：中国出现了住房危机。它正在向天空扩展，因为不断增长的人口需要塔楼。该国缺乏尖端技术，不得不到国外采购。最终，这家瑞士公司战胜了日本和美国的竞争对手。政治起了一定作用。瑞士于1950年承认中华人民共和国，是一个中立国。如今，中国拥有庞大的国内电梯行业，并与芬兰通力公司和日本日立公司等建立了合资企业。中国也需要汽车。它与大众汽车达成协议，到 1983 年春天，大众帕萨特的一个版本（更名为桑塔纳）开始在道路上行驶。其棱角分明的风格成为私人交通革命的象征。这些汽车是由上海大众汽车公司（现称为上汽集团）与德国公司和当地投资者的合资企业生产的。如今，上汽集团已成为电动汽车和电池领域的领导者。
在航空领域，空中客车公司开创了合资制造的先河，比美国飞机制造商麦道公司的合资企业更长久，并为欧洲发动机和技术的盈利出口铺平了道路。尽管中国致力于建造自己的商业上可行的民用客机，但这些出口仍然强劲。这些故事体现了欧洲的乐观情绪，这种乐观情绪伴随着中国从 2001 年开始加入世界贸易组织 (WTO)，并推动了本世纪初的贸易交易和外国直接投资。正如香港驻日内瓦代表所说，这是“双赢”。紧张的早期迹象出现在专利和所有权纠纷中。中国官员经常将“技术转让”视为对双方都有利的好事。它成为在某些领域开展业务的条件。跨国公司的国家经理往往主要热衷于扩大在中国的业务，他们会向总部保证他们的中国合作伙伴是值得信赖的。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the second of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. At first, necessity was the mother of partnership between European commerce and the People’s Republic of China. At Swiss business schools, the example of Schindler, the elevator maker, remains a keynote study. In 1979, the Swiss company became an early joint venture partner with China, even though it had ties with Jardine Matheson, the Hong Kong-based trading house associated with the opium trade of the 19 th century. The reason: China had a housing crisis. It was expanding skyward because a growing population required tower blocks. The country lacked sophisticated technology and had to shop abroad. Eventually, the Swiss firm won out over Japanese and American competitors. Politics played a part. Switzerland had recognized the People’s Republic in 1950, and it was a neutral power. Today China has a giant domestic elevator industry of its own plus joint ventures with, among others, Kone of Finland and Hitachi of Japan. China also needed cars. It made a deal with Volkswagen and by the spring of 1983 a version of the VW Passat, renamed the Santana, was plying the roads. Its angular style became a symbol of a revolution in private transport. The cars were manufactured by Shanghai Volkswagen Automotive, today known as SAIC, in a joint venture with the German firm and local investors. Today SAIC is a leader in the field of electric vehicles and batteries.   In aviation, Airbus pioneered joint venture manufacturing, outlasting a venture by the US plane maker McDonnell-Douglas and paving the way for profitable European exports of engines and technology, which remain strong despite China’s drive to build a commercially viable civil airliner of its own. These stories exemplified the optimism in Europe which accompanied China’s membership of the World Trade Organization (WTO) from 2001 and drove trade deals and foreign direct investment through the early years of this century. It was, as the Hong Kong representative in Geneva had said, “win-win.” The early signs of strain emerged in disputes over patents and ownership. Chinese officials regularly spoke of “technology transfer” as a good which would serve both sides. It became a condition of doing business in certain fields. Multinational country managers, often keen primarily to expand their footprint in China, would assure head offices that their Chinese partners could be trusted. Meanwhile, low-cost Chinese manufactured goods poured into European markets under the tariffs agreed on entry to the WTO. Initially confident of their negotiating power as a bloc, the Europeans refrained from resorting to rhetoric about trade wars or dumping. The Chinese export wave, known today as the China Shock, was seen by specialists as a transitional phenomenon that would eliminate itself through the magic of free trade. Today’s leader, Xi Jinping, watched from a critical vantage point as the manufacturing and export boom in China turned a pariah state into an economic powerhouse that had foreign governments, banks and corporations knocking on its door. His fortunes, indeed, advanced with the country’s renaissance. Xi’s career took off in the coastal province of Fujian, which stood at the forefront of China’s export zones. It received a flood of investment from Taiwan, whose manufacturers realized that instead of trying to sell goods into the Chinese market, they should make things cheaply in China to sell to others. This was the trick that turned the world economy inside out. At some point during this period, party elders decided to favor Xi Jinping as a rising official whose consciousness of the value of trade was matched by his cautious disposition. In China, the consensus remained that prosperity and peace were indivisible (which also lowered the risks of any adventure to seize Taiwan). When Xi moved up the hierarchy to vice president in 2008, he visited a slew of European nations as he worked to understand foreign countries and to grow into the top role. He, too, was being auditioned: he met Joe Biden, then also vice president. For all the courtship of Europe, it was the United States which mattered most to China. That is why the financial crisis in the West of 2008 dealt such a blow to Chinese reformers. It broke out in the American credit markets and then spread to Asia. The economic slowdown was the most serious problem the Chinese regime had faced in the new century. Exports collapsed by a fifth, foreign investment slowed, domestic consumption fell, and thousands of factories closed, leaving between 10 and 20 million workers jobless. The blow fell most heavily in the coastal export zones where Xi had made his name and the global trade experiment was at its height. The crisis almost consumed the administration of President Hu Jintao and Prime Minister Wen Jiabao. The technocrats rallied the central bank, raided currency reserves and threw the power of the state behind a $500bn stimulus package that poured funds into high-speed trains and urban infrastructure, reforming the tax system and doling out credit. It was the zenith of pragmatic managerialism in China, but the legacy would be more Communist Party control, a taste for intervention in markets and an iron determination on the part of Xi Jinping that China would never again be subject to the shocks of international capitalism. Facing down America and balancing Chinese economic interests with Europe would be his mission. title: Two prisoners, one rift: South Korea, Europe and Russia’s war on Ukraine
zh_title: 两名囚犯，一道裂痕：韩国、欧洲和俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争
summary: 封面图片：图片联盟/韩联社|韩联社 今天的全球破裂时代迫使欧盟及其成员国深化与世界各国的战略伙伴关系。 ECFR 与布鲁塞尔高级政策制定者的对话证实，欧盟正在努力锁定一批最值得信赖的合作伙伴。除其他好处外，这些合作伙伴还将在未来的立法（例如《工业加速器法案》）中获得特权地位。 [1] 作为一个志同道合的民主国家以及技术和国防强国，韩国是许多欧洲决策者在这一领域所关注的国家。
content:
封面图片：图片联盟/韩联社|韩联社 今天的全球破裂时代迫使欧盟及其成员国深化与世界各国的战略伙伴关系。 ECFR 与布鲁塞尔高级政策制定者的对话证实，欧盟正在努力锁定一批最值得信赖的合作伙伴。除其他好处外，这些合作伙伴还将在未来的立法（例如《工业加速器法案》）中获得特权地位。 [1] 作为一个志同道合的民主国家、技术和国防强国，韩国是许多欧洲决策者在这个新兴的值得信赖的中等强国网络中所关注的国家。他们希望这能够帮助他们实现多元化，一方面摆脱对华盛顿的安全依赖，另一方面摆脱对北京的经济依赖。但最近首尔和基辅之间因将朝鲜战俘移交至韩国而发生的外交争端表明，首尔和欧洲各国首都对同一场战争及其与莫斯科的关系的看法仍然截然不同。这一事件可能会让两个合作伙伴产生分歧，并给他们不断发展的关系设置战略上限。首尔和欧洲不需要以同样的方式看待乌克兰战争；但他们确实需要就一些战略基本规则达成一致。欧洲领导人对韩国对乌克兰反应的严重程度感到惊讶，需要更好地了解李明博政府的战略思维。
与此同时，首尔应该认识到，它在基辅和莫斯科的定位将强烈影响它未来几年能从欧洲获得什么利益。 不仅仅是囚犯 在乌克兰总统泽连斯基在九月的联合国大会上单方面披露移交两名朝鲜战俘的消息后，韩国总统李在明领导下召回了驻基辅大使，并减少了驻基辅大使馆的工作人员。首尔声称他的言论违反了对转让保密的明确谅解。从首尔的角度来看，这一披露不仅损害了双边关系，而且还破坏了其改善与平壤关系并重新开启对话的中长期战略——这是本届政府的一项关键政策优先事项。尽管两国外交部长最近在巴黎举行的会议可能标志着外交正常化的开始，但首尔最初的强烈反应揭示了政府更广泛的外交政策考虑。这些都是由朝鲜战争的深远影响和半岛的持续分裂所塑造的。韩国长期以来一直优先考虑与美国的联盟，同时寻求与中国（其最重要的市场和朝鲜的主要盟友）和俄罗斯保持稳定的关系。
从韩国执政民主党的许多政策制定者的角度来看，以及当地外交政策分析人士的说法，俄罗斯之所以重要，有以下三个原因：地理位置靠近韩国；经济机会的前景，包括获得化石燃料的机会；并作为将朝鲜带回谈判桌的外交途径。[2]相比之下，欧洲地理位置遥远，对半岛事务影响不大，因此主要被视为市场和经济伙伴，而不是韩国最紧迫的安全问题的关键中间人。在李的领导下，这种等级制度变得更加尖锐。政府的官方重点外交任务是“谋求稳定管理和发展韩俄关系”。但他们不

Cover image: picture alliance / Yonhapnews agency | Yonhap Today’s age of global rupture is compelling the EU and its member states to deepen strategic partnerships with countries around the world. ECFR conversations with senior policymakers in Brussels confirm the bloc is working to lock in a group of most trusted partners. Among other benefits, these partners will gain privileged status in future legislation such as the Industrial Accelerator Act. [1] As a like-minded democracy and technology and defence powerhouse, South Korea is a country many European decision-makers look to within this emerging web of trusted middle powers. They hope it can help them diversify away from their security dependencies on Washington, on the one hand, and economic dependencies on Beijing, on the other. But a recent diplomatic dispute between Seoul and Kyiv over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea shows how differently Seoul and European capitals still view the same war and their relationship with Moscow. The incident risks driving the two partners apart and putting a strategic ceiling on their growing relationship. Seoul and Europe do not need to see the Ukraine war identically; but they do need to agree on some strategic ground rules. European leaders, surprised by the severity of the Korean response to Ukraine, need a better understanding of the Lee administration’s strategic thinking. At the same time, Seoul should recognise that its positioning on Kyiv and Moscow will strongly influence what benefits it can obtain from Europe in the coming years. More than prisoners Under President Lee Jae-myung, South Korea recalled its ambassador and reduced staff at its embassy in Kyiv after Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, unilaterally disclosed the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war at September’s UN General Assembly. Seoul claims his words breached a clear understanding to keep the transfer confidential . From Seoul’s perspective , the disclosure not only damaged bilateral relations but also undermined its mid- to long-term strategy to improve relations with Pyongyang and reopen dialogue—a key policy priority of the current administration. Although a recent meeting of both countries’ foreign ministers in Paris may have marked the beginning of diplomatic normalisation, Seoul’s initial sharp response sheds light on the administration’s broader foreign policy calculations. These are shaped by the profound legacy of the Korean war and the continued division of the peninsula. South Korea has long prioritised its alliance with America while seeking to maintain stable relations with both China—its most important market and North Korea’s main ally—and Russia. From the perspective of many South Korean policymakers from the governing Democratic Party, and according to local foreign policy analysts, Russia is important for three reasons: its geographical proximity to Korea; the prospect of economic opportunities, including access to fossil fuels; and as a diplomatic avenue to bring North Korea back to the negotiating table. [2] Europe, by contrast, is geographically distant, has little influence on peninsula affairs and is therefore mainly seen as a market and economic partner, not as a key broker for South Korea’s most immediate security concern. Under Lee, that hierarchy has sharpened. The government’s official key diplomatic tasks call for the “pursuit of stable management and development of ROK-Russia ties”. But they do not mention Europe at all, unlike the previous Democratic Party administration’s stated commitment to “Strengthening partnerships with European countries”. In a cabinet meeting in October , Lee advocated diplomacy with Russia “even in wartime” along with cooperation to secure access to Arctic shipping routes. Lee himself has also long been sceptical of stronger support for Ukraine, fearing it could undermine future relations with Russia. The recent appointment of Song Young-gil as special adviser for “peace diplomacy” points the same way. A recipient of Russia’s Order of Friendship, and former president Moon Jae-in’s special envoy to Moscow, Song demanded a public apology from Zelensky over the prisoner disclosure within days of his appointment. He also advocated closer relations with Moscow during a recent event in the National Assembly entitled “Seeking Peace on the Korean Peninsula Through the Restoration of Korea-Russia Relations”. Given his and Lee’s repeated remarks about cooperation with Russia, the escalation with Ukraine might also have been meant as a signal to Moscow. The Kremlin certainly read it this way, with Russia’s deputy foreign minister noting South Korea’s “desire to normalise relations”. None of this means Seoul is blind to the risks posed by Moscow. It has repeatedly voiced concern over—and called for the ending of—illegal military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang. And, despite the diplomatic dispute, the government is increasing its non-military aid to Ukraine to $100m next year. But during an ECFR roundtable discussion in October, Korean experts argued that Lee’s government has come to a different conclusion on the war. It assumes the conflict is set to end sooner rather than later , which will in turn reshuffle the geopolitical cards. Seoul believes Washington’s re-engagement with Moscow will bear fruit, and that early outreach will position it well for what comes next. [3] And remaining open to Moscow costs little while offering opportunities to stabilise the Korean peninsula. Not a side issue The South Korean stance on Russia is not a side issue but a key criterion for cooperation That calculation, however, risks overlooking Seoul’s valuable and growing defence and economic partnership with Europe. For Europeans, the defining security threat of the coming decade comes from Russia. Even an end to the war in Ukraine will not fundamentally change this sentiment. As the EU and member states seek trusted partners in the world, the South Korean stance on Russia is not a side issue but a key criterion for cooperation. This is especially true for frontline states such as Poland. [4] Seoul’s harsh response to Kyiv and public overtures towards Moscow thus risk sowing doubt in European minds about South Korea’s reliability as a strategic partner . These doubts are rarely voiced publicly, but they are prevalent among European policymakers and diplomats engaged in these discussions. [5] They also predate the recent prisoner dispute. [6] Even some in the South Korean diplomatic community have warned that Lee’s policy on Ukraine and Russia could damage relations with Europe. The risk is greatest for defence exports—which are Seoul’s economic priority in Europe. Unlike ordinary trade, arms sales and industrial cooperation require political trust, as projects and servicing can stretch across decades. Korean defence firms have benefited from Europe’s spending surge following Russia’s aggression: EU imports of South Korean arms and ammunition have risen almost tenfold , from €191m in 2022 to €1.82bn in 2025. Hanwha Aerospace’s new plant in Romania and its joint venture with WB Electronics in Poland show Europeans integrating Korean firms into their long-term planning. But if South Korea diverges too far for European sensibilities on Ukraine and Russia, governments in Europe could come to see these partnerships as a liability in their planning on Russia. They may look for alternatives, even if these cost more. Strategic reasoning may already have cost Korea valuable contracts. Shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean recently lost out to a German competitor as Canada’s preferred submarine supplier, with prime minister Mark Carney explaining that his government sought to “meet Canada’s combined strategic, security, and economic interests”. The German bid offered closer integration with European NATO allies. Although the decision was not directly linked to Ukraine, it suggests that, in defence, strategic alignment matters at least as much as technology and pricing. Ukraine’s reconstruction is another South Korean economic interest at risk. Conversations with Korean experts indicate that, for many in Seoul, the war in Ukraine is seen less as a security question and more as a business opportunity. [7] The World Bank estimates recovery costs at $588bn, and Korean construction, energy and infrastructure firms are eyeing a share of it . Seoul has positioned itself as a key partner in this undertaking. But ultimately, contracts will be awarded in Kyiv, with much of the initial funding coming from European public money. Strategic mistrust could thus cost Korean businesses a substantial share of prospective contracts. Listening and understanding To safeguard the immense potential of deeper cooperation between Europe and South Korea, both partners should consider some ground rules. First, Europeans need to accept that Seoul has its own strategic priorities. The continued division of the peninsula, where the great power interests of America, China and Russia intersect, means South Korea’s immediate priorities will not always match Europe’s. If Europeans expect Seoul to take their security concerns seriously, they should show more interest in South Korea’s own. That may include proactively offering to support peacebuilding efforts and dialogue on the Korean peninsula, for example through the Swedish embassy in Pyongyang.   Second, Seoul should recognise that deeper relations with Europe run through Kyiv. Europeans gain a lot from closer defence cooperation with Seoul, but they must feel confident that South Korea shares the goal of ending the war on terms acceptable to Kyiv and will enforce sanctions on Russia effectively and reliably. South Korea does not need to be a leader on Ukraine. But if Europeans interpret its moves as undermining their security, Seoul may find them raising the drawbridge. Third, cooperation should be based on interests, not values. The Lee administration explicitly describes its foreign policy as pragmatic and interest-led. Europeans should stress the concrete gains of a predictable South Korean position on Ukraine and Russia and hence a closer strategic partnership with Europe: deeper defence-industrial cooperation, a larger stake in reconstruction, and bigger market shares in other strategic sectors, from batteries and electric vehicles to chips and artificial intelligence. They should make this case not only to the government but to Korean industry, which commands significant influence in policy circles. With better mutual understanding, the “prisoner dispute” can be the beginning of a more mature strategic partnership for Europe and South Korea, rather than the start of growing strategic mistrust. summary: 香港太空馆即将推出太空展览 预计参观人数达50万 |中国劳工布告栏 星期二, 2026 年 11 月 24 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港太空馆将推出太空展览，预计将吸引 50 万参观者 香港太空馆将于 11 月 25 日起举办新的太空展览，展出神舟二十三号宇航员签名徽章和田湾相机模型。博物馆馆长苏柱荣预计参观人数约为50万人次。香港太空馆将于 2019 年 12 月起推出“太空逐梦——宇航员天宫日记”展览。
content:
香港太空馆即将推出太空展览 预计参观人数达50万 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 24 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港太空馆推出太空展览 预计参观人数达50万人次
香港太空馆将于11月25日起举办全新太空展览，展出神舟二十三号宇航员签名徽章及田湾相机模型。博物馆馆长苏柱荣预计参观人数约为50万人次。
香港太空馆将于明日（11 月 25 日）推出“太空追梦——宇航员天宫日记”展览。展览将持续至明年7月19日，免费向公众开放。
展览将展示神舟二十三号宇航员签名的任务徽章，并包括互动展品。参观者可以操作机械臂并观察科学实验。博物馆还将展示“田湾”相机的全尺寸模型，这是第一个安装在天宫空间站上的本地开发的科学有效载荷。触摸屏显示器将解释有效载荷的工作原理，并显示其探测器在香港上空收集的数据。
博物馆馆长苏柱荣表示，此次展览的时间恰逢神舟二十四号计划于明天凌晨发射。他指出，香港首位有效载荷专家黎嘉英曾参与神舟二十三号任务，近年来公众对太空的兴趣日益浓厚。据估计，参观展览的人数将在50万人左右。
展览还将包括多个主题拍照点。游客可以与“飞天”舱外宇航服复制品合影留念。

Hong Kong Space Museum to launch space exhibition, expects 500,000 visitors | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 24 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong Space Museum to launch space exhibition, expects 500,000 visitors
Hong Kong Space Museum will open a new space exhibition from 25 November, featuring the Shenzhou-23 crew-signed badges and a model of the Tin Wan camera. Museum director So Chu-wing expects about 500,000 visitors.
The Hong Kong Space Museum will launch a new exhibition titled “Chasing Dreams in Space — Astronauts’ Tiangong Diary” starting tomorrow, 25 November. The exhibition will run until 19 July next year and is free for the public.
The exhibition will display signed mission badges from the Shenzhou-23 crew and include interactive exhibits. Visitors can operate robotic arms and observe scientific experiments. The museum will also feature a full-scale model of the “Tin Wan” camera, the first locally developed scientific payload to be installed on the Tiangong space station. Touch-screen displays will explain the payload’s operating principles and show data collected by its detector over Hong Kong.
Museum director So Chu-wing said the exhibition was timed to coincide with the scheduled launch of Shenzhou-24 early tomorrow morning. He noted that Hong Kong’s first payload specialist, Carrie Lai Ka-ying, took part in the Shenzhou-23 mission and that public interest in space has grown in recent years. So estimated that around 500,000 people will visit the exhibition.
The exhibition will also include several themed photo spots. Visitors can take pictures with a replica of the “Feitian” extravehicular spacesuit.

投资推广署看到将东西方绿色科技与香港研发联系起来的机会 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 24 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
投资推广署看到将东西方绿色科技与香港研发联系起来的机会
投资推广署高级副总裁杜丽薇表示，真正的机会在于将东方供应链与西方市场连接起来，并将研发中心设在香港。她强调了香港作为绿色科技双向桥梁的作用，并列举了阿特斯阳光电力子公司和英国合作伙伴等例子。
投资推广署高级副总裁（可持续发展）杜培伟表示，投资推广署的真正机遇是将东方的供应链与西方的高价值市场连接起来，并在香港进行研发和融资。
周二，杜琪峰在 Full Vision Capital 主办的首届 TERA-Talk 演讲中表示，香港是连接绿色科技计划与真正跨境业务的双向桥梁。从东方来看，投资推广署帮助清洁科技公司扩大海外投资和生产；而它则帮助西方企业将尖端技术和贸易引入亚洲，包括大湾区。
陶告诉与会者：“我们相信，最大的绿色科技胜利只有东西方共同努力才能实现。”他指出，欧洲在回收、清洁运输和碳捕获方面拥有优势，而中国大陆在电池存储、可再生能源、电动汽车和清洁制造方面处于领先地位。
杜指出，永恒星球是可再生能源巨头阿特斯阳光电力的住宅储能子公司，投资推广署帮助该公司与香港证券交易所和结算所建立了联系，因为该公司正考虑在未来几年进行首次公开​​募股。
此外，她还将英国视为对外扩张的主要着陆点，并指出与英国保险公司保诚集团的共同努力，为新能源解决方案公司确定市场切入点。
杜强调，香港的“一国、两种制度”框架提供了同时进入中国内地和全球贸易路线的机会，并以普通法法律体系、自由资本流动、低税制和强有力的知识产权保护为基础。

InvestHK sees opportunity in linking East-West green tech with R&D in Hong Kong
InvestHK senior vice president Olivia To says the real opportunity lies in connecting Eastern supply chains with Western markets, with R&D anchored in Hong Kong. She highlighted Hong Kong's role as a two-way bridge for green tech, citing examples like Canadian Solar's subsidiary and UK partnerships.
The real opportunity at InvestHK is connecting the supply chain in the East with high-value markets in the West, with research and development anchored and financed in Hong Kong, according to Olivia To Pui-wai, senior vice president (sustainability) of Invest Hong Kong.
Speaking at the inaugural TERA-Talk hosted by Full Vision Capital on Tuesday, To described Hong Kong as a two-way bridge connecting green tech plans into real cross-border businesses. From the East, InvestHK helps clean tech companies expand their investment and productions overseas; whereas it helps Western companies to bring in cutting-edge technologies and trade into Asia, including the Greater Bay Area.
"The biggest green tech wins, we trust, happen when East and West work together," To told attendees, noting that Europe holds strengths in recycling, clean transportation and carbon capture, while mainland China leads at scale in battery storage, renewables, electric vehicles and clean manufacturing.
To pointed to Eternal Planet, a residential energy storage subsidiary of renewable energy giant Canadian Solar, which InvestHK has helped connect with Hong Kong Stock Exchanges and Clearing as the company is eyeing a potential initial public offering in coming years.
In addition, she cited the United Kingdom as a primary landing pad for outbound expansion, pointing to joint efforts with British insurer Prudential to identify market entry points for new energy solutions firms.
To emphasised that Hong Kong's "one country, two systems" framework provides simultaneous access to mainland China and global trade routes, underpinned by a common law legal system, free capital flows, a low tax regime and robust intellectual property protections.

黄仁勋 Megaspeed 丑闻对欧洲意味着什么？乍一看，情况并不多：欧洲人将继续购买英伟达芯片。但仔细观察就会发现，连锁反应将对跨大西洋关系以及欧洲与北京日益紧张的关系产生影响。荷兰及其明星芯片制造商 ASML 看起来尤其容易受到影响。黄也许是华盛顿最有影响力的中国鸽派。他几乎单枪匹马地说服唐纳德·特朗普总统及其内阁采取宽松的方式执行拜登时代对英伟达芯片的出口管制，这激怒了两党鹰派。他的影响力减弱，再加上有关通过新加坡向中国非法走私芯片规模的新揭露，意味着鹰派再次得势。美国商务部已经采取行动，禁止中国人工智能公司使用海外数据中心。三项法案似乎将被纳入《国防授权法》，以进一步打击中国使用美国芯片。其中之一——MATCH法案——针对的是中国的芯片制造工具供应。荷兰公司 ASML 是这些工具的全球主要制造商。在美国制裁的威胁下，它将被迫遵守其美国竞争对手目前面临的相同限制。

What does the Jensen Huang Megaspeed scandal mean for Europe? At first glance, not much: Europeans will keep buying Nvidia chips. But a closer look shows that the ripple effects will have consequences for transatlantic relations and for Europe’s increasingly tense relationship with Beijing. The Netherlands and its star chip machine manufacturer, ASML, look particularly vulnerable. Huang was perhaps Washington’s most influential China dove. He almost single-handedly persuaded President Donald Trump and his cabinet to take a lax approach to enforcing Biden-era export controls on Nvidia chips, to the fury of hawks on both sides of the aisle. His diminished influence, coupled with fresh revelations around the extent of illegal chip smuggling to China via Singapore, means that the hawks once again have the wind in their sails. The Department of Commerce has already moved to  block  Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centers. Three bills look  set  to be rolled into the National Defense Authorization Act that would further crack down on China’s use of US chips.  One of them — the MATCH Act — takes aim at China’s supply of chipmaking tools. Dutch company ASML is the major global manufacturer of these tools. It would be forced to comply with the same restrictions currently faced by its US competitors, under threat of US sanctions.  European and Dutch diplomats, including the Dutch Royal Family, have already  lobbied  against the MATCH Act, which looked unlikely to pass into law — until the Megaspeed scandal broke. In effect, the Act would ban ASML from selling new chipmaking machines to China, which accounts for around a  fifth  of the company’s annual revenue, and from fulfilling its contractual obligations to service existing machines already in the country.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work.
