Even if the MATCH Act passes, the White House will have discretion over how aggressively the legislation is applied. President Trump has tried to shield Nvidia and maintain good relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping. That gives Washington leeway to decline to enforce its toughest provisions — but still leaves ASML vulnerable to shifting political priorities or a future, more hawkish administration. If the US ultimately forces ASML to cut off servicing to Chinese companies, the Netherlands — and Europe — could find themselves exposed to Chinese retaliation. When Beijing  imposed  export controls on rare earths in 2025 in response to US trade actions, it ensured European companies were also caught in the crossfire. Beijing would likely not hesitate to make an example out of the Netherlands in order to discourage other countries from allying too closely with Washington. The MATCH Act is being discussed just as Europe itself is in the middle of executing a major hawkish turn on China, driven by the latter’s industrial overcapacities and supply chain dominance. Whereas the EU was unwilling to take a strong stance on China during Trump’s first term — when administration officials pressed European countries to remove Huawei telecoms equipment — and under former President Joseph Biden, the bloc is now developing powerful new trade instruments directed against Beijing. Despite this shift, Europe’s China policy remains fundamentally defensive. European capitals do not share Washington’s interest in undermining China’s AI sector. In fact, the EU benefits from Chinese competition to closed-source US frontier labs. Europe’s telecoms incumbents are resisting ripping out Huawei from their networks,  arguing  that the exclusion of Chinese suppliers would be  costly  and leave them dependent on expensive local vendors. US China hawks should think twice before trying to strong-arm Europe into mirroring US China policy. Such a move would likely backfire by galvanizing anti-US and pro-China figures in Europe. There is a deal to be done. For their part, EU countries need to follow through on the tough talk and deliver on China de-risking, with concrete measures such as improving coordination and closing gaps in EU and national licensing of chipmaking components. If Washington sees Europe acting of its own accord, it can formally take the threat of sanctions off the table. In the end, controls that allies adopt through their own volition are likely to prove more durable than those imposed on them by ultimatum. 香港在致命火灾后于周五提出两项消防安全法案中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 24 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港在致命火灾后周五提出两项消防安全法案
香港将于 2026 年 11 月 26 日发布两项消防安全法案，旨在在 2025 年大埔致命火灾后彻底修订《消防条例》。该法案引入了消防设施的固定处罚制度和责任人制度，立法辩论将于 12 月 2 日开始。
香港保安局11月24日宣布，政府将于11月28日公布《2026年消防（修订）条例草案》及《定额罚款（消防）条例草案》。这两项法案旨在实现消防安全法律框架现代化，增强公共安全，提高监管一致性和执法有效性，并明确行业责任。
保安局发言人表示，政府高度重视消防安全。 2025年11月大埔宏福苑发生第五级火灾后，政府成立由保安局局长担任主席的专责小组，全面检讨《消防条例》（第95章）及其附属法例，并规划中长期改革。这项检讨被列为2026年施政报告的优先改革措施。
发言人表示，政府已于10月29日公布独立委员会就大埔火灾的报告。修正案全面涵盖了报告中涉及消防安全并需要立法修改的八项建议。修订条例草案修订《消防条例》及三项附属规例：《消防处（装置承办商）规例》（第95A章）、《消防处（装置及设备）规例》（第95B章）及《消防处（消除危险火患）规例》（第95F章）。 《定额罚款条例草案》引入了定额罚款制度，以明确和易于核实的消防安全违法行为。
建议修订涵盖六大支柱： 加强消防装置及设备的规管制度；引入消防装置负责人制度；全面改革消防装置承办商的注册和纪律制度；增加处罚和刑事责任；引入定额罚款制度并简化危险火灾消除程序；加强消防处的执法权力，打击非法转移燃料。
保安局于5月5日咨询立法会保安事务委员会，委员普遍表示支持。 5月26日开始的为期一个月的公众咨询收到了506份有效意见，其中477份（94.3％）表示支持或积极意见。独立委员会报告发布后，政府加快了立法工作。 11月3日，安全事务委员会、经济发展事务委员会和立法事务委员会成员联合重申支持并敦促尽早立法。

Hong Kong to table two fire safety bills on Friday after fatal blaze
Hong Kong will publish two fire safety bills on 26 November 2026, aiming to overhaul the Fire Services Ordinance after a deadly 2025 fire in Tai Po. The bills introduce a fixed-penalty system and a responsible-person regime for fire installations, with legislative debate starting on 2 December.
The Hong Kong Security Bureau announced on 24 November that the government will publish the Fire Services (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Fixed Penalty (Fire Services) Bill on 28 November. The two bills aim to modernise the fire-safety legal framework, enhance public safety, improve regulatory consistency and enforcement effectiveness, and clarify industry responsibilities.
According to a Security Bureau spokesperson, the government attaches high importance to fire safety. Following a fifth-alarm fire at Wang Fook Court in Tai Po in November 2025, the government established a task force chaired by the Secretary for Security to comprehensively review the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95) and its subsidiary legislation, and to plan medium- and long-term reforms. The review was listed as a priority reform measure in the 2026 Policy Address.
The spokesperson noted that the government released the report of the independent committee on the Tai Po fire on 29 October. The amendment bill fully covers the eight recommendations in the report that relate to fire safety and require legislative changes. The amendment bill revises the Fire Services Ordinance and three subsidiary regulations: the Fire Services (Installation Contractors) Regulation (Cap. 95A), the Fire Services (Installations and Equipment) Regulation (Cap. 95B), and the Fire Services (Dangerous Fire Hazard Abatement) Regulation (Cap. 95F). The Fixed Penalty Bill introduces a fixed-penalty system for clear and easily verifiable fire safety offences.
The proposed amendments cover six pillars: strengthening the regulatory regime for fire service installations and equipment; introducing a responsible-person regime for fire installations; overhauling the registration and disciplinary system for fire installation contractors; increasing penalties and criminal liability; introducing a fixed-penalty system and streamlining dangerous-fire-hazard abatement procedures; and enhancing the Fire Services Department's enforcement powers and combating illegal transfer of fuel.
The Security Bureau consulted the Legislative Council's Panel on Security on 5 May, where members expressed general support. A month-long public consultation starting 26 May received 506 valid submissions, of which 477 (94.3 per cent) expressed support or positive views. Following the release of the independent committee's report, the government accelerated legislative work. On 3 November, members of the Panels on Security and on Economic Development and Legislative Affairs jointly reaffirmed support and urged early legislation.
The government has incorporated public feedback. For instance, the amendment bill allows a responsible person who is not the owner but has management or control over fire installations—such as a property management company—to use a defence if they can prove they took all reasonable steps and exercised due diligence. In response to the independent committee's report, the bill also empowers the Director of Fire Services to suspend or cancel a registered fire installation contractor's registration if it is in the public interest.
The government will submit the two bills to the Legislative Council on 2 December for first reading and commencement of second reading, aiming to complete the legislative process within the current government's term.

summary: 香港移民局逮捕非法导游的女子中国劳工公告 2026 年 11 月 24 日，星期二 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港入境处拘捕一名因暗中诱骗非法导游而被捕的女子 香港入境处与旅游业监管局联合行动，逮捕了一名涉嫌通过社交媒体提供非法导游和摄影服务的 23 岁女子。当局警告雇主，若雇用非法劳工，将受到严厉处罚。香港入境事务处（I
content:
香港移民局逮捕非法导游的女子中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 24 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港入境处逮捕非法导游的卧底女子
香港入境处与旅游业监管局联合行动，拘捕一名涉嫌通过社交媒体提供非法导游和摄影服务的23岁女子。当局警告雇主，若雇用非法劳工，将受到严厉处罚。
香港入境事务处（入境处）与旅游业监管局联合行动，逮捕了一名涉嫌提供非法导游和摄影服务的23岁女子。该行动于 2026 年 11 月 24 日宣布，涉及便衣警察在社交媒体平台上冒充顾客来预订嫌疑人的服务。该女子抵达香港提供服务时被拘留。
入境处表示将考虑指控她违反逗留条件。根据香港法律，任何人违反逗留条件即属犯罪。未经移民局局长事先批准，所有访客不得从事工作，无论有酬或无酬。违法者将面临检控，一经定罪，最高可被罚款港币 50,000 元及监禁最长两年。协助或教唆此类犯罪行为将受到同样的处罚。
执法行动期间，入境处及旅游局人员亦到热门旅游景点派发单张，警告市民切勿聘用非法导游或领队。
入境处发言人强调，雇用无权在香港工作的人是严重犯罪。根据《入境条例》，雇主雇用非法入境者、被驱逐令、逾期居留者或被拒绝入境者，最高可面临港币 50 万罚款和 10 年监禁，高于之前的港币 35 万罚款和三年监禁。公司董事、经理、秘书和合伙人也可能承担刑事责任。上诉法院已发布量刑指南，要求对非法工人的雇主立即监禁。
根据法院判例，在雇用任何人之前，雇主必须采取一切可行的措施来核实该人的合法工作权利。这包括检查雇员的身份证并进行查询；任何不引起对合法性合理怀疑的答案都不能作为辩护。若求职者没有香港永久性居民身份证，雇主亦须检查其有效旅行证件。违规者最高可被罚款15万港元及监禁一年。
入境处提醒雇主切勿违法，并会继续严格执法。该部门遵循标准程序，对所有可能遭受剥削的被捕者（包括非法工人、非法入境者、性工作者和外籍家庭佣工）进行筛查，以发现人口贩运或强迫劳动的迹象。如果发现此类指标，将使用标准检查表进行全面的调查和识别过程。确定的受害者将获得紧急干预、医疗、咨询、庇护所和其他支持。入境处敦促人口贩卖或强迫劳动的受害者向当局举报罪行。
公众可通过举报非法就业举报专线

Hong Kong immigration arrests woman in undercover sting on illegal tour guides | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 24 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong immigration arrests woman in undercover sting on illegal tour guides
Hong Kong's Immigration Department and the Tourism Industry Regulatory Authority conducted a joint operation, arresting a 23-year-old woman suspected of offering illegal tour guide and photography services via social media. Authorities warn employers of severe penalties for hiring illegal workers.
Hong Kong’s Immigration Department (ImmD), in a joint operation with the Tourism Industry Regulatory Authority, arrested a 23-year-old woman on suspicion of providing illegal tour guide and photography services. The operation, announced on 24 November 2026, involved undercover officers posing as customers on social media platforms to book the suspect’s services. The woman was detained when she arrived in Hong Kong to deliver the services.
ImmD said it will consider charging her with breaching her conditions of stay. Under Hong Kong law, anyone who violates a condition of stay commits an offence. All visitors are prohibited from taking up employment, whether paid or unpaid, without prior approval from the Director of Immigration. Offenders face prosecution and, upon conviction, a maximum fine of HK$50,000 and up to two years in jail. Aiding or abetting such offences carries the same penalty.
During the enforcement action, ImmD and tourism authority officers also visited popular tourist spots to distribute leaflets warning the public against hiring illegal guides or tour leaders.
An ImmD spokesman stressed that employing a person not entitled to work in Hong Kong is a serious crime. Under the Immigration Ordinance, employers who hire individuals who are illegal entrants, subject to a removal or deportation order, overstayers, or refused entrants face a maximum penalty of a HK$500,000 fine and 10 years’ imprisonment, up from the previous HK$350,000 fine and three years. Company directors, managers, secretaries, and partners may also bear criminal liability. The Court of Appeal has issued sentencing guidelines requiring immediate imprisonment for employers of illegal workers.
According to court precedent, before hiring anyone, an employer must take all practicable steps to verify the person’s legal right to work. This includes checking the employee’s identity card and making inquiries; any answers that do not raise reasonable doubts about legality will not serve as a defence. If a job seeker does not have a Hong Kong permanent resident identity card, the employer must also check their valid travel documents. Violators face a maximum fine of HK$150,000 and one year in jail.
ImmD reminded employers not to break the law, warning it will continue strict enforcement. The department follows standard procedures to screen all arrestees who may be vulnerable to exploitation—including illegal workers, illegal entrants, sex workers, and foreign domestic helpers—for indicators of human trafficking or forced labour. If such indicators are found, a full investigation and identification process is conducted using a standard checklist. Identified victims receive emergency intervention, medical treatment, counselling, shelter, and other support. ImmD urged victims of trafficking or forced labour to report the crimes to the authorities.
Members of the public can report illegal employment via the dedicated hotline 185 185, fax 2824 1166, email [email protected], or the online reporting form at www.immd.gov.hk.

title: Hong Kong to impose citywide drone ban, harbour and road curbs for Interpol General Assembly next week
zh_title: 香港下周将在国际刑警组织大会上实施全市无人机禁令、港口和道路限制
summary: 香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，与会代表
content:
香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，来自196个成员国的代表将出席，探讨全球安全问题。警方行动组总警司黄志荣在周一的新闻发布会上表示，预计将有超过 1000 人参加此次活动，其中包括国际刑警组织成员国的警察局长以及政府高级官员。他表示，峰会期间，香港的整个空域将被指定为临时飞行限制区，禁止无人机、小型飞机和直升机以及滑翔伞、风筝和“大量气球”进行未经授权的操作。黄用粤语说：“但这些限制不会影响民用飞机的运营。”他补充说，民航处将向航空公司和飞行员公布航空限制的范围。
他警告居民，在下周的临时禁令期间，不要在未经许可的情况下操作无人机，并指出，根据《小型无人机令》，违法者最高可被处以10万港元罚款和两年监禁。 海上和陆地交通限制 当局将限制国际刑警组织峰会将在湾仔举行的香港会议展览中心附近的维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通，同时会场周围的道路也将被关闭。 2024 年 4 月 3 日，一名男子俯瞰香港维多利亚港。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港水上的士是一条深受游客欢迎的跨海路线，在峰会期间将跳过湾仔站。行人也将被禁止进入会展中心外的长廊。黄先生敦促居民注意交通限制并提前计划出行。他还敦促船只和巴士运营商提前计划，避免在国际刑警组织峰会场地附近接送乘客。黄补充说，警方将在活动期间协调港口和会场附近的海上和陆地交通。这是香港首次主办国际刑警组织大会，也是该活动第三次在中国举办。北京分别于1995年和2017年举办过两次。
上周，香港警方在邻近的中国城市深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织峰会期间逮捕了五名非法无人机操作男子，此前当局在香港北部领空的大部分地区实施了为期四天的禁飞区。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong will enforce air, sea and land restrictions when it hosts Interpol’s annual summit next week, limiting drone and small-aircraft operations as well as marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour. Authorities will impose a temporary restricted flying zone across the entire Hong Kong airspace for the duration of the 94th Interpol General Assembly from November 30 to December 3, 2026. Photo: Screenshot, via Hong Kong Police. The 94th International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) General Assembly is set to take place in Hong Kong from November 30 to December 3, with representatives from 196 member countries expected to attend to address global security issues. Wong Chi-wing, chief superintendent of the police’s operations wing, told a press conference on Monday that more than 1,000 people are expected to attend the event, including the police chiefs of Interpol’s member countries as well as senior government officials. He said Hong Kong’s entire airspace would be designated a temporary restricted flying zone for the duration of the summit, barring unauthorised operations of drones, small aircraft and helicopters, as well as paragliders, kites and “large numbers of balloons.” “But the restrictions will not affect civil aircraft operations,” Wong said in Cantonese, adding that the Civil Aviation Department would publicise the scope of the air restrictions for airlines and pilots. He warned residents against operating drones without a permit during the temporary ban next week, noting that offenders face a maximum penalty of a HK$100,000 fine and two years’ imprisonment under the Small Unmanned Aircraft Order. Sea and land traffic curbs Authorities will restrict marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour off the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, where the Interpol summit will take place, while roads surrounding the venue will also be closed. A man looks out over Victoria Harbour in Hong Kong, on April 3, 2024. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Hong Kong Water Taxi, a cross-harbour route popular with tourists, will skip its Wan Chai stop for the duration of the summit. Pedestrians will also be barred from entering the promenade outside the convention and exhibition centre. Wong urged residents to take note of the traffic restrictions and plan their journeys in advance. He also urged boat and bus operators to plan ahead and avoid picking up or dropping off passengers near the Interpol summit venue. Police will coordinate sea and land traffic in the harbour and near the venue for the duration of the event, Wong added. This will be the first time Hong Kong hosts the Interpol General Assembly and the third time the event has taken place in China. Beijing hosted it twice, in 1995 and 2017. Last week, Hong Kong police arrested five men over illegal drone operations during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the neighbouring Chinese city of Shenzhen, after authorities imposed a four-day restricted flying zone across much of Hong Kong’s northern airspace.

title: Hong Kong police arrest 38-year-old man over fatal Tsim Sha Tsui crash that killed Muslim community leader
zh_title: 香港警方因尖沙咀车祸导致穆斯林社区领袖死亡而逮捕38岁男子
summary: 周日，一辆汽车在尖沙咀驶上人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤，警方拘捕一名涉嫌酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡的38岁男子。 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。据警方新闻稿称，事件发生在下午 2:30 左右，发生在 Prat Avenue。当地媒体分享了闭路电视和旁观者的镜头，显示司机和一名女乘客在事发后试图逃离现场。
content:
周日，一辆汽车在尖沙咀驶上人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤，警方拘捕一名涉嫌酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡的38岁男子。 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。据警方新闻稿称，事件发生在下午 2:30 左右，发生在 Prat Avenue。当地媒体分享了闭路电视和旁观者的镜头，显示司机和一名女乘客在事故发生后试图逃离现场。总督察刘家恒在周日的警方新闻发布会上表示，有几名公众跟踪司机并向当局报警。 2026 年 11 月 22 日，总督察刘家恒（左）在新闻发布会上。图片：香港警务处截图，来自 Facebook。新闻稿称，一名53岁男性行人在昏迷不醒的情况下被送往伊丽莎白女王医院，并于下午3时23分证实死亡。新闻稿称：“经进一步调查，该名38岁私家车男司机因酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡被捕，现被拘留调查。” 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。
警方补充，一名62岁非华裔男性行人头部受伤，两名年龄分别为31岁和70岁的女性行人四肢受伤。三人均在神志清醒的情况下被送往伊利沙伯医院。事故发生后，人行道和路边看到一串损坏的自行车、碎片和破损的栏杆。穆斯林领袖被杀 香港穆斯林理事会在社交媒体上发布的帖子称，受害者是当地主要伊斯兰教育组织 Khatme Nubuwwat 伊斯兰理事会有限公司的副主席贾维德·马哈茂德 (Javed Mahmood)。屏幕截图：香港穆斯林理事会，来自 X。酒后驾驶的最高处罚是罚款 25,000 港元和监禁三年。危险驾驶致人死亡罪名成立，可判处十年监禁及罚款港币五万元。没有报告交通意外亦违反《道路交通条例》。然而，警方周一告诉香港新闻社，目前还没有关于被捕男子可能面临的指控的最新消息。致命车祸发生后的第二天，警方的 Instagram 页面上出现了一幅人工智能生成的漫画，上面写着“现实生活不是游戏。喝酒吗？不要开车”，这显然是对新发布的视频游戏《侠盗猎车手 VI》的模仿。西九龙交通部第一特别调查队正调查案件。目击者或任何知情者请致电 3661 9188 与警方联系。

【原文 English Original】
Police have arrested a 38-year-old man on suspicion of drink-driving and dangerous driving causing death after a vehicle mounted a pavement in Tsim Sha Tsui on Sunday, leaving one person dead and three injured. A vehicle mounted a pavement on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm on Sunday, November 22, 2026, leaving one dead and three injured. Photo: Courtesy of James Ockenden. The incident took place on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm, according to a police press release. Local media shared CCTV and bystander footage appearing to show the driver and a female passenger attempting to flee the scene after the crash. Speaking at a police press briefing on Sunday, Chief Inspector Lau Ka-hang said several members of the public followed the driver and alerted authorities. Chief Inspector Lau Ka-hang (left) at a press briefing on November 22, 2026. Photo: HKPF screenshot, via Facebook. The press release said a 53-year-old male pedestrian was rushed to Queen Elizabeth Hospital unconscious and was certified dead at 3:23pm. “After further investigations, the 38-year-old private car male driver was arrested for drink driving and dangerous driving causing death and is being detained for enquiries,” the press release said. A vehicle mounted a pavement on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm on Sunday, November 22, 2026, leaving one dead and three injured. Photo: Courtesy of James Ockenden. Police added that a 62-year-old non-ethnic Chinese male pedestrian sustained head injuries, while two female pedestrians, aged 31 and 70, suffered limb injuries. All three were taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in a conscious state. A trail of damaged bicycles, debris and mangled railings was seen across the pavement and roadside following the crash. Muslim leader killed Social media posts by the Muslim Council of Hong Kong identified the victim as Javed Mahmood, the vice-chair of Khatme Nubuwwat Islamic Council Limited, a major local Islamic education organisation. Screenshot: Muslim Council of Hong Kong, via X. The maximum penalty for drink-driving is a HK$25,000 fine and three years behind bars. Those convicted of causing death by dangerous driving face 10 years’ imprisonment and a HK$50,000 fine. Failing to report a traffic accident is also a breach of the Road Traffic Ordinance. However, police told HKFP on Monday that there was no update yet on the charges the arrested man might face. A day after the fatal crash, an AI-generated cartoon appeared on the police Instagram page stating that “real life is not gaming. Drank? Don’t drive,” in an apparent parody of the newly released video game Grand Theft Auto VI. Special Investigation Team 1 of Traffic Kowloon West is investigating the case. Witnesses or anyone with information are urged to contact officers on 3661 9188.

title: Anatomy of a Chinese loanbook
zh_title: 中国贷款簿剖析
summary: ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ 数据团队剖析了 200 多个贷款机构
content:
ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ数据团队剖析了2010年至2024年期间的200多份贷款协议和修正案。ICIJ发现，在审查的协议和修正案中，工银伦敦至少与另一家中国国有商业银行合作。在中国的银行中，中国银行脱颖而出，成为工银伦敦分行的主要中方合作伙伴：双方签署了 102 项协议。 ICIJ 的分析显示，这家中国银行业巨头的伦敦分行通常与其他中国和国际银行合作，达成价值数亿美元甚至更多的贷款协议。 ICIJ 发现了 36 项贷款协议和修正案，其中一半或以上的资金是由中国贷方提供的。其中 16 个案例的财务承诺完全来自中资银行。
ICIJ 的一项审查发现，作为对该行客户尽职调查过程的一部分，中国工商银行准备的文件显示，该行有时会淡化合规问题，或以其他方式证明继续与其被归类为高风险的客户开展业务是合理的。 在赞比亚，中国工商银行在加剧该国债务负担、造成对中国贷款的依赖以及给赞比亚人造成多年困难方面发挥了作用。在英国，中国工商银行的银行管理人员无视其一位中国客户在美国法院面临的法律风险，以便该银行能够为该公司收购英国竞争对手并巩固其市场份额提供资金。下面的案例研究揭示了一家银行在中国党国议程的推进与其自身的全球商业野心之间取得平衡的内部运作方式。无视红灯 01 2024年5月，工商银行的高风险客户名单包括全球燃料贸易商和分销商Puma Energy的融资部门以及大股东Trafigura Pte.有限公司是一家注册并总部位于新加坡的贸易巨头，主要贸易业务位于瑞士，以及另外两家托克实体。尽管中国工商银行对 Puma 和 Trafigura 的担忧至少可以追溯到 2015 年，但 ICIJ 发现 2015 年至 2024 年间涉及 Puma 和 Trafigura 的 19 项银团信贷安排协议，总价值达 387 亿美元。 ICBC 的伦敦实体在这些贷款中总共承诺提供 14 亿美元。
2015年，工商银行加大了对Puma旗下融资工具Puma International Financing的尽职调查力度；在其2015年5月的强化尽职调查（EDD）报告中，将该公司的贿赂风险评为“高”。 当时，Puma的股东包括安哥拉国有石油公司Sonangol和Cochan Holdings LLC（一家由安哥拉总统顾问Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento创立并担任主席的投资公司）。该报告承认，媒体广泛报道了涉及安哥拉高级官员的贿赂和腐败行为，其中包括当时的总统若泽·爱德华多·多斯桑托斯及其子女，以及Sonangol、Cochan和Nascimento。尽管如此，工行仍对大部分逆回购进行了描述

【原文 English Original】
ICIJ’s China Capital investigation revealed how the London units of the world’s largest bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), routinely financed companies to push Beijing’s geopolitical agenda, sometimes flouting their own compliance rules in the process. ICIJ, in collaboration with 23 media partners, obtained 4.8 million internal documents leaked from ICBC London, including loan application forms, due diligence reports, know-your-client documents and internal email exchanges. To better understand ICBC’s London operations, the ICIJ data team dissected more than 200 loan agreements and amendments dated from 2010 to 2024. ICIJ found that ICBC London partnered with at least one other Chinese state-owned commercial bank in more than half of the agreements and amendments reviewed. Among the Chinese lenders, Bank of China stands out as the main Chinese partner of ICBC London: They joined forces in 102 agreements. ICIJ’s analysis shows that the London units of the Chinese banking giant usually partnered with other Chinese and international banks on loan agreements often worth hundreds of millions of dollars—or more. ICIJ identified 36 loan agreements and amendments for which half or more of the money was provided by Chinese lenders. In 16 of those cases, the financial commitments were entirely from Chinese banks. ICBC documents prepared as part of the due diligence process on the bank’s clients show how the bank at times downplayed compliance problems or otherwise justified continued business with clients it had classified as high risk, an ICIJ review found. In Zambia, ICBC played a role in exacerbating the country’s debt burden, creating dependency on Chinese loans and contributing to years-long difficulties for Zambians. In the U.K., ICBC bank officers disregarded legal risks faced in a U.S. court by one of their Chinese clients so the bank could finance the company’s acquisition of a British competitor and consolidate its market share. The case studies below reveal the inner workings of a bank balancing the advancement of the agenda of the Chinese party-state with its own global commercial ambitions. Ignoring Red Lights 01 In May 2024, ICBC’s high-risk client list included the financing arm of global fuel trader and distributor Puma Energy, along with a major shareholder Trafigura Pte. Ltd., a trading giant registered and headquartered in Singapore with major trading operations in Switzerland, and two other Trafigura entities. Despite ICBC's concerns about Puma and Trafigura dating back to at least 2015, ICIJ identified 19 syndicated credit facility agreements involving Puma and Trafigura, between 2015 and 2024, with a combined value of $38.7 billion. ICBC's London entities committed a total of $1.4 billion across those facilities. In 2015, ICBC escalated its due diligence of Puma’s financing vehicle, Puma International Financing; in its May 2015 Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) report, it rated the company’s bribery risk as high. At the time, Puma's shareholders included Angola's state-owned oil company Sonangol and Cochan Holdings LLC, an investment company founded and chaired by Angolan presidential adviser Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento. The report acknowledged extensive adverse media coverage alleging bribery and corruption involving senior Angolan officials, including then-President José Eduardo dos Santos and his children, as well as Sonangol, Cochan and Nascimento. Still, ICBC characterized much of the adverse reporting as “rumour based and unfounded” and continued the relationship, subject to enhanced monitoring. In February 2020, ICBC’s EDD report again identified allegations centered on Nascimento’s close ties to former President dos Santos and speculation in media reports and elsewhere that he had used political connections to acquire a stake in Puma Energy while serving as a public official. The report also noted that Nascimento had faced investigations into alleged corruption, conflicts of interest and money laundering in several countries. Yet ICBC cited reasons for discounting the risks, noting that Nascimento did “not appear to have been convicted” of wrongdoing. In December 2021, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Nascimento and Cochan, saying Nascimento and another Angolan official had embezzled billions from the Angolan government. In 2025, an Angolan court convicted Nascimento of fraud, document forgery, money laundering and influence peddling. Likewise, ICBC's October 2019 Enhanced Due Diligence report came after a highly public Brazilian corruption investigation into allegations that commodity traders, including Trafigura, had bribed employees of Petrobras, Brazil’s state-owned and state-controlled oil company. A month earlier, Reuters reported allegations that senior Trafigura executives Mike Wainwright and José Larocca knew about the bribes. But ICBC's EDD report referred only to "two high-ranking executives” at Trafigura, without identifying them, despite separately listing both men as key controllers of Trafigura. Wainwright's adverse-media assessment was marked "No." ICBC continued the relationship, citing Trafigura's status as a longstanding "strategic client," the participation of major international banks in syndicated loans, its compliance controls and the absence of suspicious activity detected by ICBC. In 2024, Trafigura Beheer B.V., the Dutch-registered former parent company of the Trafigura Group, pleaded guilty in the U.S. to conspiring to violate U.S. anti-bribery laws in a scheme that ran from approximately 2003 to 2014. The companies also reached a settlement agreement with Brazilian authorities. Read responses Responses Trafigura: In response to ICIJ's questions, a Trafigura spokesperson said lender due diligence was a normal part of doing business and that the company cooperated with lenders' reviews, supported by its public financial and sustainability disclosures. Regarding the Petrobras bribery case, the spokesperson referred to Trafigura's 2024 statement announcing the resolution of the U.S. investigation, in which the company said the misconduct involved former employees or agents and was inconsistent with its principles and code of conduct. The statement said U.S. authorities had recognized improvements to Trafigura's anti-corruption compliance procedures. Puma: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Nascimento: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Angolan government: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Cochan: ICIJ could not successfully contact Cochan for comment. Sonangol: Didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. A legal representative for Mike Wainwright didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. José Larocca: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: Didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Puma International Financing S.A., Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Trading LLC Amount $1.4 billionTotal loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2024 From the China Capital files PUMA In their own words: There is a wealth of adverse news in the public domain citing the Angolan Government's bribery and corruption and monopolisation of various industries in Angola.Risk From the China Capital files TRAFIGURA In their own words: The risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened [...] and thus this poses an increased reputational risk to the Bank.Risk Trafigura is an existing and strategic client of the Bank.Mitigating factors Financing Kleptocrats 02 ICBC started lending to Socar, Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas concern, in 2015 when ICBC London took part in a revolving credit facility to one of the company’s subsidiaries, Socar Trading SA. Even though the bank decided to exit this facility in 2019 because of the company's “underperformance and ongoing restructuring," a review of ICBC documents shows that under the head office’s encouragement, ICBC’s London and Turkey offices maintained close connection with Socar. Bank officers in an internal memo noted “Azerbaijan's geopolitical importance in the area's political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors,” adding “SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China's 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy." ICBC London committed to at least three additional loans, each between $25 million and $89 million, even as the bank continued to list Socar among high-risk clients, with one document stating: “the risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened." Corporate bank officers underlined the risks presented by the nature of Socar’s business and its jurisdiction, Azerbaijan; the fact that all the members of its board of directors were, at the time, identified as politically exposed persons, including the president and 12 vice presidents; Socar’s lack of transparency and accountability; and that the company had recently featured in major international corruption scandals. Yet the same year that ICBC listed these risks, 2021, the bank agreed to lend Socar $89 million. ICBC and Socar had deepened their ties in 2018, when the bank’s London branch listed $1.58 billion worth of green bonds on the London Stock Exchange, and Azerbaijan's State Oil Fund, SOFAZ, decided to invest $150 million. Socar, which sells oil and gas on the state’s behalf, contributed about 90% of SOFAZ’s 2017 revenue. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project later reported that leaked documents from inside British Petroleum exposed that two Socar subsidiaries were set to siphon off more than $1.7 billion from the Shah Deniz 2 gas project through padded contracts and fake charges. Socar denied the allegations. Read response Response Socar: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. SOFAZ: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower Socar and its subsidiaries Amount $217 million (4 loans)Total loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2021 From the China Capital files In their own words: Given Azerbaijan’s geopolitical importance in the area’s political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors, SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China’s 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy aimed at creating infrastructure and establishing links among the Eurasian countries.Risk Consolidating Market Share 03 ICBC records show bank risk management officials looking past the potentially illegal actions of a Chinese customer seeking a loan to buy out one of its competitors. In 2017 ICBC London Branch agreed to back China’s Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.’s acquisition of Sepura PLC, a British telecommunications competitor in the mobile radio communications sector. Hytera designs and manufactures professional mobile communications devices commonly used by law enforcement agencies worldwide — including two-way radios, a market that at the time was expected to be worth $7.3 billion by 2025. The agreement with ICBC London, which was the only lender involved, allowed Hytera to borrow up to $57.1 million over three years. Sepura shareholders had approved the $92.7 million acquisition in January 2017 but antitrust authorities in the UK and Germany, where governments relied on Sepura’s technology, stalled the acquisition. Spanish antitrust authorities also assessed the transaction, which was eventually approved in May of that year. While conducting their due diligence work to approve the loan in early 2017, ICBC London employees discovered that Motorola Solutions Inc., another competitor in the mobile telecommunications market, had filed a lawsuit pending against Hytera in a U.S. federal court for alleged patent infringement and industrial espionage. The bank’s compliance officers allowed the loan to go forward anyway, adding a handwritten note on a printout of an article about the suit that the case wasn’t related to any major financial crime. The article mentioned, however, that Motorola accused Hytera of hiring ex-Motorola employees after they had allegedly stolen thousands of pages of confidential documents. By early 2020, while Hytera was repaying the loan ICBC employees flagged a problem — Hytera had lost its U.S. case. In a briefing note to the bank’s credit committee at the end of April, they wrote that the verdict “confirms that Hytera engaged in illegal trade secret theft and copyright infringement, validating Motorola's global litigation against Hytera.” Following the U.S. court verdict ICBC London received an injunction from a British court ordering the bank to freeze Hytera assets, potentially stopping the repayment of the loan. Seven Hytera employees were later indicted for their alleged roles in the thefts from Motorola; one pleaded guilty in 2022 to charges of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and is awaiting sentencing. Hytera pleaded guilty in 2025 to “conspiracy to steal trade secrets” and was fined $50 million. Hytera was also ordered to pay Motorola more than $400 million in a separate lawsuit. In 2021, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission published a list of Chinese manufacturers, including Hytera, which “pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States.” The same year, the British government passed the National Security and Investment Act which gave heightened power to the government to proactively review acquisitions in 17 sensitive sectors, including communications. Hytera sold its entire shareholding in Sepura in July 2022. Read responses Responses Hytera: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In an email to ICIJ, Sepura said that "neither Sepura PLC nor its shareholders or management at the time were involved in Hytera’s choice of funding for its acquisition of Sepura” and that the company “had no customer relationship with ICBC and held no accounts with the bank” following the acquisition. It also said that it was not “a party to the litigation brought by Motorola against Hytera concerning Motorola’s intellectual property” and that “the technology at issue was distinct from that developed and used by Sepura in its own products”. “Sepura's proprietary technology and IPR were ring-fenced by statutory undertakings, as mandated and defined by the UK government and accepted by Hytera.” Sepura said it “has had no further interaction with Hytera since the sale” in 2022. ICBC:didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Borrower Project Shortway Ltd. (ultimately owned by Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.) Amount up to $57.1 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2017 From the China Capital files In their own words Handwritten note on an article: Not major financial crime issues relatedRisk Buying your backyard 04 ICBC participated in syndicated loans — financing provided by a group of lenders who share the risk — for a Chinese commercial real estate venture that went bust and defaulted on its loans, according to internal loan agreements and property assessments reviewed by ICIJ. In 2017, Chinese real estate tycoon Chen Hongtian and his wife bought two office towers in London’s trendy Canary Wharf commercial district, hoping to convert their $900 million investment into a profitable venture. ICBC London described the area as “one of the world’s premier commercial districts,” with “24 office buildings with around 200 shops, bars, and restaurants” according to a 2022 assessment of 5 Churchill Place’s value by the real estate company managing the asset. The real estate firm’s assessment came as the bank and other creditors looked to liquidate the assets of the embattled tycoon who had found himself short on cash and unable to make payments. By then, ICBC London Branch had committed $205 million out of roughly half a billion in loans made with other banks to Chen’s companies in the British Virgin Islands, through which he and his family owned the London properties. One of those properties, at 20 Canada Square, was mainly occupied by two Western firms, according to a 2022 ICBC internal credit report. But the properties couldn’t compete with more modern and energy-efficient real estate, and their value plummeted. By April 2023 ICBC London had reclassified the loan to Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., a BVI company through which Chen owned some units of the Canada Square property, as “non performing” and added the borrower to its watchlist. Around the same time that ICBC was reviewing the properties, the UK government passed the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act which required overseas entities that hold property in England and Wales to file beneficial ownership information with the company registry. A report published in 2017 by the U.S. Government Accountability Office warned that leasing space in foreign-owned buildings "could present security risks such as espionage and unauthorized cyber and physical access.” The UK’s National Security and Investment Act took effect in January 2022, but real estate was not among the sensitive sectors subject to its mandatory screening requirements for acquisitions. Read responses Responses Chen Hongtian/Cheung Kei group: The Cheung Kei group didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In statement posted on its website in 2023 the group said that “like all heavy asset holders”, it was “experiencing a phase of cash problems” and that its “overall asset scale and asset quality” were “very high, with a low debt ratio among peers.” At the time the group was “selling some equity in some assets and actively negotiating repayment arrangements with relevant financial institutions” and said it “believed that subsequent financial institution issues will be properly resolved.” ICBC London: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Jovial Link Holdings Ltd. for 5 Churchill Place; Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., Cheung Kwan Holdings Ltd. for 20 Canada Square (London properties) Start dates of loans 2022 Amount $61.7M / $143.5MTotal loan commitments From the China Capital files In their own words: About 5 Churchill Place, from a credit loan application: The deal as outlined herein offers ICBC London an ideal opportunity to assist an incoming Chinese client in the purchase of a major “trophy” asset that is both well let to tenants of significant covenant strengths and well located within the popular Canary Wharf developmentRisk Trapping In Debt 05 ICBC records on Zambia show a lender watching a borrower facing growing financial risks, while quietly putting protections in place for its own loans. ICBC financed a range of major projects in the country, providing loans for government-owned housing, a hospital, an airport and power projects running to hundreds of millions of dollars. Among them was a $285 million loan approved in 2010 to ZESCO, Zambia's state-owned power company, for two power transmission projects. Between 2015 and 2018, ICBC provided or participated in at least six more loans to ZESCO, totaling $1.2 billion according to AidData estimates, even as the bank was aware of mounting financial pressures on both Zambia and ZESCO. By 2017, a sovereign risk assessment in the bank's files described Zambia as facing limited financing options, rising interest costs, and substantial debt—and specifically pointed to financial pressures on ZESCO. Government net debt had climbed from 23% of GDP in 2013 to an estimated 57% in 2017, while debt costs consumed nearly a quarter of government revenue. ICBC had classified ZESCO as a high-risk client since 2018, citing Zambia's country risk, politically exposed persons and historical adverse media coverage including bribery and corruption allegations, according to a 2023 internal report. Despite these concerns, the bank continued its lending relationship with ZESCO, requiring annual reviews. ICBC built protections into its lending. ZESCO maintained a debt-service reserve account at ICBC London for repayments on the $285 million loan. Money deposited into the account could only be withdrawn by ICBC's head office, which was also the lender, agent and security trustee. ZESCO’s financial precarity triggered a cascade of credit problems. By March 2020, its failure to pay Maamba Collieries Ltd., a Zambian power supplier, had left Maamba unable to meet its own loan obligations to ICBC and other lenders. ICBC records show that lenders sent letters to Zambia's Ministry of Finance seeking government support, contacted Chinese state-owned insurer Sinosure and discussed restructuring the loan. ICBC officials warned that Maamba's loan would be classified as non-performing if payments remained overdue for more than 90 days. The documents offer a window into how the bank continued banking a financially strained borrower while using safeguards to limit its own losses. Read responses Responses ZESCO: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Zambian MOF: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower ZESCO Amount $285 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2011 From the China Capital files In their own words: The lenders have jointly sent two letters to Ministry of Finance (MOF), emphasizing the continuing non-payment by the ZESCO which may lead to Borrower’s default on the repayment of principal and interest, to seek support from MOF to solve this issue…Risk Contributors: Micael Pereira (Expresso); Scilla Alecci, Miguel Fiandor-Gutiérrez, Micah Reddy, Dean Starkman, Antonio Cucho Gamboa (ICIJ)

title: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic
zh_title: 欧洲与中国 1 – 中华人民共和国的到来
summary: 这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词的出现，世界已经站在了门口。
content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济正在快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词成为每次企业峰会的议程，世界已经来到了门口。为了重现这一转变，历史学家必须首先确定其背后的政治人物。即使天安门上的鲜血被冲洗干净——当未来的国家主席习近平的妻子、歌手彭丽媛为戒严部队唱小夜曲时——许多中国领导人知道他们犯了一个可怕的错误。其中包括习近平的父亲、两次被清洗的退伍军人习仲勋，他公开赞扬镇压“反革命暴乱”的“明智”和“坚决”决定，但私下里对经济改革的挫折表示哀悼。习仲勋亲自执掌南方经济强国广东，在20世纪80年代把它变成了吸引外资的世界工厂。他是影响 1989 年后中国下一届领导人选择的造王者之一。
这两名新面孔是从沿海贸易大都市上海走上来的。江泽民是上海共产党的领导人，也是一名受过苏联训练的工程师，后来成为国家主席和党的领导人。然而，关键人物却是一位名叫朱镕基的市长，他是一位出生于1928年、头脑敏锐的技术官僚。他先后担任央行行长和总理。天安门事件发生时，两人曾监督和平结束中国商业首都的大规模抗议活动。上海没有发生大屠杀。相反，朱在电视上发出严厉警告，当局则部署警察和民兵慢慢平息示威活动。上海很快就恢复了商业秩序。欧洲公司是浦东新金融区的第一批投资者。两位领导人不顾党内左派的强烈反对，决心让中国向世界经济开放。他们的活动可以通过日内瓦世贸组织的档案来追踪，这是谈判的宝贵指南。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.” Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit. To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder. They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform. Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989. The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister. The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong. Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. As early as 1986, China had applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), but the major trading powers had decided to transform the GATT into a new body that would govern services as well as trade from January 1, 1995. It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package. Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era. John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China. “How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked. The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996. Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001. The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal. The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought. The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. content:
这篇文章发表在《今日必读的一个故事》时事通讯中。在这里注册。十一天。斯卡拉穆奇一个。我的冰箱里有黄仁勋倒台前买的牛奶，我可能会倒一杯来纪念他的回归。回顾一下：黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞职，此前他被曝与一名被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍的女子有染，该女子将被禁运的英伟达芯片运送给中国人工智能公司。据称，黄还与一位高管有染，该高管是他在 Nvidia 的 60 名直接下属之一。辞职五天后，英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，该公司“不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官”。五天后，特朗普总统发帖表示他希望如此。今天早上，董事会援引“美国政府高层的意见”，一致投票决定让他回来。那么，在这种完全正常的公司治理情况下到底发生了什么？三种理论。理论一：金钱。英伟达是全球经济的引擎，在没有皮革老爹首席执行官的情况下，该公司股价较 10 月份的峰值下跌了约 40%，市值损失了数万亿美元。在宣布他复职的简单新闻稿后，该股上涨了 33%，而标准普尔 500 指数整体上涨了近 5%。员工们希望他回来。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 与其他近 20 万人一起签署了一份请愿书，要求他返回。
董事会——黄用了三十年的时间精心策划，其成员中没有一个成员曾对他说过不——屈服于金融逻辑。盖茨比回到了豪宅，人工智能派对又重新焕发了生机。理论 2：一致的激励。据《纽约时报》报道，总统大约一年前获悉黄与一名疑似中国间谍有牵连的情况。 5月份，在黄登上飞往北京的航班前不久，他在空军一号上再次听取了简报。不管怎样，特朗普还是把黄带到了一起。这是……一个有趣的选择。如果你想猜测为什么特朗普（呵呵）全力支持詹森，那就继续吧。但在黄以普通公民身份接受司法部和证券交易委员会调查的11天里，他是最危险的证人。他没有工作需要保护，没有董事会需要听从，个人生活支离破碎，并且有充分的理由做出自己的交易。处于该职位的人倾向于告诉调查人员他们所知道的每个人的情况。 [阅读：黄仁勋丑闻应该会改变一切]英伟达的激励措施也好不到哪儿去。在临时首席执行官和独立董事会的领导下，没有什么可以阻止公司公开文件和合作。从历史上看，司法部的政策对此给予了奖励。公司的律师-委托人特权由该公司的经营者控制。这 11 天里，黄仁勋都没有。但现在是了。黄回到房间，决定英伟达交出什么。
总法律顾问将于 12 月 2 日接受国会采访，再次向他汇报。黄的工作至少部分归功于总统的公开竞选。 （Semafor 报道称，特朗普还召集了 Nvidia 董事会会议，游说成员支持黄仁勋的回归。）就像这样，黄仁勋、Nvidia 和白宫都想要同样的事情。这并不一定意味着黄将在 12 月 1 日接受众议院外交事务、情报和中国特别委员会的闭门采访中接受第五次采访。现任首席执行官拒绝

【原文 English Original】
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. Eleven days. One Scaramucci. There’s milk in my refrigerator that was bought before Jensen Huang’s downfall, and I may pour a glass to mark his return. To review: Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after revelations that he’d had an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Huang allegedly also had an affair with an executive who was one of his 60 direct reports at Nvidia. Five days after the resignation, Nvidia’s board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company “ does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO .” Five days after that, President Trump posted that he hoped it would. This morning, citing “input from senior levels of the United States government,” the board voted unanimously to let him come back. So what’s actually going on in this totally normal corporate-governance situation? Three theories. Theory 1: Money. Nvidia is the engine of the global economy, and without its Leather Daddy CEO, the stock fell about 40 percent from its October peak, losing trillions in value. Following a simple press release announcing his reinstatement, the stock jumped 33 percent, while the overall S&P 500 rose almost 5 percent . Employees wanted him back. Elon Musk signed a petition along with almost 200,000 other people demanding his return. The board—which Huang spent three decades curating, and none of whose members has a history of telling him no—caved to the financial logic. Gatsby returns to the mansion and the AI party roars back to life. Theory 2: Aligned Incentives. The president was briefed about Huang’s involvement with a suspected Chinese spy about a year ago, according to The New York Times . He was briefed again in May, aboard Air Force One, shortly before Huang jumped aboard for a flight to Beijing. Trump brought Huang along anyway. That is … an interesting choice. If you want to speculate about why Trump was (heh) All-In on Jensen , go ahead. But during the 11 days that Huang was a private citizen under investigation by the Justice Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission, he was the most dangerous kind of witness there is. He had no job to protect, no board to answer to, a shattered personal life, and every reason to make his own deal. People in that position tend to tell investigators what they know, about everyone. [ Read: The Jensen Huang scandal should change everything ] Nvidia’s incentives were no better. Under an interim CEO and an independent board, there was nothing to keep the company from opening its files and cooperating. Justice Department policy, historically, rewards that. And a company’s attorney-client privilege is controlled by whoever runs that company. For 11 days, that wasn’t Jensen Huang. But now it is. Huang is back in the room deciding what Nvidia hands over. The general counsel, who sits for an interview with Congress on December 2, reports to him again. And Huang owes his job, at least in part, to the public campaigning of the president. ( Semafor reports that Trump also called into the Nvidia board meeting to lobby members for Huang’s return.) Just like that, Huang, Nvidia, and the White House all want the same thing. That doesn’t necessarily mean Huang will take the Fifth in his December 1 closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees. A sitting CEO who refuses to answer questions is a disaster for his company. In civil cases, silence can be held against him and against the corporation, and the fastest way to wipe out Nvidia’s stock rebound would be for Huang to invoke his right against self-incrimination over and over. Being CEO also makes him the custodian of Nvidia’s records, and under the Supreme Court’s Braswell rule, a person running a company can’t hide behind the Fifth to avoid handing them over. Theory 3: Nothing Matters. A few years ago, every single action in this story would have been a colossal scandal. A CEO resigns over a relationship with a suspected spy. The president, who was reportedly warned about it, campaigns for his return. The board, which said it wouldn’t reinstate him, suddenly reinstates him. To be clear, I suspect that all of this matters quite a bit. But the bet being placed here—by Huang and Trump, by Nvidia’s board, and by the investors pumping up the stock value—is that it doesn’t: that the investigators will wander off, that Congress will take its transcribed interview and move on. Maybe a 33 percent pop settles everything—or maybe executive privilege does. That’s a wild risk. But it’s being taken by people for whom a wild risk may be the last, best strategy left. My glass of milk is just fine. Based on today’s insanity, I suspect they know theirs is spoiled.

Tad DeHaven 11 月 12 日，特朗普总统表示，英伟达“只有一个人”取代黄仁勋。他指的是苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克。 11 天后，英伟达宣布黄仁勋复职，特朗普对 CNBC 表示，“我做了这笔交易。”  为什么总统要达成这样的协议？黄在承认与一名涉嫌与中国情报部门有联系的女性有染后辞职。两位英伟达股东敦促董事会对让他回归持开放态度。一名英伟达员工建立了一个网站，人们可以在上面签署一封呼吁他回归的信。股东和员工完全有权向董事们提出自己的理由，而董事们在 11 月 17 日告诉投资者，他们无意恢复黄的职位。英伟达董事会也有充分的理由询问联邦官员对可疑情报行动的了解。根据董事会的声明，政府的回答缓解了他们对国家安全的担忧。他们还会见了黄，并表示他们对他能够领导公司感到满意，尽管他们自己的调查仍在进行中。但特朗普向他们施压，要求他们恢复黄的职位，从而越界了。任何仍然认为让黄回来是一个错误的董事都被迫权衡英伟达违抗总统可能付出的代价。这让人有理由怀疑英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的决定是否真的正确。如果董事会的内部调查发现更多涉及黄的令人不安的信息，会发生什么？
特朗普宣称其复职对美国繁荣至关重要，它会不愿意对这位首席执行官采取行动吗？当 CNBC 的萨拉·艾森问特朗普他的底线在哪里时，他回答说：“我是为了国家而这样做。”用特朗普的话说，美国的繁荣取决于黄仁勋掌管英伟达。难怪吉姆·克莱默在同一次电话会议上询问，如果该公司陷入财务困境，华盛顿是否会提供援助。特朗普表示，他认为事情不会发展到这个地步，但他正在回答有关一家上季度盈利 653 亿美元的公司的救助问题。我们已经看到，当华盛顿认定一家公司太重要而不能倒闭时，董事会会发生什么。 2009年，通用汽车依靠联邦救助维持生存，奥巴马政府罢免了首席执行官里克·瓦格纳，并任命了他的继任者弗里茨·亨德森。亨德森后来告诉调查人员，通用汽车的董事认为财政部篡夺了他们选择首席执行官的权力。美国政府已经对英伟达的业务拥有足够的发言权，可以要求削减对中国的某些芯片销售。下次特朗普向黄求助时，他可以提醒黄是谁帮助他重新获得了工作。正如我的同事斯科特·林西科姆 (Scott Lincicome) 今天指出的那样，这种干预的经济成本比周一英伟达股价的上涨更难以看出。以英特尔为例。 2025 年 8 月，特朗普因首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 与中国的关系而要求他辞职。

【原文 English Original】
Tad DeHaven On November 12, President Trump said there was “only one man” to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia. He meant former Apple CEO Tim Cook. Eleven days later, Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement, and Trump told CNBC , “I made the deal.”  Why was that the president’s deal to make? Huang resigned after acknowledging an affair with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Two Nvidia shareholders urged the board to keep an open mind about bringing him back. An Nvidia employee set up a website where people could sign a letter calling for his return. Shareholders and employees had every right to make their case to the directors, who had told investors on November 17 that they had no intention of reinstating Huang. Nvidia’s board also had good reason to ask federal officials what they knew about the suspected intelligence operation. The government’s answer eased their national security concerns, according to the board’s statement . They also met with Huang and said they were satisfied that he could lead the company, though their own investigation remains open.  But Trump crossed the line by pressuring them to reinstate Huang. Any director who still thought it was a mistake to bring back Huang was forced to weigh what it might cost Nvidia to defy the president. That makes it fair to wonder whether Nvidia’s board was truly kosher with reinstating Huang. What happens if the board’s internal investigation turns up more troubling information involving Huang? Will it be reluctant to act against a CEO whose reinstatement Trump declared essential to American prosperity?  When CNBC’s Sara Eisen asked Trump where he drew the line, he replied, “I’m doing it for the country.” In Trump’s telling , American prosperity depends on having Huang at the helm of Nvidia. Little wonder that Jim Cramer asked on the same call whether Washington would come to the company’s aid if it got into financial trouble. Trump said he didn’t think it would come to that, but here he was fielding a bailout question about a company that earned $65.3 billion last quarter. We’ve seen what happens to a board when Washington decides a company is too important to fail. In 2009, while General Motors depended on a federal bailout to stay afloat, the Obama administration ousted CEO Rick Wagoner and appointed his successor, Fritz Henderson. Henderson later told investigators that GM’s directors felt Treasury had usurped their authority to choose the CEO. The administration already has enough say over Nvidia’s business to claim a cut of certain chip sales to China. And the next time Trump asks Huang for a favor, he can remind him who helped get him his job back. As my colleague Scott Lincicome pointed out today , the economic costs of this kind of interference are harder to see than Monday’s jump in Nvidia’s share price.  Take Intel . In August 2025, Trump called on CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over Tan’s ties to China. Tan scurried to the White House, where Trump says he told him , “If you’re smart, give the United States of America 10 percent of your company.” Tan kept his job, and the federal government became an Intel shareholder.  That same month, Tim Cook went to the White House seeking a tariff exemption for Apple. As Scott has documented , Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly pressed Cook to have Intel make some of Apple’s chips. Apple got its exemption. Ten months later, Trump took credit for what he described as a deal between Apple and Intel. “We want capital flowing to companies for commercial reasons,” Scott told the New York Times . Good luck with that when the president is out recruiting customers for a company in the federal portfolio . “Investors have grown accustomed to President Trump influencing the prospects of different companies, whether it’s rare earth metals, energy, and chips,” JoAnne Feeney, a portfolio manager at Advisors Capital Management, told Bloomberg . “It certainly has made investing more complicated because it has to be factored into which stocks you choose to hold. It’s not the way the US capitalistic system is designed.” No, it’s not .  Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 about chip exports. Congress is already asking the administration which officials weighed in with Nvidia’s board and what they said to get Huang reinstated.  But Congress ought to keep Nvidia in mind as it considers the Senate’s defense authorization bill . Section 1051 would let the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital buy stakes in suppliers of critical minerals and other materials while barring its director from taking a board seat or obtaining other voting representation. Trump didn’t need a seat on Nvidia’s board to get its directors on the phone. Now imagine taking that call when the federal government is also one of your largest shareholders.

title: Hong Kong man jailed for life for murdering yoga instructor ex-girlfriend in luxury hotel
zh_title: 香港男子在豪华酒店谋杀瑜伽教练前女友被判终身监禁
summary: 一名香港男子因四年前在豪华酒店房间内刺死瑜伽教练前女友而被判处终身监禁。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，32 岁的亚历克斯·罗 (Alex Lo) 在高等法院被判处无期徒刑，一天前，由五男两女组成的七名陪审团一致判定犯有谋杀罪。他被判于2022年6月29日至30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。在一封缓解信中，罗向周、她的母亲和朋友道歉，并说
content:
一名香港男子因四年前在豪华酒店房间内刺死瑜伽教练前女友而被判处终身监禁。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，32 岁的亚历克斯·罗 (Alex Lo) 在高等法院被判处无期徒刑，一天前，由五男两女组成的七名陪审团一致判定犯有谋杀罪。他被判于2022年6月29日至30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。据法庭新闻媒体《见证人》报道，罗在一封缓刑信中向周、她的母亲和朋友道歉，并表示他只是不认罪，并根据一位未透露姓名的律师的建议接受审判。 “如果定刑20年、30年监禁，我相信我最早就会认罪，”他用中文写道。根据香港法律，被判犯有谋杀罪的成年人将面临强制性终身监禁，认罪后不得减刑。罗说，他从未希望公开披露他与周的关系细节，并补充说她是他“最心爱的女人”。 “我在这段感情中用了错误的方式去爱，我愿意承担后果，”他写道。然而，法官郭定邦认为，罗只表现出了轻微的悔恨，并指出他试图让陪审团相信他的行为源于“盲目的爱情”以及与周的财务纠纷。
法官表示，罗刺伤周是出于愤怒、仇恨和嫉妒，“也许根本与爱无关。”法官补充说，如果他真的爱她，他应该饶她一命。Aqua Chow。照片：yoga.aqua，来自 Instagram。法官援引政府法医病理学家Gary Ying的证词指出，周身上有43处刀伤，最深达15厘米。法官称，被告将周放在浴缸里，并在离开酒店前换了衣服，称他的行为冷静且深思熟虑。法官表示，他在审讯期间也没有说出真相，而是声称自己在周女士的挑衅下刺伤了周女士，以减轻自己的罪行。周去世时年仅23岁。 2022 年 6 月 30 日，她的尸体在酒店浴缸中被发现，当时她原定飞往美国参加瑜伽培训课程。法庭在庭审中获悉，罗与周于 2021 年 2 月成为情侣，并于次年 1 月分手，但仍保持联系。罗作证称，他带周女士去高档餐厅并为她购买奢侈品而欠下了巨额债务，并表示他非常爱她。他说，债务让他产生了自杀念头，因为贷款公司追着他还钱。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong man has been sentenced to life behind bars for murdering his yoga instructor ex-girlfriend by stabbing her inside a luxury hotel room four years ago. The High Court. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Alex Lo, 32, was given life imprisonment at the High Court on Friday, a day after being unanimously found guilty of murder by a seven-member jury comprising five men and two women. He was convicted of murdering yoga instructor Aqua Chow between June 29 and June 30, 2022, at the Ritz-Carlton in West Kowloon. In a mitigation letter, Lo apologised to Chow, her mother and friends, and said that he only pleaded not guilty and stood trial on the advice of an unnamed lawyer, according to court news outlet The Witness. “If there were a fixed penalty of 20 or 30 years in jail, I believe I would have pleaded guilty at the earliest stage,” he wrote in Chinese. Under Hong Kong law, adults convicted of murder face mandatory life imprisonment, with no sentencing discount for pleading guilty. Lo said he had never hoped to publicly disclose the details of his relationship with Chow, adding that she was his “most beloved woman.” “I used the wrong way to love in this relationship and I am willing to bear the consequences,” he wrote. Judge Anthony Kwok, however, found that Lo only demonstrated slight remorse, noting he sought to convince the jury that his actions stemmed from “blind love” and financial disputes with Chow. The judge said Lo stabbed Chow out of anger, hatred, and jealousy, and “perhaps it was nothing about love at all.” If he really loved her, the judge added, he should have spared her life. Aqua Chow. Photo: yoga.aqua, via Instagram. Citing testimony from government forensic pathologist Gary Ying, the judge noted that Chow had sustained 43 knife wounds, with the deepest reaching 15 centimetres. The defendant placed Chow inside a bathtub and changed his clothes before leaving the hotel, the judge said, calling his actions calm and deliberate. He also did not tell the truth during the trial, instead claiming that he stabbed Chow after being provoked by her in a bid to lessen his offence, the judge said. Chow was 23 when she died. She had been scheduled to fly to the US for a yoga training course when her body was found in the hotel bathtub on June 30, 2022. The court heard during the trial that Lo and Chow became a couple in February 2021 and broke up the following January, although they stayed in touch. Lo testified that he had run up enormous debt taking Chow to high-end restaurants and purchasing luxury items for her, saying he loved her very much. The debt left him suicidal, he said, as loan companies chased him to repay the money.

This is the third of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe.   The negative numbers began to cascade across European balance sheets as soon as China entered the World Trade Organization in late 2001.   But the cost-benefit calculations were not equal for all Europeans. Some nations, such as Germany, initially gained from high-value exports and joint ventures. Others, like Greece and Portugal, faced a surge of low-cost Chinese goods and strategic investments by entities linked to the Chinese state.  The Chinese economy was barely one-eighth the size of that of the European Economic Community before the People’s Republic embarked on its policy of “reform and opening up” at the Third Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in December 1978. By 2025, the relative economic weight of China and the European Union was almost equal. Together they account for about a third of world trade. In 1975, their bilateral trade was worth about €2bn ($2.2bn) annually; 50 years later, it was €2bn a day , according to figures compiled for the Institut Jacques Delors.   By any measure, it should have been a success story. But the two were not playing on the same field. State subsidies in China, ranging from concessionary land deals to direct financial aid and favorable local taxation, handed Chinese firms a competitive advantage which added to their low labor costs. A thicket of protectionist rules and non-tariff barriers to entry frustrated foreign enterprises and channeled investment into joint ventures tied, inevitably, to forced technology transfer.   The EU trade deficits with China climbed remorselessly, from €39.6bn in 2001 to peak at €397bn in 2022 after the Covid-19 pandemic, before settling above €350bn annually. While the EU maintains a surplus in services, it is only in the tens of billions.   Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. New infrastructure accelerated the flow of exports. While Chinese goods had to be shipped or flown to the United States, they could be loaded onto trains to Europe, cutting the transit time from more than a month to less than two weeks, avoiding bottlenecks and crisis points. Traffic on the railway link multiplied almost tenfold in the last decade.  At the same time, China’s leaders redirected their own investments abroad from buying fixed assets, like ports and factories, into new plants built to get around tariffs on electric vehicles and similar items. The Communist Party encouraged rapid growth in research and development, no longer content to copy and to sell. It meant to originate and to own the value in new products.  China’s patent filings now dwarf those by the EU, its universities regularly outrank their European counterparts, and Chinese academics lead the world in scientific publications. In short, a juggernaut was coming for the workplaces and welfare systems of Europe. The response has been episodic and ineffective.  In 2003, the European Commission declined to recognize China as a market economy, prompting ire in Beijing. The next year, the two made a customs co-operation agreement and pursued “dialogues” on tricky subjects like intellectual property and industrial policy.   A decade later, the EU changed its anti-dumping regulations to stay compliant with its WTO obligations but still refused to define China’s economy as playing by market rules. By then, Xi Jinping was settled in power, having taken all the great offices of the Chinese system between 2012 and 2013. Xi encouraged engagement on big-picture issues like climate change, but his focus on exports and technology acquisition was relentless. Meanwhile, waves of repression inside China created political barriers, notably to a bilateral agreement on investment which foundered amid strident criticism in Europe of the human rights abuses against the Uyghur Muslim minority in the far west of China. Such protests were never likely to move the Chinese leader. They merely encouraged him to grow economic ties with Russia and countries in what China was soon calling the “Global South.” The Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, followed by EU economic sanctions, deepened the dependency between Moscow and Beijing.   Their bilateral trade almost doubled as Russian oil and gas fueled Chinese factories and Chinese-made electric cars poured into the Russian market.  European leaders found that the political climate turned hawkish; Europe found itself caught between trade wars, a new strain of assertiveness in Chinese politics and the search for a balance between co-operation and rivalry, both between China and the West and within the EU. The Chinese decision starting in April 2025 to restrict exports of rare earths, valuable minerals for manufacturing everything from catalytic exhausts to pharmaceuticals, in reprisal for President Donald Trump’s tariffs, shocked business and political elites.  The “second China shock” has hollowed out the German industrial belts, forcing Berlin to move closer to the French preference for tariffs and barriers. By some counts in the German media, the country is losing more than 10,000 industrial jobs a month, fueling support for the right-wing AFD party, while France is struggling with its public debts.  In October, the two nations submerged their differences to write to the European Commission, urging it to use the trade weapon against competitors who exploited state subsidies and undervalued currency to destroy their rivals. There is also talk of diversifying supply chains and a “buy Europe” policy. The letter did not name names, but everyone knew the target was China. The proposed “second strike” capacity aimed at imposing duties on countries that retaliate when the EU imposes trade measures is an escalatory step that has uncomfortable echoes of nuclear deterrence doctrine. In Beijing, the Ministry of Commerce is unsheathing its own weapons and already talks of countries harming themselves by “wrong steps.”   The scene is set for a showdown of some kind. It is a far cry from the hopes of 2001.  Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese.   Europe’s Edge  is CEPA’s online journal covering critical topics on the foreign policy docket across Europe and North America. title: Trump defends ‘fantastic’ ties with Xi, Putin after summit backlash
zh_title: 峰会遭到强烈反对后，特朗普捍卫与习近平和普京的“出色”关系
summary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五为他与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京的“重要”峰会进行了辩护，因为他从中国回国，面临中期选举后的严厉批评和动荡。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 20 日在华盛顿特区的白宫詹姆斯·S·布雷迪新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/法新社。回国后的第二天，特朗普在白宫举行的新闻发布会上表示，他与中国和俄罗斯领导人的“良好关系”有助于确保美国的安全。特朗普部分
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五为他与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京的“重要”峰会进行了辩护，因为他从中国回国，面临中期选举后的严厉批评和动荡。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 20 日在华盛顿特区的白宫詹姆斯·S·布雷迪新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/法新社。回国后的第二天，特朗普在白宫举行的新闻发布会上表示，他与中国和俄罗斯领导人的“良好关系”有助于确保美国的安全。当他们在深圳会面时，特朗普有争议地称普京为“我的朋友”，之后特朗普特别捍卫了他与普京的关系，并坚称克里姆林宫老板真心希望结束俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。特朗普对记者说：“我们举行了多年来最重要的国际峰会之一。”他补充说，世界主要核大国领导人之间存在“巨大的电力”。 “我与普京的关系非常好。这是一件非常好的事情。我与习主席的关系非常好。
这是一件好事，我们的国家因此而安全。”不过，特朗普补充说，他不确定无核化——美国总统称无核化是中国峰会的主要议题之一——“能够实现”。这位80岁的老人在白宫讲台上的两侧是副总统万斯和国务卿马可·鲁比奥，五角大楼负责人皮特·赫格斯和财政部长斯科特·贝森特坐在附近。在美国媒体和他的民主党对手嘲笑这次峰会只不过是给跛脚鸭总统拍照的机会之后，特朗普试图宣扬这次峰会的成就，此举“令人尴尬”。在本月早些时候美国中期选举惨败后，他抵达亚洲寻求胜利，伊朗战争仍在继续，白宫面临即将上任的民主党领导的国会的多项调查。 2025 年 10 月 30 日，中国国家主席习近平在韩国釜山金海国际机场航站楼出席中美双边会议。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。但特朗普-习近平-普京的会议几乎没有产生什么具体成果，除了特朗普在新闻发布会上在画架上展示的简短的“和平宣言”，其中没有提到伊朗或乌克兰。众议院民主党党鞭凯瑟琳·克拉克 (Katherine Clark) 在 X 节目上表示：“特朗普在世界舞台上令人尴尬。”“没有什么可以结束他的伊朗战争。对乌克兰没有任何帮助。没有任何关于人工智能安全的内容。
相反，他只是痴迷于独裁者。”美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 表示，这次会议对特朗普来说只不过是“一次恰逢其时的合影”，但对习近平和普京来说，这“证明了他们的愿景，即世界正在经历根本性的权力再平衡”。毫不奇怪，特朗普在长达一小时零二十八分钟的新闻发布会上花了大部分时间来反驳对与华盛顿主要对手的独裁领导人会面的批评。他说，在与普京的双边会晤中，这位俄罗斯领导人“明确表达了他希望看到通过外交手段结束乌克兰战争的愿望”。当被问及是否认为普京是美国的朋友时，特朗普表示“我无法与美国交谈”，但补充说，他们“非常良好的关系……给了我们很多额外的力量”。与此同时，特朗普猛烈抨击“失控”的国际刑事法院，并表示普京对国际刑事法庭并不满意，该法庭已向俄罗斯发出逮捕令。

【原文 English Original】
US President Donald Trump on Friday defended his “momentous” summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as he returned home from China to face bitter criticism and turmoil after the midterm elections. U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during a news briefing in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on November 20, 2026 in Washington, DC. Photo: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/AFP. Speaking at a news conference in the White House the day after flying back, Trump said his “fantastic relationships” with the Chinese and Russian leaders helped keep the United States secure. Trump particularly defended his ties to Putin after controversially calling him “my friend” when they met in Shenzhen — and insisted that the Kremlin boss genuinely wanted to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. “We had one of the most momentous international summits in many years,” Trump told reporters, adding that there was “great electricity” between the leaders of the world’s main nuclear powers. “I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That’s a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That’s a good thing, and our country is safe because of that.” Trump however added that he was unsure whether denuclearization — which the US president said was one of the main topics of the summit in China — “can ever happen.” The 80-year-old was flanked at the White House podium by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sat nearby. ‘Embarrassment’ Trump’s bid to tout the achievements of the summit came after US media and his Democratic opponents mocked it as little more than a photo opportunity for a lame-duck president. He arrived in Asia seeking a win after a bruising defeat in US midterm elections earlier this month, with the Iran war grinding on and the White House facing multiple investigations by the incoming Democratic-led Congress. Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a China-US bilateral meeting at the Gimhae International Airport terminal, in Busan, South Korea, on October 30, 2025. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. But the Trump-Xi-Putin powwow produced few concrete results except a brief “Declaration toward Peace” — which Trump displayed on an easel during his news conference — that made no mention of Iran or Ukraine. “Trump is an embarrassment on the world stage,” House Democratic whip Katherine Clark said on X. “Nothing to end his Iran war. Nothing to help Ukraine. Nothing about AI safety. Instead, he’s just obsessing over dictators.” Broadcaster CNN said the meeting was little more than “a well-timed photo-op” for Trump — but for Xi and Putin it was a “vindication of their vision that the world is undergoing a fundamental rebalancing of power.” It was no surprise then that Trump spent much of the one hour and 28 minute press conference pushing back at criticism for meeting the autocratic leaders of Washington’s main adversaries. He said that during a bilateral meeting with Putin, the Russian leader “clearly expressed his desire to see the war in Ukraine end by diplomatic means.” Asked if he believed Putin was a friend to America, Trump said “I can’t speak to America” but added that their “very good relationship… gives us a lot of additional strength.” ‘Out of control’ Trump meanwhile lashed out at the “out of control” International Criminal Court and said that Putin wasn’t “happy” with the tribunal, which has issued an arrest warrant for the Russian leader over the Ukraine war. Vladimir Putin. File photo: Wikicommons. On Iran, Trump accused Iran of “bullshitting for 51 years” and said Tehran’s leaders “want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me.” Trump was also full of praise for Communist Party leader Xi over the clean and futuristic streets of Shenzhen, comparing it favorably with what he said were run-down, Democratic-led cities in the United States. But the Republican president struck an unusually conciliatory tone towards the Democrats, despite them threatening him with multiple investigations when they take control of Congress next year. Trump suggested he was ready to work with Congress on healthcare, the entertainment industry and possibly on migration — though said he was also ready to veto legislation if needed.
