summary: 2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机
content:
2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯同一地区的日本领空。飞机穿过对马海峡，在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后进入菲律宾海。作为回应，日本航空自卫队西部防空司令部的日本航空自卫队战斗机紧急紧急升空。日本飞机向可疑的俄罗斯飞机发出了通知和警告。日本飞机无法看到俄罗斯飞机，也无法目视确认进入该空域的飞机类型。
会议记录显示，小泉纯一郎表示：“虽然很难明确说明俄罗斯飞机这次行动背后的意图或目的，但无论如何，防卫省和自卫队将继续高度关注俄罗斯的军事行动，并将采取一切可能措施，确保对领空侵犯保持警惕、监视和适当反应。”不仅侵犯了日本的主权，而且对日本的安全构成了威胁。小泉表示，日本政府已通过外交渠道向俄罗斯政府提出抗议，要求类似事件不再重演。俄罗斯飞机周四进入日本、韩国和台湾的防空识别区（ADIZ）。防空识别区始于主权空域结束处，是一段确定的国际空域，为了国家安全利益，在其中检测和跟踪飞机。战斗机经常紧急起飞拦截和跟踪外国飞机，直到其离开防空识别区。虽然国际法不承认，但许多国家都设有防空识别区，因为领空距离一个国家的海岸线仅延伸 12 海里。这三个国家没有确认这架俄罗斯飞机的身份。
据当地航空观察员称，当天晚些时候，两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 IL-76 运输机降落在越南岘港国际机场。岘港的一个社区社交媒体页面发布了轰炸机抵达的照片以及停在机场的四架俄罗斯飞机的视频。截至发稿时，俄罗斯和越南均已就越南境内出现轰炸机问题发表官方声明。日本军队于 2026 年 6 月 27 日拍摄到一架俄罗斯 Tu-95 轰炸机。日本联合参谋部照片 2015年，路透社报道称，美国已要求越南停止允许俄罗斯加油机使用金兰湾。据报道，这些加油机被用来为在关岛附近进行挑衅性飞行的俄罗斯轰炸机加油。俄罗斯轰炸机最后一次部署到东南亚是在 2017 年 12 月 5 日，当时两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 Il-76 运输机降落在印度尼西亚比亚克岛。印尼空军表示，此次访问的目的是

【原文 English Original】
Flight path of the suspect Russian aircraft on Nov. 12, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map Suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace twice on Thursdays, prompting fighter aircraft to be scrambled in response, Japan’s Defense Minister announced Tuesday. Between 4:07 and 4:10 a.m. on Thursday, one suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, which lies in the East China Sea, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in his regularly scheduled Tuesday press conference. Subsequently, between 4:09 and 4:12 a.m., a second suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace in the same area. The aircraft passed through the Tsushima Strait, flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan, and proceeded into the Philippine Sea. Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft from the JASDF’s Western Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. The Japanese aircraft issued notifications and warnings to the suspected Russian aircraft. Japan’s aircraft were unable to see the Russian aircraft and visually confirm the type of aircraft that entered the airspace. “Whilst it is difficult to state with certainty the intent or purpose behind the Russian aircraft’s actions on this occasion, the Ministry of Defense and the Self-Defense Forces will, in any case, continue to monitor Russia’s military movements with the utmost attention and will take every possible measure to ensure vigilance, surveillance and appropriate responses to airspace violations,” said Koizumi, according to a transcript of the conference . Koizumi called the violation of Japan’s territorial airspace by Russian aircraft not only a serious infringement of Japan’s sovereignty but also a threat to Japan’s security. The Japanese government has lodged a protest with the Russian government through diplomatic channels and demanded that such incidents not be repeated, Koizumi said. The Russian aircraft entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Thursday. An ADIZ begins where sovereign airspace ends and is a defined stretch of international airspace in which aircraft are detected and tracked in the interest of national security. Fighter aircraft are often scrambled to intercept and shadow the foreign aircraft until it leaves the ADIZ. While not recognized under international law, a number of countries have ADIZs because territorial airspace extends just 12 nautical miles from a country’s coastline. The three countries did not identify the Russian aircraft. Two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports landed at Da Nang International Airport, Vietnam, later that day, according to local aviation spotters. A Da Nang-based community social media page posted photos of the bombers arriving and videos of the four Russian aircraft parked at the airport. Russia nor Vietnam, as of publication, have issued official statements on the presence of the bombers in Vietnam. A Russian Tu-95 bomber photographed June 27, 2026, by Japanese forces. Japan Joint Staff Office photo In 2015, Reuters reported that the U.S. had requested Vietnam to stop allowing Russian tanker aircraft to use Cam Ranh Bay. The tankers were reportedly being used to refuel Russian bombers that conducted provocative flights near Guam. The last known Russian bomber deployment to Southeast Asia was on Dec. 5, 2017, when two Tu-95MS bombers and two Il-76 transports landed on Biak Island, Indonesia. The Indonesian Air Force said that the visit was for a navigation exercise. The Russian Defense Ministry said at the time that the bombers were refuelled in the air by Ilyushin Il-78 tankers over the Pacific Ocean. The last time a Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace was on Sept. 23, 2024 , when a Russian IL-38 Maritime Patrol Aircraft violated Japan’s territorial airspace three times north of Rebun Island. The Defense Minister Minoru Kihara said at the time that JASDF F-15J and F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft were scrambled and discharged flares after the Russian aircraft appeared to have ignored the warnings issued. The incident was the first time Japan had released flares against foreign aircraft.

通过提前付款，高市政府计划保障国际刑事法院从 2027 年 4 月开始的下一财年的资金支持，并在美国制裁生效时解决任何资金短缺问题。

International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane meets with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the Prime Minister's Office in Tokyo on Tuesday. | Pool / via AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has moved forward Japan’s financial contribution to the International Criminal Court, ICC President Tomoko Akane said Tuesday after her first meeting with Takaichi since the U.S. announced sanctions on Akane in August.
With the early payment, the Takaichi administration plans to safeguard the ICC’s funding for the next fiscal year, starting April 2027, and address any shortfall if U.S. sanctions take effect.
Japan currently contributes the largest share among ICC members toward the court’s budget, equating to approximately ¥4.6 billion out of a roughly ¥34.5 billion budget.

title: 抗中滲透升級 立委修法：鼓吹武統最高罰100萬
summary: 【大紀元2026年11月24日訊】（大紀元記者吳旻洲台灣台北報導）中共近年對台滲透、認知戰、跨國鎮壓等行徑日益猖獗，立委王定宇、林楚茵等16人提出《國安法》、《反滲透法》修法。除提高相關刑責，也擬明定公開鼓吹武統台灣者最高可罰100萬元，相關網路內容情節重大可「封網」；軍公教等人員涉犯國安相關罪行判刑者，暫發半數退休金。 提案內容提到，中共近年在我國境內實施的跨國鎮壓（Transnational Repression），手法從過往的跟監、恐嚇脅迫，逐漸轉變為具體的騷擾或攻擊行
content:
【大紀元2026年11月24日訊】（大紀元記者吳旻洲台灣台北報導）中共近年對台滲透、認知戰、跨國鎮壓等行徑日益猖獗，立委王定宇、林楚茵等16人提出《國安法》、《反滲透法》修法。除提高相關刑責，也擬明定公開鼓吹武統台灣者最高可罰100萬元，相關網路內容情節重大可「封網」；軍公教等人員涉犯國安相關罪行判刑者，暫發半數退休金。
提案內容提到，中共近年在我國境內實施的跨國鎮壓（Transnational Repression），手法從過往的跟監、恐嚇脅迫，逐漸轉變為具體的騷擾或攻擊行為，相關案件也急遽增加，包含指使境外及在台協力者，監視、跟拍我特定國人，意圖取得隱私資訊，做為威脅籌碼；或冒用反中人士名義寄送恐嚇郵件，謀詆毀鎮壓對象名譽，甚至製造肢體衝突、潑漆討債、假車禍等事故，冀以暴力威嚇行動，使人心生畏懼，引發寒蟬效應。
提案還指出，檢警調在偵辦相關類案件時，引用《刑法》妨害社會秩序罪，並依《反滲透法》相關規定加重其刑至二分之一，不僅刑度偏低，針對在台協力者之不法行為樣態，目前反滲透法相關規範不足因應。
王定宇等人提出《反滲透法》修正草案，針對刑責作出三大調整，首先針對受滲透來源教唆、幫助或共同違法捐贈政治獻金、公投經費，或從事《總統與公職人員選舉罷免法》禁止的助選行為，從現行處5年以下有期徒刑，提高至「3年以上、7年以下有期徒刑」，得併科新台幣1000萬元以下罰金，增設3年最低刑度門檻。
其次是加重國安機密遊說刑責，受滲透來源教唆、幫助或共同就國防、外交及大陸事務涉及國家安全或機密進行遊說者，從現行處3年以下有期徒刑，調整為1年以上、5年以下有期徒刑；此外，還擴大在台協力者加重處罰範圍，草案大幅擴張適用範圍至《刑法》第二編分則各章、《跟蹤騷擾防制法》等。
至於《國家安全法》部分，草案明定，任何人不得公開鼓吹、倡議或支持外國、大陸、港澳或境外敵對勢力對台灣發動戰爭，或採取非和平手段消滅我國主權，經內政部會商法務部、陸委會等機關認定違反規定者，處10萬元以上、100萬元以下罰鍰。
若公開網路內容涉及鼓吹戰爭，或公開散布錯假訊息、為大陸從事具有政治目的的宣傳，而有危害國安或社會、財政、經濟安定之虞，內政部會商數位發展部、陸委會等機關後，得命網路平台或服務提供者限制瀏覽、移除內容或限制帳號服務；情節重大或情況急迫時，得逕令網際網路接取服務提供者停止解析或限制接取（封網）。
平台業者無正當理由不遵行命令，可處10萬元以上、100萬元以下罰鍰，並按次處罰；未依法保留使用者資料180日者，處6萬元以上、60萬元以下罰鍰。
草案也增訂「參與組織罪」，禁止參與受大陸、港澳或境外敵對勢力控制，且足以危害國家安全或社會安定的組織；為上述勢力或其所設立、實質控制的組織、機構、團體或其派遣之人犯國安法之罪者，以及故意犯國安法之罪的現役軍人、公務員，均加重其刑至二分之一。
退休金部分，軍公教及公營機關人員若犯《國安法》、《反滲透法》或內亂、外患等罪，經法院任一審級判處有期徒刑以上之刑，自宣示判決日起暫停發給50%退休（職、伍）給與，待有罪判決確定後全數剝奪並追繳已支領款項，領受撫卹金或遺屬年金的遺族也適用。◇

content:
【大紀元2026年11月24日訊】中華民國2026年「九合一」大選將於11月28日投票，選戰進入最後倒數，中共對台介選手段持續升級。近日，總統賴清德為基隆市長候選人童子瑋助選時，一度眼眶泛淚，他表示，大家不用擔心，他會把台灣給顧好，絕對不接受共產黨統治。
11月22日晚上7時，民進黨基隆市長候選人童子瑋在基隆國門廣場舉辦大型造勢活動。前總統蔡英文、總統賴清德、前基隆市長林右昌及民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋等人接力站台助選。
當晚9時許，賴清德作壓軸講話，除了回顧基隆近年來的城市轉變，更感性談起自己30年前棄醫從政的心路歷程，過程中一度眼眶泛淚，情緒激動。
賴清德表示，30年前，台灣民主運動的前輩一次又一次前往成大醫院，邀請他投入國民大會代表選舉，讓原本立志行醫的他，最終選擇走上政治這條路。
賴清德說，「我從小就想當醫生，但看到台灣的需要，我勇敢站出來，承擔國家的責任。」
他激動地向台下支持者喊話，「大家不用擔心，我會勇敢堅強，把台灣給顧好，絕對不接受共產黨統治，絕對會把台灣民主繼續深化。」
賴總統： 堅決拒絕接受中國共產黨！ https://t.co/6Mh1kHuP0W
— XKC@軒愷 (@gooddaykpc) November 22, 2026
視頻在X等社交媒體上熱傳。不少使用簡體中文的網民留言：「堅決支持。我們都是中華民國的子民。」
「有共產黨的地方就沒好的，只有被中共洗腦下的中國人會支持中共，這也不怪他們，（中共）洗腦系統太成熟了。」
「中國民眾，羨慕台灣和台灣民眾。共產黨踏進台灣，所有人敢想嗎？以為是新疆集中營？」
「台灣是中共的一個變數，而這個變數使中共走向死亡。」
台灣自1996年首次總統直選以來，中共介入台灣選舉的手段不斷演變，從早期的軍事威嚇、政治施壓與經濟利誘，逐步擴展至境外資金滲透、在地人際網絡、網軍操作、真假訊息混雜、跨境鎮壓，以及AI生成短影音等。
美國戰爭研究所（ISW）與美國企業研究所（AEI）最新一期《中國與台灣情勢更新》（The China & Taiwan Update）報告提到，中共近期正顯著升級對其定義為「台獨頑固分子」的脅迫策略，由鎖定政治人物個人，延伸至對其在商界發展的親屬實施制裁與經濟打壓。

黄仁勋本周恢复担任英伟达首席执行官，给震惊华盛顿和硅谷的丑闻增添了另一个转折。风险不仅仅在于股票市场的波动或黄氏事务的色情细节，包括与新加坡公司 Megaspeed 前高管、潜在的中国资产爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的关系。从本质上讲，这起丑闻暴露了比任何个人或公司都重要得多的事情：美国的出口管制政策仍然漏洞百出，因无能和内讧而举步维艰，并且脱离了明确的战略。除非华盛顿解决这个问题，否则美国来之不易的人工智能优势可能会受到损害。
这一出口政策的失败不仅仅是具体缺陷的总和。这源于特朗普政府对中国的更广泛立场。华盛顿在拥抱不受限制的人工智能加速的同时，也对北京采取了更加宽松的立场。这种结合为爆炸性的 Megaspeed 丑闻埋下了伏笔，或许还有其他尚未浮出水面的丑闻。结果，中国已经能够获得数量惊人的先进芯片，从而缩小与美国的人工智能差距，并为其人工智能驱动的军事现代化提供动力。据人工智能研究机构Epoch AI称，中国多达三分之一的人工智能算力可能来自走私芯片。中国顶尖的人工智能模型现在仅落后美国几个月。这一微小的差距反映出中国真正的创新和对丰富能源资源的获取，以及其为规避美国控制而做出的不懈努力。
黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的要求下重返英伟达，这表明该公司和白宫似乎对阻止中国强大的人工智能芯片完全不感兴趣。相反，国会将负责确保美国利用其计算优势并保持其人工智能优势。中期选举和两党对 Megaspeed 灾难的担忧日益加剧，为国会提供了纠正方向的新动力。其近期议程应包括堵住已知的漏洞，这些漏洞在允许 Megaspeed 向中国供应先进芯片方面发挥了关键作用，并加大力度

How China Exploited a Massive Loophole in U.S. National Security—and How Congress Can Close It

The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia this week added another twist to a scandal that has transfixed Washington and Silicon Valley. The stakes go beyond the swings of the stock market or the salacious details about Huang’s affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed and a potential Chinese asset. At its core, the scandal has exposed something that matters far more than any one man or company: American export-control policy remains riddled with loopholes, hobbled by incapacity and infighting, and divorced from clear strategy. Unless Washington fixes this, it risks imperiling the United States’ hard-won advantage in artificial intelligence.
This export policy failure is more than the sum of specific deficiencies. It stems from the Trump administration’s broader posture on China. Washington has embraced unfettered AI acceleration at the same time as it has struck a more accommodating stance toward Beijing. That combination set the stage for the explosive Megaspeed scandal—and perhaps others that have yet to emerge. As a result, China has been able to access an alarming number of advanced chips that have enabled it to narrow the AI gap with the United States and power its AI-driven military modernization. According to the AI research institute Epoch AI, up to a third of China’s AI computing power may come from smuggled chips. China’s top AI models are now just months behind the U.S. frontier. The narrow gap reflects China’s genuine innovation and access to abundant energy resources as well as its relentless efforts to circumvent U.S. controls.
Huang’s return to Nvidia at the behest of President Donald Trump suggests that both the company and the White House seem utterly uninterested in keeping powerful AI chips from China. It will instead fall to Congress to ensure that the United States leverages its compute advantage and maintains its AI edge. The midterm elections and mounting bipartisan concerns over the Megaspeed debacle give Congress new momentum to correct course. Its near-term agenda should include closing known loopholes that played a key role in allowing Megaspeed to supply advanced chips to China, stepping up enforcement of existing controls, and strengthening oversight of the administration’s export-control decisions.
Over the medium term, Congress must also tackle the broader question of how to balance the strategic benefits of exporting U.S. technology to build the world’s AI infrastructure with robust controls to prevent its leakage to China. The long-standing debate over which American AI chips and capabilities Washington should permit to diffuse globally and under what conditions has finally boiled over into the mainstream—and, in a perverse way, the national security community can thank Alice Huang for forcing the issue.
The issue before Congress, however, is much broader than addressing the specifics of the Nvidia scandal. Congress must also contend with the underlying impulses driving the administration’s China policy and install guardrails to avoid the erosion of U.S. export controls. This means that after Congress passes near-term bills to mop up the Megaspeed mess, it must then take the reins on setting long-term export-control strategy.
Congress cannot stand by idly as AI blazes forward. OpenAI’s top model can now perform professional tasks as well as or better than humans 85 percent of the time, up from just 14 percent in 2024. The time an AI model can independently work on a task is doubling every four months. Last week, a researcher at Anthropic announced that AI helped him untangle the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous problems in pure mathematics.
As capabilities have grown, so have risks. Frontier models can now complete simulated cyberattacks on networks on their own, and hackers are using AI models to partially automate their attacks. In the July incident involving the AI platform Hugging Face, rogue AI agents escaped their testing environment and plotted to evade human oversight, underscoring the difficulty of aligning model behavior with human intent. The growing power of AI and the risks from misuse or loss of control make U.S. leadership a national security imperative.
At its core, the U.S.-Chinese AI competition boils down to which country can deploy the best chips in the highest quantities to train and adopt advanced AI models. The Biden administration’s controls slowed Chinese AI developers by leaving them with fewer, worse chips. Nvidia’s top Blackwell chips are nearly seven times better than Huawei’s Ascend equivalents. By the end of 2026, Huawei will likely have produced less than four percent of the compute that Nvidia will have over the same time. As the founder and CEO of DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI companies, admitted in 2024, “Our problem has never been money—it’s the embargo on high-end chips.”
To circumvent Biden-era restrictions, elaborate networks for smuggling and transshipment emerged to divert chips to China from other countries that could legally acquire them, and Chinese companies leveraged export-control loopholes to remotely access U.S.-powered compute through data centers abroad. Chinese firms funded companies such as Megaspeed to facilitate these workarounds. Backed by the Chinese tech giant Alibaba, Megaspeed has purchased $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips since 2023, prompting an investigation from the U.S. government. Chinese companies also used a technique known as adversarial distillation—training their models on the outputs of top U.S. models at a fraction of the compute. All of this needlessly shrank the United States’ AI lead over China, even after the imposition of export controls.
Congress must take the reins on setting long-term export-control strategy.
These developments should have spurred the Trump administration to better resource, enforce, and update the export controls when it came into office. It did the opposite. In May 2025, the administration suspended the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule, which had established rules for which countries could access advanced chips and in what quantities. Then, after initially prohibiting sales to China of Nvidia’s H20 chip, which was custom-built as a less powerful product for the Chinese market, the Trump administration reversed course in December 2025 and greenlighted the sale of Nvidia’s H200 chip. Although the H200 is two generations behind top U.S. chips, it remains superior to anything China can produce. An investigation from the House Foreign Affairs Committee in November revealed that between December 2025 and May 2026, the Trump administration approved the sale of more than 800,000 of Nvidia’s H200 chips and AMD’s MI325X equivalent, including to companies that the Pentagon has designated as linked to the Chinese military. This week, under pressure from Congress, the administration added Megaspeed to the entity list, which blocks those listed from buying U.S. products without a license—but before that, the administration had not added a single new individual or business to the list in 2026.
This regulatory vacuum and policy incoherence created the perfect conditions for Megaspeed. The Singaporean firm at the center of the Nvidia scandal seems tailor-made to operate in the seams of U.S. export controls. In 2024, the Commerce Department initiated a formal investigation of the company, which could have led to sanctions such as being placed on the entity list. But the Trump administration dragged its feet in pursuing the investigation. In the meantime, Megaspeed stocked Southeast Asian data centers with thousands of U.S. chips, enabling remote access for Chinese firms. This remote access loophole in U.S. export controls was a well-known and increasingly popular workaround for China-linked firms, but the Trump administration left it open for nearly two years and closed it only last week amid pressure from the Nvidia scandal. Regardless of the Megaspeed specifics, the net result of the Trump administration’s actions and inaction is that China has enjoyed access to far more computing power than it should have during a vital period of the AI competition.
The administration’s long-awaited closure of the remote access loophole is a welcome step. The rule requires foreign data centers to secure a license before offering significant computing power to China-based customers. It also requires a license to export advanced chips to places that could facilitate remote access and chip diversion, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. This rule will make it harder for firms such as Megaspeed to import chips in the first place, or to use them to serve China-based customers. But the rule will be difficult to enforce because the U.S. Commerce Department does not have the legal authority under export controls to directly regulate services such as cloud computing. More important, the administration’s lax enforcement of past controls—and internal divisions over the new ones—raise serious questions about its willingness to follow through. Huang’s reinstatement as CEO, with Trump’s backing, will make it harder to vigorously enforce these new controls and move toward a tougher posture on China.
Since Congress cannot rely on the administration to fix export controls and protect the United States’ AI lead, lawmakers should urgently advance bipartisan measures to address the underlying conditions that gave rise to entities such as Megaspeed. As a starting point, Congress should pass the Remote Access Security Act, which would give the administration clear legal authority for controlling remote access to data centers powered by U.S. compute. While implementation will require close congressional oversight, getting the right legal structure in place is an important first step. Next, it should work with industry and technical experts to fund and fast-track “on-chip” technologies—basically, features that can verify a chip’s location and counter smuggling and diversion. Beyond sorting out the technical feasibilities, Congress will need to work with industry to understand the implications of on-chip security mechanisms for global competitiveness and the potential surveillance risks should China develop similar controls since it produces much of the world’s legacy chips.
Along with these technical fixes, Congress should seize on the Megaspeed scandal to strengthen oversight. The AI Overwatch Act, which may be included in the annual defense bill, would codify existing export controls on advanced chips into law, preventing the current or a future administration from reversing them. It would also empower Congress to review and block advanced chips sales to U.S. adversaries. Congress can go even further by establishing a new investigative committee or inspector general to strengthen oversight of sensitive chip export-control policies. Together, these actions would go a long way toward combating the circumvention that let firms such as Megaspeed thrive.
Trump has emphasized summitry optics over pushing China on any sensitive issues.
At the same time, closing loopholes and codifying rules is insufficient to fix the underlying issues that led to the Megaspeed scandal in the first place. This mess is directly downstream from Trump’s dovish shift on China that has seen the administration take a softer line on Beijing just as the AI race accelerated. The administration’s own overreach forced Washington into a conciliatory posture. Administration officials failed to realize that China had learned its lesson from the first Trump administration’s trade wars and was poised to retaliate hard in the second term. After China responded to Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs and export controls with its own punishing controls on rare earths, the Trump administration found its way into a vaguely defined and fragile truce. This has severely constrained U.S. policymaking, including related to compute controls.
Indeed, Trump became an easy sell for advocates of aggressive AI promotion such as Jensen Huang. This camp argues that U.S. leadership in the global AI race requires pushing American AI technologies to as many parts of the globe as possible—including China. They claim that keeping China “addicted” to the U.S. AI stack gives Washington leverage and outweighs the national security concerns that could come with helping China improve its AI capabilities. Huang even pushed demonstrably false narratives that China’s military was not interested in Nvidia’s chips and labeled his critics as “unpatriotic” for not wanting U.S. chips spread as far and wide as possible and therefore depriving American tech firms of global market share.
Trump, who was interested in stabilizing the relationship with China and prioritizing near-term, transactional victories on trade, bought it. He also broke with decades of U.S. foreign policy precedent to negotiate export controls with China. In a series of “do nothing” leader-level meetings since, the president has emphasized summitry optics over pushing China on any sensitive issues. And Huang’s restoration at Nvidia ensures that the president’s worst impulses on China will continue to be egged on by his favored tech CEO, to the detriment of U.S. national security.
A core part of Congress’s longer-term agenda should be outlining the basic principles to determine who can import or remotely access advanced AI chips and under what conditions. Administrations have gone back and forth over this line-drawing exercise. The Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule would have imposed a global licensing regime that controlled not just the export of chips but also the aggregate U.S.-powered compute that any country could receive. Under Trump, only a handful of countries face restrictions. A smarter approach would condition advanced chip sales on the buyer’s ability to protect them from diversion and guard against misuse by malign actors looking to skirt safety and security rules. Allied and partner governments could demonstrate this by developing robust economic security policies to prevent chip diversion or remote access. Foreign companies would have to show strong compliance and security commitments. In practice, this would mean having internal procedures to ensure that chips are not diverted and maintaining cooperation with Commerce Department officials to verify that such procedures were working.
Congress can also help rebuild allies’ confidence in U.S. export-control policy. There was hard-won, if imperfect, progress on allied alignment in key areas of export controls under the Biden administration, notably with the Dutch and the Japanese on controls of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The painstaking work needed to get allies on board can be agonizingly slow, but once achieved, it is far more likely to endure than if the United States imposes extraterritorial controls over their objections. The MATCH Act, one of the bills revived following the Megaspeed scandal, requires controls on allied-produced tools if Washington is unable to negotiate allied alignment. It is a rather rude approach at a moment when U.S. export controls seem to be on shaky footing, U.S. tariffs against allies have pushed relations to a near breaking point, and allies rightly question whether the United States still views China as a strategic threat. Instead, Congress should support efforts to create durable frameworks for allied alignment, such as economic security agreements in key strategic sectors.
A longer-term agenda must include fixing the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, the main agency responsible for administering and enforcing export controls. The bureau has been gutted by dismissals and low morale during the Trump administration, but it has been underresourced for far longer. Congress should increase funding and require modernization of the bureau’s antiquated IT system. Just as important, Congress needs to help insulate policymaking decisions from corporate influence, and it can help by insisting that future Commerce Department officials commit to independent and risk-based decision-making to earn confirmation.
None of these steps will be easy. The president’s support of Huang’s restoration shows that stock market fluctuations weigh more heavily in his decision-making than national security, and the administration is unlikely to welcome increased congressional oversight. The Constitution gives the executive wide deference on matters of foreign policy and national security. But Congress has a role in ensuring that the president faithfully executes the laws and is supported by the right resources, oversight, and strategic priorities. The United States’ AI lead may hinge on whether it meets the moment.

summary: 2026 年 6 月 25 日，分配到第 4 海军陆战旅的菲律宾海军陆战队员和分配到第 3 海军陆战师第 3 海军陆战团第 3 濒海战斗队的美国海军陆战队员，参加 KAMANDAG 10 期间在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊巴亚特举行的海上关键地形安全行动累积训练活动。美国海军陆战队照片菲律宾马尼拉 — 美国承诺拨款 2 美元数十亿美元的外国军事融资贷款计划，用于马尼拉的军事现代化努力和吕宋海峡机场的开发。有针对性的国防援助是几项交易之一
content:
2026 年 6 月 25 日，分配到第 4 海军陆战旅的菲律宾海军陆战队员和分配到第 3 海军陆战师第 3 海军陆战团第 3 濒海战斗队的美国海军陆战队员，参加 KAMANDAG 10 期间在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊巴亚特举行的海上关键地形安全行动累积训练活动。美国海军陆战队照片菲律宾马尼拉 — 美国承诺拨款 2 美元数十亿美元的外国军事融资贷款计划，用于马尼拉的军事现代化努力和吕宋海峡机场的开发。有针对性的国防援助是唐纳德·特朗普总统上周访问菲律宾参加东南亚国家联盟年度峰会期间签署的几项协议之一。这些协议与菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯一起宣布，标志着华盛顿对其长期印太盟友的承诺大幅增加。白宫称，这 20 亿美元的国防贷款将提供给菲律宾，用于出售“美国供应商的关键国防和安全能力”。白宫在马尼拉协议的新闻稿中写道：“美国将利用 4 亿美元（外国军事融资）帮助菲律宾军队扩大其在南海的作战范围和威慑能力，包括远程火力、指挥和控制、关键基础设施和多域无人机，支持 1,500 个美国就业岗位。”
据美国海军学院新闻了解，菲律宾已收到洛克希德·马丁公司提供的大量提案，涉及各种系统，包括 M142 高机动火箭系统和 F-16V Viper 战斗机。此外，洛克希德·马丁公司还与吉布斯和考克斯合作，武装其国际级护卫舰设计，该设计已向菲律宾海军推销。马尼拉此前曾表示有兴趣采购洛克希德·马丁公司的中程能力，这是一种陆基 Mark 41 垂直发射系统，美国陆军自 2024 年 4 月以来已在菲律宾前沿部署该系统。美国为马尼拉新生的非对称能力计划（一个无人系统网状网络）提供的美国援助计划涉及无人机公司 Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. 和 Ocean Aero。美国国防部官员此前告诉美国海军学院新闻，攻击无人机将于明年转移。除了贷款之外，白宫新闻稿还宣布了苏比克湾和巴丹群岛的国防基础设施开发。其中包括位于苏比克湾的一座价值 4000 万美元的燃料储存设施，该基地是前美国海军基地的所在地，华盛顿在其区域威慑努力中越来越多地利用该基地。自2022年以来，美国军队几乎每个分支都在苏比克湾部署了部队和物资。近年来，美国陆军和美国海军陆战队在战略海湾周围承包了车辆和物资储存设施。今年夏天，我们看到了美国
菲律宾海军主要基地对面的码头上的海岸警卫队舞台快艇。分配给海军陆战队第三师、海军陆战队第三团的第三濒海战斗队的海军陆战队队员，从分配给海军陆战队空中加油机运输中队（VMGR）152、海军陆战队第12大队、海军陆战队第一联队的一架KC-130J超级大力士上卸下海军陆战队远征舰拦截系统，在KAMANDAG 10期间进行海上关键地形安全行动。菲律宾巴丹群岛伊特巴亚特，2026 年 6 月 19 日。美国海军陆战队照片在吕宋海峡中部，

【原文 English Original】
Philippine marines assigned to 4th Marine Brigade, and U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, participate in a cumulative training event for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo MANILA, Philippines — The U.S. pledged to grant a $2 billion foreign military financing loan package for Manila’s military modernization efforts and the development of an airport in the Luzon Strait. The targeted defense assistance was one of several deals inked last week during President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ annual summit. Announced alongside Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., these deals mark a drastic increase in Washington’s commitment to its longtime Indo-Pacific ally. The $2 billion in defense loans will be made available for the Philippines covering the sale of “critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers,” according to the White House. “The United States will utilize $400 million in [foreign military financing] for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs,” reads the White House’s release on the Manila deals. The Philippines has received considerable proposals from Lockheed Martin covering a variety of systems, including M142 High Mobility Rocket Systems and F-16V Viper fighter jets, USNI News understands. Additionally, the defense prime partnered with Gibbs and Cox to arm its International-class frigate design, which has been pitched to the Philippine Navy. Manila previously voiced interest in procuring Lockheed Martin’s Mid-Range Capability, a ground-based Mark 41 vertical launching system that the U.S. Army has had forward deployed in the Philippines since April of 2024. American aid packages contributing to Manila’s nascent Asymmetric Capabilities Program , an unmanned systems mesh network, involve drone firms Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. and Ocean Aero. U.S. defense officials previously told USNI News that attack drones will be transferred next year. Beyond the loans, defense infrastructure developments at Subic Bay and the Batanes Islands were also announced in the White House release. These include a fuel storage facility worth $40 million at Subic Bay, the site of a former U.S. Navy base that has been increasingly tapped by Washington in its regional deterrence efforts. Since 2022, almost every branch of the U.S. military has staged forces and supplies at Subic Bay. In recent years, the U.S. Army and the U.S. Marine Corps contracted storage facilities for vehicles and supplies around the strategic bay. This summer saw the U.S. Coast Guard stage cutters at a pier across from the Philippine Navy’s primary base. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, unload a Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System from a KC-130J Super Hercules assigned to Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 152, Marine Aircraft Group 12, 1st Marine Aircraft Wing, for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 19, 2026. US Marine Corps photos In the middle of the Luzon Strait, the allies plan to increase their “operational access” through the modernization of Basco Airport. Located within 100 miles of Taiwan, the airport is in an area that would become crucial in a potential cross strait conflict. Since 2025, the U.S. Marine Corps has used the airport to insert maritime sensing teams and anti-ship missile-equipped Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction Systems. From the Batanes Islands, Washington and Manila can lock down the strategic first island chain chokepoint. U.S. and Philippine Marines have practiced delivering missile systems and setting up ground-based radar nodes across the archipelago. One of these maritime domain awareness teams emplaced on an island only 88 miles away from Taiwan during an exercise in 2024.

值得注意的是，这些被罢黜的将领中，有 50% 到 80% 是各级作战指挥官。 清洗运动震撼了国防机构 与此同时，中国的国防机构仍在承受四十年来最彻底的组织重组的冲击。 2016年启动的这次改革，不仅是为了增强解放军发动二十一世纪联合作战的能力，也是为了精简和集中军队，使其受中央军委主席习近平的直接指挥。这次重组被称为“中国的戈德华特-尼科尔斯”，以强调与美军在越战后时期强制各军种联合作战的举措的相似之处，这一举措花了几十年才完全实施。没有人知道习近平雄心勃勃的计划进展如何，因为中国人民解放军——包括空军、海军、陆军、火箭军和其他特种军种——尚未在21世纪发动战争，战争是对任何一支军队的严峻考验。现代化已将一支技术含量低、以轻步兵为中心、拥有陈旧空军和小型褐水海军的军队转变为一支机械化地面部队​​，拥有大量第四代和第五代战斗机空中力量，以及世界上最大的蓝水海军舰队。

How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA H.Seidl Tue, 11/17/2026 - 11:58 picture alliance / Xinhua News Agency | Gao Zeming Comment Nov 17, 2026 4 min read How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA The country’s armed forces are more capable than ever but in turmoil. Whatever the shortcomings of China's military, Andrew Scobell says it is likely to prove a formidable adversary in any war. The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in late October elected the vice chair of the Central Military Commission (CMC), General Zhang Shengmin, to the CCP Politburo . The party leadership also confirmed the September expulsions of top generals from the CMC, but did not appoint any replacements. This left China’s rough equivalent to the US military’s Joint Chiefs of Staff with just two members, down from its usual seven: Xi Jinping as its civilian chair and one single uniformed officer, General Zhang.   The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is by many accounts the most modern, capable, professional and best equipped military in the history of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). But it is also enduring its greatest upheavals in six decades—since the turmoil of Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution in the 1960s. Purges have swept away more than 100 senior officers since 2022 as part of Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption crusade. Remarkably, between 50 and 80 percent of these ousted general officers have been operational commanders at various levels . Purges have rocked the defense establishment At the same time, China’s defense establishment is still absorbing the shock of the most thoroughgoing organizational restructuring in four decades. This revamping, launched in 2016, was not only intended to make the PLA more capable of waging twenty-first century joint warfare, but also to streamline and centralize it under the direct chain of command of CMC chairman Xi. This reorganization, dubbed “ China’s Goldwater-Nichols ” to underscore the parallels with the US military’s post-Vietnam War era initiative to compel separately stovepiped services to fight jointly—an effort that took decades to fully implement.  No one knows how well Xi’s ambitious initiative is faring, since the PLA – comprising the PLA Air Force, PLA Navy, PLA Ground Force, PLA Rocket Force, and other specialized services – has yet to wage war in the 21st century, warfighting being the acid test of any military. Modernization has transformed a low-tech, light infantry-centric military with an antiquated air force and a small brown-water navy into a mechanized ground force, with a sizeable airpower inventory of fourth-  and fifth-generation fighter jets, and the world’s largest blue-water naval fleet. Moreover, today’s PLA units engage in more realistic combat training and, for the past two decades, have participated in numerous, albeit largely small-scale, multinational field exercises. China’s armed forces have become increasingly activist and aggressive around the PRC’s periphery. In the far west, ground forces have deployed in ever greater numbers, engaging in occasional bloody small-scale clashes with India’s army along the two countries’ disputed Himalayan border . In the South China Sea , the PLA Navy, PRC Coast Guard and People’s Maritime Militia have stepped up harassment of naval ships, coast guard cutters and fishing boats, notably those of the Philippines and Vietnam. In the East China Sea , PRC maritime forces have conducted similar operations against Japanese and South Korean vessels. Perhaps most alarming is the dramatic escalation of so-called gray zone provocations around Taiwan. Modernization has strengthened the PLA  PLA formations are also operating further and further from China’s borders. Ground force units have served on United Nations peacekeeping missions around the world, while some air formations have also operated overseas. In 2026, the PLA acknowledged its first air installation outside of the PRC in Laos. Yet the most routinely deployed service overseas has been the PLA Navy. Its vessels have operated continuously in the Gulf of Aden since late 2008 and have been more active across the Western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean, and even making appearances in the Atlantic, Arctic and Baltic seas. The PLA Navy has operated a support base in Djibouti on the Red Sea since 2017 and opened a naval base in Ream, Cambodia, in 2025.  But increased peacetime operational experience and tempo do not guarantee wartime successes. While PLA drills and deployments do not seem to have been impacted by the unprecedented waves of purges continuing across all echelons of China’s military, their effects could be different under actual combat conditions. The PLA has not fought a major war since China’s conflict with Vietnam in 1979. Muscular and intimidating shows of force around the PRC’s periphery and the periodic spectacle of smartly turned-out troops with gleaming military hardware on parade in Beijing are not incontrovertible proof of combat readiness. Nevertheless, as a former US defense chief famously remarked , “You go to war with the army you have.” In the event of conflict, the leaders of the PRC – just as much as those of other great powers – will have no choice but to send their militaries into battle irrespective of their condition or level of combat readiness – and their armed forces will salute and follow orders, executing operations as best they can. The PLA will remain something of a puzzle for a while, but it is likely to make a credible account of itself in any conflict. Its combat record over the decades has shown that it can fight effectively, absorb heavy casualties and adapt under fire. The views expressed in this piece are those of the author. 中国将台湾视为自己的领土，但并不统治这个民主岛屿，称执政的民进党台北候选人沉普马是“叛徒”，他正在渲染中国威胁，以欺骗人们投票给他。

China slams ruling party candidate ahead of Taiwan’s mayoral and county votes
Supporters of the Democratic Progressive Party's Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen wave flags and hold campaign posters at a rally ahead of the election in Taipei on Nov. 15. | REUTERS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
TAIPEI – Taiwan’s mayoral and county chief elections on Saturday are not directly about China, but the ruling party’s nomination for Taipei mayor — a lawmaker wanted by Chinese police for “separatism” — has sent Beijing into a flurry of denunciations.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory but does not govern the democratic island, says the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Taipei candidate Puma Shen is a “traitor” who is playing up the China threat to trick people into voting for him.
In October, Taipei prosecutors indicted four people for putting monitoring devices on a scooter parked outside Shen’s home, issuing arrest warrants for two people from Hong Kong it said were behind the scheme.

content:
中共新法影响恶劣 台政府3招反制、绿委促修国安双法(图) 民族團結進步促進法 | 台灣 | 跨國鎮壓 | 时政聚焦 || 看中国网
2024年5月19日，中共军用直升机飞越福建省平潭岛，平潭岛是中国大陆距离台湾本岛最近的岛屿。（图片来源：HECTOR RETAMAL/AFP via Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月24日讯】（看中国记者李净瑶综合报导）中共于7月开始实施的“民族团结进步促进法”将适用范围扩大至境外，引发各界担忧。台湾陆委会主委邱垂正出席一场国际研讨会时指出，中共这部法律有三个层面的恶劣影响，台湾政府将持续因应，守护自由与民主。另外，绿委促修国安双法，以因应日益猖獗的中共跨国镇压。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
《中央广播电台》11月22日报导，达赖喇嘛西藏宗教基金会22日举办“雪域论坛—2026寻找共同点：因应中华人民共和国民族团结进步促进法的恶劣影响及对应策略”国际研讨会，邀请国内外学者专家，探讨中共《民族团结进步促进法》对少数民族权利及跨国镇压的影响。
陆委会主委邱垂正在研讨会上致词表示，中共今年7月1日施行的“民族团结进步促进法”，不是单纯的法律规范，而是中共近年持续构建的“长臂管辖网络”中极为关键的一环。
根据陆委会的观察，中共的这部法律有三个层面的恶劣影响。第一，中共假借所谓的“共同体意识”之名，表面上促进民族团结、共同发展，实际上却是将中共的政治意志，透过法律制度进一步深入人民生活，强化思想控制与同化政策。
第二，“促进法”是中共第一部将台湾纳入其民族工作范畴的法律，以“民族团结”包装“国家统一”，标志着对台法律战从“反独”转向“强制促统”。这不仅增加台湾人赴中国大陆及参与交流的风险，中共也会在未来各面向的两岸交流纳入促统内涵和标准，让本应健康有序、不带政治前提的两岸交流活动变成中共推动统战及政治控制的工具。
第三，“促进法”纳入域外适用规定，企图将中共的长臂管辖扩张，成为跨境镇压的法律工具。中共不只控制境内人民，也透过法律，结合跟监、骚扰、恐吓，以及暴力袭击等手段，威胁境外人士，迫使异议人士噤声。而自去年起已陆续发生多起事件，如台港人汤伟雄两次泼漆、媒体人矢板明夫先生遭攻击、喜剧演员黄逸豪遭遇“假车祸”，以及《国有器官》纪录片发行商与放映戏院遭到系统性炸弹恐吓等跨境镇压等。
邱垂正指出，面对中共“以法促统”与跨国（境）镇压的蛮横作为，台湾政府将从“预防”、“保护”、“反制”三个面向积极因应。目前，行政院已督导成立“跨国（境）镇压跨机关协处平台”，将保护国人的工作提升至跨部会层级。
另外，政府已将赴陆港澳旅游警示调升为“橙色”，吁请台湾民众应尽量避免前往，若有必要，也务必于行前至陆委会“赴陆港澳动态登录系统”完成登录，以便政府在必要时提供及时协助。
“中共的极权扩张本质，短期内无法消失或转变；台海与区域和平稳定的愿景，仍将面临诸多严峻挑战。但是，我们仍会坚守对民主、自由、人权与法治的信仰，持续致力守护这些珍贵的普世价值，守护民主台湾。”邱垂正说。
另据《自由时报》11月24日报导，因应中共日益猖獗的对台渗透、认知作战与跨国镇压，民进党立委王定宇、林楚茵等16人提出《反渗透法》与《国家安全法》修正草案（国安双法）。他们指出，中共在台湾境内施行的跨国镇压，已从过去的跟监、恐吓胁迫，逐渐转变为具体的骚扰或攻击行为，相关案件在剧增，包含指使境外及在台协力者，监视、跟拍特定人物，意图取得隐私资讯，做为威胁筹码；或冒用反中人士名义寄送恐吓邮件，谋诋毁镇压对象名誉，甚至制造肢体冲突、泼漆讨债、假车祸等事故，冀以暴力威吓行动，使人心生畏惧，引发寒蝉效应。
提案续指，检警调在侦办这类案件时，引用“刑法”妨害社会秩序罪并依“反渗透法”相关规定加重其刑至二分之一，不仅刑度偏低，而且针对在台协力者之不法行为样态，目前反渗透法的规范也不足因应。
草案将《反渗透法》刑责提高至3年以上、7年以下有期徒刑，并扩大在台协力者处罚。参与组织并违反国安法者加重其刑至二分之一，军公教人员一审判刑即暂停半数退休金。此外，公开鼓吹“武统”者最高处新台币100万元罚锾。

content:
中共自爆某部委官员对外泄露国家秘密 被判死刑(图) 情報人員 | CIA | 中情局 | 动向 || 看中国网
2017年10月18日，在北京人民大会堂举行的中共第十九次全国代表大会开幕式上，中共官兵和安保人员等待人大代表们抵达。（图片来源：GREG BAKER/AFP via Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月24日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）日前，中共官方平台发文称，一名中共部委机关干部在境外工作期间，被他国情报人员策反，回国后提供上百份情报资料，法院审理时认定其泄露9项秘密级国家秘密和26项机密级国家秘密，以“间谍罪”判处死刑。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
2026年11月23日，据中共保密宣传教育平台“保密观”微信公众号发文称，一名麻姓中共部委工作人员在驻A国工作期间，与B国驻A国情报人员凯琳结识。刚开始时，凯琳以“加强沟通”、“学习中文”为由，与麻姓工作人员频繁约见，还承诺会向对方支付一定报酬。随着两人交往的深入，凯琳逐渐把话题转向政治敏感议题和国际时事，并打探中共驻A国机构的人员和工作情况。
“保密观”文章声称，麻姓工作人员向凯琳透露“大量敏感信息”，包括机构内部电话簿。凯琳又把情报人员唐正介绍给麻姓工作人员认识。文章称，唐正要求麻姓工作人员加入B国的情报机构，并以举报相要挟。
麻姓工作人员最终接受间谍任务，并签署了包含“保密”、“忠诚”等条款的合作文件，每个月领取固定报酬。唐正为他配了专用发送和接收情报的笔记本电脑。
麻某在结束驻外工作后回中国。他在白天根据B国的要求，从接触到的工作涉密文件材料中搜集资料，晚上下班后把整理好的材料通过间谍网站发送到境外。文章称，麻某窃取提供百余份情报资料，并以在中国国内接头、在国外见面的方式获取报酬，对方也根据他提供情报的质量额外支付奖金。
文章称，麻姓人员最终落网。法院审理认定他泄露9项秘密级国家秘密和26项机密级国家秘密，因此获取百万余元，法院以“间谍罪”判处麻某死刑，并没收全部个人财产。
但文章并没有具体提及麻姓人员所属的部委、涉及的境外A国、B国名字、案发和宣判时间，也没有说明是否已对其执行死刑，因此无法证实该文所提及的消息内容真伪。
“保密观”文章结尾写道，处于重要岗位的中共官员加强“党性修养和保密意识”，隐蔽战线的斗争从未停歇，要净化社交圈、朋友圈，严防被“围猎”，即严防被渗透策反。
据《美国之音》报导，2026年2月12日，美国中央情报局(CIA)在YouTube、X平台和脸书等多个社媒平台发布一段普通话视频，试图策反中共军人，招募他们为中情局线人。
#DW中文 https://t.co/cTrYAGQ1iI
— DW 中文- 德国之声 (@dw_chinese) February 13, 2026
短视频的名字是《挺身而出的原因：为拯救未来》，里面描述一名虚构的中共男性军人在经历对中共军中高层腐败的不满和挫败感后，最后通过匿名信息系统安全联系美国中情局的过程。视频告诉他们：“世界的命运掌握在你的手中。”
其实，早在2025年5月，美国中情局就已经发布了两段中文视频，题目是《选择合作的原因：创造美好远景》与《选择合作的原因：成为命运的主宰者》，目的是想吸引中共基层官员和高官的关注，并提供联系中情局的途径。CIA把这种联系行为定义为一种“掌握命运”与“保护家人”的道德抉择，而不是传统意义上的背叛。
选择合作的原因：创造美好远景 https://t.co/4BsFttl79P https://t.co/nNrrf2SNus
选择合作的原因：成为命运的主宰者 https://t.co/4BsFttl79P https://t.co/mjA3wPJdzT
2026年1月15日，中情局又发布第三个视频，并更新了联系信息，视频显示：“中情局想知道中国的真相，我们正在寻找知道并能告知真相的人。”这段视频恰巧在张又侠落马前发布，时间点敏感。
此视频提供安全联系中央情报局的全套步骤。以下有几个在进行安全联系之前及在过程中务必考量的事项。
— CIA (@CIA) January 15, 2026
紧接着，中情局又在张又侠落马后不到一个月的2月12日，再次发布第4支针对中共军人的影片：《挺身而出的原因：为拯救未来》。
一名中情局官员用匿名的方式向路透社披露说，过去的视频接触到数百万人，并由此激发了新的讯息来源，但这名官员没有提供细节。
此外，中情局局长约翰‧拉特克利夫在一份声明中也表示，“去年，中情局的中文视频宣传活动触及了许多中国公民，我们知道还有更多人正在寻找改善生活、让国家变得更好的方法。”

content:
黄仁勋离职11天闪电回归 川普为何突然怕了中共?(图) 英偉達（Nvidia） | 深圳APEC | 时评 |陈静| 看中国网
2026年11月20日：美国总统唐纳德·川普在白宫詹姆斯·S·布雷迪新闻发布厅举行的新闻发布会上回答提问时，做出准备手势。川普总统在结束对中国的访问后向媒体发表讲话。 （图片来源：Kevin Dietsch／Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
2026年11月23日，黄仁勋离职仅仅11天后恢复原职务。同日，川普接受《美国消费者新闻》与商业频道（CNBC）专访时的表态。他几乎是用一种毫不掩饰的紧迫感解释自己为何力保黄仁勋。他说，北京一直在全球范围内延揽人才且手段“非常狡猾”，若让黄仁勋在受委屈的情况下继续赋闲，中方随时可能抛出橄榄枝：“我仿佛看到他们（中共）走过来对黄仁勋说：‘嘿，你想不想来中国执掌华为，或者掌管我们的一家公司？’我保证他们会满足他的一切要求。”他甚至透露，在深圳会晤期间，习近平曾亲口对他说，黄仁勋是“一个天才”。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
不过川普没想到的是，10多亿中国人还缺天才吗，当然不缺，缺的只是没有天才成长的环境。马斯克当年那句最经典的疑问：“马云去了哪里？”如今还在人们的耳边回响。是的，马云们去了哪里？谁来回答这个问题？黄仁勋如果去了中共囯，黄仁勋还会有在美国的自由待遇吗？就算他可以身边美女如云，就算天下美女都给他，他也只能夜塌一张床而已。
11月18日至19日，第33届APEC领导人非正式会议在深圳香蜜湖畔的深圳国际交流中心登场。这是美国在任总统历史上首次踏足这座所谓改革开放的橱窗城市。习近平罕见亲赴深圳宝安机场接机，随后举行了备受瞩目的“川习会”。
返抵白宫后，川普在记者会上对深圳不吝溢美之词。据台湾钜亨网等媒体引述，他称赞这场峰会“极其成功”，对深圳的整洁有序、基础建设与发展速度赞叹不已，甚至拿来与美国部分城市的街头乱象作对比。
说的也没错，美国的基础建设确实需要加强；但是，如果美国想与中共比面子工程，那还是小巫见大巫了，甚至比不了、没法比。而中共为什么那么喜欢做面子工程？答案非常简单：能骗人，确实也骗了很多很多的人，连川普也被骗了，直夸深圳好。可是他们看不到的是，光鲜的外表下面，处处都是空壳。
其实大家也知道，所有的民主国家都没有中共囯那里那么光鲜，但是人家有就业有富足的民生，而中共有吗？就在深圳如此光鲜的时候，有一位女子就饿晕在大街上。
在中共官方叙事里，这正是“APEC中国年”希望呈现的完美答卷：双语路标林立、簕杜鹃沿街盛开、斥资约百亿人民币新建的主会场与升级版夜间灯光秀交相辉映，展现出华为、比亚迪、大疆等科技巨头汇聚的现代化奇迹。然而，在聚光灯照不到的城市褶皱里，当地市民与独立媒体记录下的却是另一番景象。
据台湾公共电视引述多名深圳居民的说法，早在大会揭幕前，这座千万人口的一线城市便已全面进入“APEC时间”。自11月1日起，广东省公安厅即动员全省警力增援深圳，机场与主会场周边部署了配备反无人机系统与巡逻机器人的“战狼突击队”，街头出现“三步一哨、五步一岗”的密集巡防；就连东莞、惠州等邻近城市的人行天桥上，也有警员驻守并随机检查行人的背包，禁止逗留与拍照。采访记者进入会场前须提前申报设备，手机前后镜头甚至被贴上封条；部分餐厅的菜刀被要求上锁固定，高压瓶罐与刀具则被列入禁寄清单。
而在宝安区坪洲地铁站附近，一栋自2005年起停工长达20余年的烂尾楼，竟在峰会前10天被蓝色围挡布料整体包裹，远看宛如一座崭新的现代蓝楼，引发当地网友调侃它是“APEC最大受益者”。与此同时，连夜在绿化带补种花卉、蹲地擦洗地铁地板顽垢、重新粉刷路边管线的突击工程也在全城同步铺开。
11月16日，据《南方都市报》援引高德地图数据，会议周启动后，深圳早高峰拥堵指数骤降28.09%，拥堵里程大减84.23%，地铁早高峰客流亦减少近两成。代价是逾150万名车主因被要求“绿色出行”，而不能开车出门；但在社区基层，物业人员与网格员上门劝导、路口举牌呼吁“让路给远客”、交警比对停车场进出与路面抓拍记录以核验停驶情况；写字楼里火速撤下“加班至深夜、让爱车躺平”标语，都让不少打工族自嘲“路不堵了，心里更堵了”。
更有核心地段如香蜜湖周边的居民在网上披露，部分住宅楼宇被封控看守，住户领取每日约600元人民币的补贴暂时住酒店；各地进京或赴深上访的民众，乃至于部分并无上访记录却曾留有特殊档案的市民，据知情人士与受访者透露，都在会前被提前拦截带离或纳入“维稳”名单。
在现实的双重魔幻交错之下，川普返美后对黄仁勋案的强势出手，才显得格外耐人寻味。
《卫报》、《富比士》与《时代》杂志披露，黄仁勋的交往对象中包括一名被美国情报界怀疑与中共情报部门有关的中国女子黄乐。至今，美国司法部尚未就黄乐的身份得出正式结论。
按常理，一名掌握美国最尖端AI算力命脉的企业领袖卷入潜在的情报渗透疑云，向来对华强硬的华府理应严查到底。然而，川普在CNBC专访中却轻描淡写地表示，他在深圳根本没向习近平提起黄乐一事，因为“他（习近平）级别很高，我认为他不知道这件事”。相反地，川普反复强调的，是失去黄仁勋对美国构成的“威胁”，在他眼中，习近平根本不需要靠间谍去偷技术，只要开出天价条件直接把打造出“Blackwell”芯片的灵魂人物请去中共国，就能一举改写中美AI竞赛的胜负。
川普在深圳看到的，是一套不受民意牵制、能在一夜之间让百万车主停驶、让20年烂尾楼穿上新衣、并集中全国资源押注科技巨头的极权动员机器。当习近平当面盛赞黄仁勋是“天才”时，这位习惯以强人姿态示人的美国总统川普怕了，川普嗅到了独裁政权不惜一切代价的手段，和对人性弱点的深刻洞悉。
不过有一点是让人担忧的：患上了恐惧症的川普，可以让黄仁勋一夜恢复原职，但是他能保证那么多的美国人，不会因为各种利益倒向中共吗？
川普或许认为，为了美国的利益需要和独裁中共勾肩搭背，也没啥关系。没想到一趟短暂的深圳之行，就被中共吓得不轻；那么在中共治下的老百姓，又有多少被害死、被吓死的呢？
中共不是一个普通的政权，那是一个魔鬼组织。算计了你，你还要对它感恩戴德。从这个角度来说，被中共算计了的黄仁勋，反过来还要感激中共了呗，因为习近平夸他是一个“天才”，因为川普的深圳行，才有他的回锅成功。
有多少中国人，就是这样被中共算计了、迫害了，反过来还要对这个党感激涕零，也就不足为奇了。
人是战胜不了魔鬼的，只要你一靠近它，就会被其附体、洗脑。可是连川普这样聪明的人，都不能明白这个道理，难怪共产主义如今在全世界肆意横行、无法无天。什么时候，人们能够清醒呢？
看来“天灭中共”这四个字，是真实不虚的。人战胜不了魔鬼中共，只能够神来出手了。
来自《看中国》的报导：其实早在2002年6月，在贵州境内发现了2.7亿岁的“藏字石”，五百年前崩裂的巨石断面内惊现六个排列整齐的大字“中国共产党亡”，其中那个“亡”字特别的大。中国大陆官方媒体都报导了此新闻，但隐去“亡”字，光提“中国共产党”，不过人民网、新华网等刊出的照片中却看得很清楚。
2003年8月中旬，平塘县邀请了贵州省地质专家到掌布作考察，写出了详细考察报告，认定“藏字石”是从河谷左岸陡崖上坠落下来的一块巨石，在陡崖上仍可看到崩塌岩体留下的相应凹槽。崩塌岩体坠地后，分裂为左右两块巨石，“中国共产党亡”几个大字就清晰地显现在右边巨石的内侧断裂面上。
事隔三月，应平塘县委、县政府的邀请，由全国政协委员、中国科学院地学部副主任、中国科学院院士、著名地质学家李廷栋，中国科学院院士、著名地质专家刘宝君，中国地质大学教授、国土资源部国家地质公园评委、著名古生物学专家李凤麟等15人组成的“贵州平塘地质奇观－中国名家科学文化考察团”，于2003年12月5日至8日深入掌布河谷重点对“藏字石”进行实地考察。
专家一致认为，掌布河谷景区“藏字石”上的字，位于距今2.7亿年左右的二叠统栖霞组深灰色岩中。字的均匀排列现象，虽是极其罕见的小概率事件，但均可从地质科学特别是沉淀地质学上得到解释和说明。“藏字石”上至今未发现人工雕凿及其他任何为加工痕迹，堪称世界级奇观，具有不可估量的地质研究价值。
这次考察，有20多家陆媒记者随团采访报导，100多家报纸、电视、网站转发了这一科学考察活动消息。但是没有人敢提那第六个字“亡”，纷纷报导前五个字“中国共产党”，但每一个亲眼观看的人都心知肚明。
人们都说眼见为实，事实摆在人们的面前了，明明知道这不是人力所能为的，那就是天意，神在出手了。那为什么24年过去了，中共还没倒台呢？其实，是神在给人留下清醒的时间和机会。否则等到真相大白的那一天，后悔都没机会了。

台湾九合一选举 美智库揭“中共介选”手法(图) 美國智庫 | 台商 | AI假訊息 | 新闻 美国 - 看中国新闻网 - 海外华人 历史秘闻 时政评析 || 看中国网
美国智库最新报告示警，中共正透过机票补助、渗透台湾征信业者及人工智能（AI）假讯息等多重手段，介入台湾选举。（示意图/图片来源：I-HWA CHENG/AFP via Getty Images) 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月24日讯】（看中国记者立明综合报导）台湾九合一选举28日登场，美国智库最新报告示警，中共正透过机票补助、渗透台湾征信业者及人工智能（AI）假讯息等多重手段，介入台湾选举，企图扶植亲中候选人并削弱民众对民主制度的信任。报告也揭露，中共不仅锁定在中国的台商及其家属返台投票，更透过监控、个资搜集与社群帐号操作，对台湾政治人物及亲台人士施加压力。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
美国两大智库“战争研究所”（ISW）及“美国企业研究所”（AEI）20日发布“中国与台湾情势更新”报告，获“保卫台湾联盟”（CDOT）计划支持，揭露北京当局在选前透过多种方式影响台湾选举。
报告引述台湾国安官员说法指出，中共国台办及地方政府与中国旅行社、航空公司合作，为居住在中国的台商及家属提供部分或全额机票补助、票价折扣及保留机位，甚至推出金厦小三通船票搭配金门飞往台湾本岛的优惠套票。
部分商业组织成员也获得交通优惠，包括惠州市台商投资企业协会及代表台湾人陆配的组织，但条件是必须返台投票，或协助汇整潜在选民名单。
报告并指出，中国航空公司也配合控管机位分配，例如中国东方航空在选前每班飞往台湾的定期航班，预留30个座位供返台投票的台商使用。
智库分析，北京此举可能是希望借由台商与中国较紧密的经济连结，促使他们支持对中国较友善的候选人。不过，优先保留机位也可能排挤其他同样居住在中国、但未参与相关组织的台湾人，甚至推高机票价格，影响返台投票的便利性。
除了交通补助，报告也关注中共透过私人调查业者搜集台湾亲台人士个资的情况，并以台湾检方11月17日起诉3名征信人员涉嫌受中共指使、监控网红八炯（温子瑜）及闽南狼（陈柏源）的案件为例，指出北京可能正建立境内情报搜集管道。
根据检方调查，上海市公安局官员及一名中共关联人士于2025年6月招募台湾征信人员王秉宏，要求监视八炯、闽南狼及其家人。王秉宏随后找来另外两名征信人员协助，在台湾反中示威活动中跟监两人，搜集敏感个人资料，并于同年11月赴中国时交给上海市公安局官员。
中共安全部门随后公开两人的个人资料，指控他们涉嫌“煽动分裂国家”。报告研判，中共公安公布的资讯很可能来自台湾征信人员所提供的资料，显示北京可能借由渗透私人调查业者，掌握亲台人士的生活资讯及行踪。
报告也提到，中共曾多次公开台湾政治人物及军方人员的个资，包括2025年10月公布民进党立委沈伯洋，以及同年6月、10月公布的两批台湾军方人员资料。智库认为，相关行动意在营造北京已具备全面监控能力的印象，对台湾社会形成心理威慑。
在认知作战方面，报告指出，中共也利用社群平台、假民调、特定对象讯息操作及AI生成内容，试图加剧台湾社会对立。
外媒20日引述台湾官员及政府内部报告指出，台湾近期已向Meta检举近2700个疑似涉及中共资讯战的Threads帐号，其中被标记的2400个帐号，有74%所在地点设于中国。
这些帐号先伪装成分享日常生活的台湾网友，借此建立可信度，再逐渐转向政治攻击，甚至散布“不要去投票”等讯息，企图降低选民投票意愿。
此外，约260个帐号被发现散布超过2150部AI生成影片，内容锁定民进党及沈伯洋等执政党政治人物，累计吸引约235万次互动。
Meta表示，已移除台湾方面检举的相关帐号，其中多数在接获检举前就已遭系统停权。中国国台办则未对相关报导作出回应，并否认涉及干预台湾选举。
报告另外提及，海基会前副董事长邱进益提出“10年和平统一方案”，主张两岸在2030年前建立共同市场、2032年前使用共同货币，并于2036年前透过联邦制或“一国两制”模式完成统一。中国国台办11月18日也借此进行宣传。
智库分析，这并非北京第一次利用台湾人士提出的统一主张进行政治操作。中共可能借此将统一塑造成台湾内部具有一定支持基础的政治选项，同时将民进党政府描绘成阻碍两岸和平的少数“分离主义者”，为未来可能采取的强硬对台行动寻找政治论述。
不过，报告也强调，尽管北京持续透过资讯战及政治宣传推动统一论述，台湾民众整体仍普遍反对统一，也不接受中国提出的“一国两制”治理模式，显示中共积极操作相关议题，并不代表已获得台湾社会广泛认同。

content:
在此订阅：Apple 播客 | Spotify | YouTube |阴天 | Pocket Casts 就这样，黄仁勋又回到了巅峰。据报道，特朗普总统致电英伟达董事会，鼓励其恢复两周前被赶下台的前首席执行官的职位。特朗普在《Truth Social》上写道，董事会做出了“正确且恰当的决定”，这确保了“不仅是公司的成功和繁荣，也是美国经济的成功和繁荣。”总统看上去很高兴。技术领导者松了口气。股市似乎因这一消息而上涨。然而，许多其他感兴趣的各方仍然存在紧迫的问题。两党议员正计划盘问黄与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情以及相关的国家安全威胁。但刚刚强烈投票反对人工智能、数据中心和富人之间的欺诈行为的美国人将如何接受总统向他的科技首席执行官朋友放行呢？在大西洋广播电台的这一集中，查理·沃泽尔谈论了英伟达、黄仁勋、科技首席执行官的短期思维以及被人工智能劫持的经济。以下是该集的文字记录： 查理·沃泽尔：我们刚刚举行了一次选举，正如您提到的，美国对人工智能和数据中心表示了深切关注，数据中心是所有英伟达芯片的所在地。
一群新的立法者带着美国的授权来到这里，试图控制这个，比如，科技精英阶层，这个人们觉得类似于人质情况的人工智能经济，对吧？你会在华盛顿特区发生所有这些冲突，我认为这将是一场噩梦。我真的这么做。 [音乐] Hanna Rosin：今天，黄仁勋恢复担任芯片制造巨头英伟达董事长。埃隆·马斯克在 X 上发帖称，“错误已被纠正。”总统称这是“正确且恰当的决定”，并发布了一条人工智能生成的表情包，显示黄的举起拳头的姿势与特朗普本人在 2024 年宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒刺杀事件后采取的姿势相同。因此，对于总统、黄仁勋和其他科技巨头来说：秩序已恢复。但对于很多其他人来说——什么？我是汉娜·罗辛。这是大西洋广播电台。距离与总统关系密切的黄承认与一名疑似中国间谍有染仅两周时间。此时此刻，国会领导人仍在继续传唤黄先生就他的事件对国家安全构成的危险作证。与中国围绕间谍活动、人工智能主导地位的摊牌仍然是我们这个时代迫在眉睫的威胁。然而，黄就在他角落的办公室里，穿着他最新的皮夹克。与我一起讨论的是科技作家兼 Galaxy Brain 播客主持人 Charlie Warzel。查理，我们再次在这里谈论这个永不停息的故事。
欢迎来到这个节目。 Warzel：谢谢你邀请我。我两周前就告诉过你这是噩梦般的场景，而我们现在正处于噩梦之中。 Rosin：我知道这是我的第一个问题。所以，当你今天早上醒来得知黄仁勋重返 Nvidia 的消息时，你是否认为，不可能？或者我知道这会发生。我告诉过你了？沃泽尔：老实说，介于两者之间。周日，[财政部长]斯科特·贝森特开始退缩了一些。他参加了——我相信是哥伦比亚广播公司——的一个早间节目，他最初采取了非常强硬的立场，即英伟达董事会需要在公司外部寻找领导力。

Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Just like that, Jensen Huang is back on top. Reportedly, President Trump called Nvidia’s board and encouraged it to reinstate the former CEO, who had been pushed out only two weeks earlier. The board made the “correct and proper decision,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, which ensures the “Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.” The president seemed happy. Tech leaders were relieved. The stock market seemed to rally with the news. A lot of other interested parties, however, still have burning questions. Lawmakers from both parties are planning to grill Huang about the affair he had with a suspected Chinese spy and the related threats to national security. But how will Americans, who just voted resoundingly against AI, data centers, and grift among the rich, receive the president giving a pass to his tech-CEO friend? On this episode of Radio Atlantic , Charlie Warzel talks about Nvidia, Huang, the short-term thinking of tech CEOs, and an economy held hostage by AI. The following is a transcript of the episode: Charlie Warzel: We just had an election where, as you alluded to, America expressed deep concern with artificial intelligence in general, with data centers, which are the thing that house all the Nvidia chips. And you have a class of new lawmakers who are coming in with a mandate from America to try to rein in this, like, tech-elite class, this AI economy that people feel is akin to a hostage situation, right? You’re gonna have, like, all of that collide in D.C., and I think it’s gonna be a nightmare. I really do. [ Music ] Hanna Rosin: Today, Jensen Huang was reinstated as chairman of Nvidia, the chip-manufacturing giant. Elon Musk posted on X, “The mistake has been corrected.” The president referred to it as the “correct and proper decision” and posted an AI-generated meme showing Huang in the same raised-fist pose that Trump himself adopted after the 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania. So for the president, for Huang, and for other tech giants: order restored. For a lot of other people, though—what? I’m Hanna Rosin. This is Radio Atlantic . It’s been just about two weeks since Huang, who is close to the president, admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Congressional leaders are at this very moment continuing to call up Huang to testify about the dangers his affair posed to national security. The showdown with China over spying, over AI dominance, is still a looming threat of our era. And yet, there is Huang, right back in his corner office with his latest leather jacket. Joining me to discuss is tech writer and host of the Galaxy Brain podcast Charlie Warzel. Charlie, we are here once again talking about the story that never stops giving. Welcome to the show. Warzel: Thank you for having me. I told you this is the nightmare scenario two weeks ago, and here we are in the nightmare. Rosin: I knew that was my first question. So when you woke up this morning to the news that Huang was reinstated at Nvidia, do you think, No way ? Or I knew this was gonna happen. I told you so ? Warzel: Somewhere in between, honestly. It was starting to get—on Sunday, [Treasury Secretary] Scott Bessent sort of walked back a little bit. He was on—I believe on CBS—one of the morning shows, and he initially took this very strident position that the Nvidia board needed to look outside the company for leadership. And then when pressed on it again, he kind of backtracked and said, Well, you know, Jensen Huang is actually now on the outside . And so that signaled a little to me that this week could get a little crazy. I didn’t anticipate it happening this quickly, though. Rosin: I mean, there has been a lot of reporting that President Trump was involved in the decision, that he called into the Nvidia board meeting to advocate for the return of Huang. What do we know so far about the president’s involvement? Warzel: I mean, this is—I don’t know if it’s unprecedented. But this is a lot of involvement from the president of the United States in a publicly traded company’s personnel decisions to—he said he both intervened directly and indirectly, whatever indirectly means. But there were calls, supposedly. There have been communications over the recent weeks with Trump and Jensen Huang, who are cellphone buddies. It’s remarkable. The hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman said that the wisdom of the crowd has spoken , which I think is a very odd way to describe the president of the United States intervening in the workings of a corporate board. But hey, the wisdom of a crowd has spoken, I guess. Rosin: Okay, so what we know so far is that the president was probably heavily involved in the decision to return back to the top of this company someone who was implicated in a national-security scandal. So it’s not obvious why a president would intervene in that way. So let’s unpack it a little bit. One theory why Trump would intervene in this way is the economy, right? Warzel: So there’s a lot here. As we talked about on a previous episode of this, as a lot of people, including myself, have written about and reported on: Nvidia, in some ways, can be seen as , like, a load-bearing block of the global economy, right? They both power the AI boom with their chips. They also invest into the AI companies through this, like, five-layer cake that Jensen Huang helped create, the circular financing, right? So they both power the boom; they finance the boom. That makes them very critical to the global economy. There are a lot of people who argue that Jensen Huang essentially, like, is the one man whose fate determines whether the market goes up and down. Nvidia stock for a while was down, but the rest of the economy was doing okay. It was kind of shouldering this. And then late last week, there was a pretty big sell-off led by a lot of tech stocks. And a lot of the year’s gains in the S&P 500 were lost. So people were kind of freaking out. I think it’s also no coincidence that this was announced—Huang’s reinstatement came—just, you know, right before the markets opened on Monday, after this huge sell-off on Friday. So the economy is a big part of this. Donald Trump believes, according to all the reporting that we’ve seen, that Jensen Huang is a critical part of the AI boom, which is, you know, propping up the rest of the stock market. Rosina: So it’s not just that Nvidia is too big to fail. It too much of a risk. It’s Jensen Wang, specifically? Warzel: That’s the belief. I mean, that’s at least what a lot of these tech leaders are saying too. So there’s really, like, three cohorts that have been agitating for this. One is Nvidia shareholders, who, obviously, Jensen Huang has made them tons and tons of money, especially if you’ve been a shareholder for a very long time in the company. But even anyone who got in after the ChatGPT revolution has seen huge gains, a stock split. So they want this guy back because he’s made them a lot of money. Then you have the Silicon Valley–elite class. I would argue the Silicon Valley–elite class wants this because they want the AI boom to continue. They have a lot riding on this. All the AI CEOs have a whole bunch of investments of their own that are predicated on all the numbers going up and up and up. But also, I think, there’s a cultural reason for this, which is: They do not want to see arguably the greatest visionary, the most irreplaceable CEO in Silicon Valley ousted, because it means that they could be ousted. It means that the CEO is vulnerable, that the visionary founder is vulnerable. I think that’s, like, a very big part of this. This is one of the existential crises that these guys have been going through, because everyone thought that Jensen was too big to fail. The fact that he had to resign after all this pressure and the board didn’t want him back is, I think to them, a very, very scary proposition because it means they can no longer act with impunity. So that was one of the reasons. And then I think you have Donald Trump, who wanted the economy to keep going on his watch, and this was the thing, the lever he thought he could pull to make number go up. Rosin: So it’s like there’s a Silicon Valley myth of a genius, and Trump has used the word genius recently. And that’s a cultural trope, but it’s also real because it drives the stock market. So it’s kind of a circular logic around this word visionary and genius that you just mentioned. Warzel: Yeah, I mean, I think that so much of stock markets, it’s a confidence game. And I don’t mean that in the sense of: It’s a con. I mean, it’s about having confidence in the market, having confidence in the direction of things. For so long, we have been talking about the economy as being propped up by AI, and we’ve been talking about AI in America as having all this very peculiar circular financing, about Is this a bubble? Is this not a bubble? And there’s this idea around all of it of extreme precarity, right? That all of this is contingent on a big bet that has been made, both about the technology succeeding but also about all of this different type of financing and all this historic investment actually meaning something and going somewhere. You need confidence from all of these investors, from all of these folks. Jensen Huang is somebody who, for this class of people, projected a lot of confidence and instilled a lot of confidence in the direction of where the economy and where the AI boom is going. So with him out of it, there was a lot of uncertainty. We were starting to see that in the markets. This freaked a lot of people out. Rosin: Right, and they don’t like uncertainty. Okay, let me run another Trump motivation by you. Lately, Trump has been talking about Alice Huang—the woman who Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with and who U.S. intelligence officials are suspecting to be a spy—has been sort of diminishing her role. He said recently, “Every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy.” Now we’ve heard this from the president, not from U.S. intelligence officials. And I was wondering if there’s something in here about Trump minimizing affairs because of his own history, sort of minimizing the importance of this kind of scandal taking down a great leader. Warzel: I think it’s not only just Trump; it’s all these folks we’re talking about in Silicon Valley. They’ve all been approaching this scandal not from the geopolitical angle of this, but from the moral-infidelity angle, right? Saying, you know, Everyone has their foibles; everyone is flawed; geniuses can be flawed too. Everyone deserves a second chance . And it’s really not a question about morality. There’s obviously, you know, the corporate-HR level of things, which is that there’s been reporting about Huang having affairs with employees in the company, including a direct report. Alice Huang was also a client of Nvidia’s, of Jensen Huang, so there’s an impropriety there. But that’s not the thing that people, that lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are upset about right now. They’re upset about the fact that Alice Huang has this alleged tie to Chinese intelligence, and what, if anything, this did to the larger geopolitical question: whether Megaspeed, this company she worked with, was skirting U.S. chip-export bans, allowing Nvidia chips to get into China or to be used by China in these remote-access data centers; or whether or not Alice Huang was reporting on things that Jensen Huang was doing; whether she had access to any of his devices or anything like that—all of those geopolitical concerns. So it’s interesting to watch both Trump and all these executives sort of not talk about that, and just focus on this other morality play. But I think what we know is actually very troubling. There’s good evidence to suggest that a lot of chip-smuggling was going on. We don’t know whether Huang and Nvidia were directly related to this, but we know that Megaspeed certainly had some role to play in this ecosystem. And Megaspeed, it should be said, has declined all allegations of wrongdoing here. And The New York Times reported on Sunday that Alice Huang had been keeping in touch with an agent in the Chinese intelligence service for over a year. She’d been speaking with this person and staying in contact with them while she was maintaining this relationship with Jensen Huang. So that’s a lot of time. And it’s very interesting to see that report come out on Sunday and have him get reinstated on Monday. [ Music ] Rosin: When we come back, we talk about how this is more than just an economic story. [ Break ] Rosin: So right now, at this moment, there are two camps. There’s the President Trump–Jensen Huang tech-leader camp. They want Jensen Huang to come back. But the other track, which is the national-security track, is continuing to move forward. Congressional leaders are still asking Jensen Huang to come and testify. And polls show that Americans actually do care about the national-security risks involved here. So presumably, the story—you and I are gonna be talking about this again. This story is not going to go away. Let’s take the congressional testimonies first. What does it look like if you have Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, testifying before Congress with the president’s backing—as opposed to what could have been, which is Jensen Huang, a citizen, not beholden to the company, not the CEO, and without the support of the president? Warzel: In an interesting way, this is just a way bigger scandal now. Like, this is a way bigger, thornier, more intense, more interesting scandal. Which, again, if you’re Donald Trump—and, also, people who care about, you know, Nvidia’s relationship to the global economy and the AI boom—the logic doesn’t fully make sense there, right? You would probably want this to go away rather than become, like, the central story of Washington, D.C., for the next 12 months or so. It remains to be seen whether Huang will just come there and plead the Fifth, right? Just say, like, absolutely nothing because basically anything he could say seems like it may or may not jeopardize Nvidia’s position, a bunch of other people. He is now in charge of this company. It’s also going to absolutely invigorate the investigations, again, which you’re seeing are coming from both China hawks or just people who are very upset about the way that this has been handled by the Trump administration and Trump’s involvement in getting him reinstated. I sort of don’t have words for how charged this is going to be. We just had an election where, as you alluded to, America expressed deep concern with artificial intelligence in general, with data centers, which are the thing that house all the Nvidia chips. And you have a class of new lawmakers who are coming in with a mandate from America to try to rein in this, like, tech-elite class, this AI economy that people feel is akin to a hostage situation, right? You have all of these people saying, If you don’t let us build what we wanna do and act the way that we wanna do, then the numbers gonna go down. All this, you know—the bubble’s gonna pop, and good luck, right? Nice economy you got there; hope nothing happens to it , sort of situation. You’re gonna have, like, all of that collide in D.C., and I think it’s gonna be a nightmare. I really do. Rosin: Yeah, that’s absolutely correct because if there is one desire from this midterm flip, it’s accountability. Like, let us enter an era of accountability where rich people don’t get to get away with whatever they want to get away with. That’s what the people seem to be asking for, both in their concerns about corruption, their concerns about data centers, everything that you just mentioned. And this just feels like a sort of pushback to all that. Warzel: Absolutely. And I think that a lot of people are gonna have stuff to prove here, right? They’re gonna wanna make an example out of all of this. And I was talking to somebody in Silicon Valley this morning about this, and they were saying to me that the election really showed this really short-term political thinking, right? The tech leaders were so focused on the AI bet that they allowed themselves to get caught up in, you know, hitching their wagon to Trump and the MAGA situation, right? Like, all the donations for the ballroom, the standing behind him at the inauguration, all of the meetings, the fawning, and all of that. And not seeing that the political winds could blow, you know, in other directions, that hitching your star to this guy so completely was a bad calculation. It’s because they had this short-term thinking. And this person described this to me as, like, another perfect example of the short-term thinking. Like, yes, we solved this problem in the very near term. The stock market is gonna rally now on all of this. But what’s it gonna mean for this to become a far bigger political scandal? Like, what is that going to mean potentially to, you know, how the Democrats are going to position themselves against AI in 2028? Like, it seems like they are playing checkers instead of, you know, the seven-dimensional chess that they always claim to be playing. Rosin: Yeah. Well, Charlie, it looks like there’s gonna be a showdown, and I look forward to talking to you about it when it unfolds. Thank you so much for explaining this to us. Warzel: Yeah. Absolutely. Happy to be here. Rosin: That is all for today’s show. [ Music ] Rosin: This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It was engineered by Miguel Carrascal and has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of podcasts, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here today, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can find them on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page. You can find them on Apple or Spotify or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And you can subscribe to this publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Hanna Rosin.

title: Hong Kong doctor found guilty over fraudulently issuing over 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemptions
zh_title: 香港医生因欺诈性发放超过 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免而被判有罪
summary: 一名香港医生被指控在大流行期间欺诈性地签发约 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免证书，被判以不诚实的意图访问计算机罪。 BioNTech Covid 疫苗。照片：BioNTech。大江城在不认罪后于周五在区域法院接受判决。他还被判犯有洗钱罪。该诊所的一名志愿者 Kriselle Young 也因恶意访问计算机而被判有罪。检方称，两人于2022年2月至9月期间串谋诈骗卫生局
content:
一名香港医生被指控在大流行期间欺诈性地签发约 3,700 份 Covid-19 疫苗豁免证书，被判以不诚实的意图访问计算机罪。 BioNTech Covid 疫苗。照片：BioNTech。大江城在不认罪后于周五在区域法院接受判决。他还被判犯有洗钱罪。该诊所的一名志愿者 Kriselle Young 也因恶意访问计算机而被判有罪。据检方称，两人在 2022 年 2 月至 9 月期间合谋诈骗卫生局，不诚实地声称一些患者在健康上不适合接种 Covid-19 疫苗。戴秉国发放了 3,751 份疫苗豁免，每份收费在 1,000 港元至 4,000 港元之间。在 Covid-19 大流行期间，公众必须满足疫苗接种要求才能进入餐馆、健身房和其他指定场所。湾仔区域法院。资料图片：HKFP。欧内斯特·林法官在作出判决时表示，该诊所利用“自私”公众的“不合理、不科学的恐惧”来获取商业利益。他表示，戴某作为一名医生，有足够的医学知识，能够了解医院管理局的指引。然而，他给予疫苗豁免只是因为他的病人付钱给他，而不是在评估他们的医疗状况之后。
林说，杨不是受过训练的医生，但她向诊所介绍病人，并给护士分配工作。法官补充说，她故意协助戴输入虚假信息。警方诱捕行动 在一次导致两人被捕的卧底行动中，三名警察乔装成病人，前往戴的诊所请求豁免 Covid-19 疫苗，称他们害怕接种疫苗。戴发布了豁免，其中包括针对一名未出席任命的军官的儿子的豁免。一名妇女在购物中心外扫描她的 LeaveHomeSafe 应用程序。照片：香港政府一站通。戴在审判期间作证说，他并没有盲目地向患者提供豁免，称他们患有胃炎、胸痛、哮喘和其他使他们不适合接种疫苗的疾病。杨也作证说，她是诊所的志愿者，她相信戴的判断。她说她从来没有想到他滥用了豁免证书的发放。当检方询问她向患者发送的一条 WhatsApp 消息，上面写着“别担心，[它]肯定会发放”时，杨否认向患者保证他们将能够获得豁免证书，而是说她是在安慰他们。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong doctor accused of fraudulently issuing around 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemption certificates during the pandemic has been found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent. BioNTech Covid vaccine. Photo: BioNTech. Tai Kong-shing received his verdict at the District Court on Friday after pleading not guilty. He was also found guilty of money laundering. A volunteer at the clinic, Kriselle Young, was also found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent. According to the prosecution, the pair conspired to defraud the Health Bureau between February and September 2022 by dishonestly claiming that some patients were medically unfit to receive the Covid-19 vaccine. Tai handed out 3,751 vaccine exemptions, charging between HK$1,000 and HK$4,000 each. During the Covid-19 pandemic, members of the public were required to meet vaccination requirements to access restaurants, gyms and other specified premises. District Court in Wan Chai. File photo: HKFP. Delivering the verdict, Judge Ernest Lin said the clinic made use of the “unreasonable, unscientific fears” of “selfish” members of the public for commercial gain. He said Tai, as a doctor, had sufficient medical knowledge to understand the Hospital Authority’s guidelines. Yet he gave out vaccine exemptions simply because his patients were paying him, rather than after assessing their medical conditions. Lin said that Young was not a trained medical practitioner, but that she introduced patients to the clinic and allocated work to the nurses. She knowingly assisted Tai in inputting false information, the judge added. Police sting operation During an undercover operation that led to the pair’s arrest, three police officers disguised themselves as patients and visited Tai’s clinic to request Covid-19 vaccine exemptions, saying they were afraid to get the jab. Tai issued the exemptions, including one for an officer’s son who was not at the appointment. A woman scans her LeaveHomeSafe app outside a shopping mall. Photo: GovHK. Tai testified during the trial that he did not blindly give out exemptions to patients, saying they had suffered from gastritis, chest pain, asthma and other conditions that made them unfit for the vaccine. Young also testified, saying that she was a volunteer at the clinic and that she trusted Tai’s judgement. She said she never thought that he had abused the issuing of exemption certificates. When asked by the prosecution about a WhatsApp message she had sent to a patient reading “don’t worry, [it’ll] definitely be issued,” Young denied reassuring the patient that they would be able to obtain an exemption certificate, saying instead that she was comforting them.

title: In Taiwan, investors ‘really happy’ at Jensen Huang’s return
zh_title: 在台湾，投资者对黄仁勋的回归“非常高兴”
summary: 周二，台湾投资者欣喜若狂，因为黄仁勋在突然退出导致股价暴跌不到两周后重返英伟达，台湾以科技股为主的股市飙升逾 9%。台北 101 大楼上的一条信息写着：“台湾爱 Jensen。”照片：@VVTing2026，来自 X. 黄出生于台湾，在访问期间像摇滚明星一样受到欢迎，为这个处于全球人工智能热潮中心的岛屿创造了巨额财富。今年岛上的投资者纷纷涌入股市，其中越来越多的人借钱购买繁荣的股票
content:
周二，台湾投资者欣喜若狂，因为黄仁勋在突然退出导致股价暴跌不到两周后重返英伟达，台湾以科技股为主的股市飙升逾 9%。台北 101 大楼上的一条信息写着：“台湾爱 Jensen。”照片：@VVTing2026，来自 X. 黄出生于台湾，在访问期间像摇滚明星一样受到欢迎，为这个处于全球人工智能热潮中心的岛屿创造了巨额财富。今年，随着基准指数创下历史新高，岛上的投资者纷纷涌入股市，越来越多的人借钱购买蓬勃发展的科技行业的股票。尽管许多人对黄与一名美国官员怀疑为中国情报机构工作的女性的恋情持悲观态度，但他们更担心的是丑闻对其投资的影响。 “看到他回来让我真的很高兴，”33 岁的教育行业工作人员安迪·陈 (Andy Chen) 说。 “网上大家都在开玩笑，‘黄爸爸事件’给了很多人抄底的机会。” Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 5 月 19 日在台湾台北举行的 Computex 2025 上发表主题演讲。照片：Nvidia。台交所上周暴跌 17.5%，促使政府出手干预稳定市场。但周二，在芯片巨头台积电和联发科股价上涨 10% 的推动下，该指数飙升逾 9%。
英伟达在纽约的股价飙升了 31.5%，使该公司的市值增加了超过 9000 亿美元。“前天和前几天，每个人都非常痛苦，因为我们的净资产缩水了，”30 岁的财务经理 Jennifer Lin 告诉法新社。林说，黄回到英伟达“是一个非常好的决定”。 “我的股票回来了，我的股票市值也恢复了……心情真好。”尽管英伟达的回归似乎稳定了这家芯片巨头以及更广泛的股市和人工智能生态系统，但到底发生了什么仍然存在疑问。有人猜测黄的外遇和突然离开公司是一个阴谋的一部分。 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 出席在华盛顿特区安德鲁·W·梅隆礼堂举行的白宫人工智能峰会。 2025 年 7 月 23 日。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。 36 岁的制药公司员工雪莉·施 (Sherry Shih) 告诉法新社：“一个企业家的私生活会对全球经济产生如此巨大的影响，我感到非常惊讶。” “整个事情发展得如此之快，让你觉得幕后有什么事情吗？”林更加强调：“我认为有人陷害了他。”陈说，英伟达最近的惊人业绩让这家科技巨头的董事会“别无选择，只能要求他回来”。 “当然，他的私人道德行为很糟糕，”陈承认。 “但生意归生意，个人归个人。
他的个人行为并不能抹杀他对公司运营、对世界、对台湾的贡献。”

【原文 English Original】
Taiwanese investors rejoiced on Tuesday as the island’s tech-heavy stock market soared more than nine percent following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia less than two weeks after his abrupt exit sent shares plummeting. A message on Taipei 101 reads, “Taiwan loves Jensen.” Photo: @VVTing2026, via X. Huang, who was born in Taiwan and feted like a rock star during his visits, has generated huge amounts of wealth for the island at the centre of the global AI boom. Investors on the island have piled into the stock market this year, a growing number of them borrowing money to buy shares in the booming tech sector, as the benchmark index hit record highs. Though many took a dim view of Huang’s affair with a woman US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, their greater concern was the scandal’s impact on their investments. “Seeing him come back makes me really happy,” said Andy Chen, 33, who works in the education industry. “Everyone online is joking that the ‘Papa Huang incident’ gave a lot of people a chance to bottom‑fish and buy in.” Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang gives a keynote speech at Computex 2025 in Taipei, Taiwan, on May 19, 2025. Photo: Nvidia. The Taiex plunged 17.5 percent last week, prompting the government to intervene to stabilise the market. But it soared more than nine percent Tuesday, boosted by gains of 10 percent in chip giants TSMC and MediaTek. Nvidia rocketed an eye-watering 31.5 percent in New York, adding more than US$900 billion to the firm’s market value. “Everyone was really miserable the day before yesterday and the previous few days, because our net worth shrank,” Jennifer Lin, a 30-year-old finance manager, told AFP. Huang’s return to Nvidia “is a very good decision”, Lin said. “My stock has come back, the market value of my shares has recovered too… I’m in a really good mood.” While the return to Nvidia appears to have stabilised the chip giant and the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, there are still questions over what really happened. Some people speculated that Huang’s affair and sudden departure from the company had been part of a conspiracy. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the White House AI Summit at Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, DC. on July 23, 2025. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. “I feel it’s quite surprising that the private life of a single entrepreneur could have such a huge impact on the global economy,” Sherry Shih, 36, a pharmaceutical company employee told AFP. “The way the whole thing has developed so quickly just makes you think is there something going on behind the scenes?” Lin was more emphatic: “I think someone set him up.” Nvidia’s recent blockbuster results had given the tech giant’s board “no choice but to ask him to come back”, Chen said. “Of course, his private moral conduct is bad,” Chen conceded. “But business is business, personal is personal. His personal behaviour doesn’t erase his contributions to the company’s operations, to the world, and to Taiwan.”

东盟秘书长警告泰国与柬埔寨将再次发生冲突，对敲定南海协议持乐观态度

更新于 2026 年 11 月 24 日 06:31
高金胡恩警告说，除非谈判加快，否则脆弱的泰国和柬埔寨停火可能会失败。他表示，新加坡作为 2027 年主席国，可以帮助防止“再次可能爆发的战斗”。
高说，新加坡也可能帮助完成与中国的南海行为准则谈判。他表示，草案已获得约 80% 的同意，但法律形式和执行仍需改进。
他表示，东盟将继续与缅甸接触，同时敦促减少暴力、提供援助和包容性政治进程。他还支持主要经济计划，包括东盟数字经济框架协议和东盟电网。
雅加达 — — 在新加坡准备于 2027 年担任该地区组织主席之际，东盟秘书长高金宏警告说，除非两国加强谈判，否则泰国和柬埔寨之间脆弱的停火可能会陷入新一轮战斗。
高在接受《海峡时报》独家采访时表示，尽管东盟历届主席国努力结束冲突，但两国之间的谈判几乎没有取得任何进展，导致边境局势容易受到新的敌对行动的影响。
他表示相信新加坡能够帮助双方重返谈判桌，并将新加坡描述为“小国家，大外交”。
“我们不应该允许第三轮冲突发生。我认为我们必须防止再次爆发战斗，”他指的是 2025 年发生的两轮边境冲突。
高锟对新加坡能够帮助完成东盟与中国就南海行为准则（COC）进行的长期谈判表示强烈乐观，尽管该准则的法律性质和实施存在棘手问题。
他发表此番言论之前，菲律宾于 11 月 17 日在马尼拉举行的东盟峰会上正式将东盟轮值主席国职位移交给新加坡。新加坡将于 2027 年 1 月 1 日（即东盟成立 60 周年）接任这一职务。
新加坡宣布以“深化一体化，扩大伙伴关系”为主席国主题，重点加强经济合作，落实重大区域倡议。
据总部位于布鲁塞尔的国际危机组织称，泰国和柬埔寨沿 800 公里边界的长期领土争端于 2025 年 7 月和 12 月爆发战斗，造成至少 150 人死亡、约 100 万人流离失所。
尽管双方都互相指责对方违反协议，但当年 12 月 27 日达成的停火协议已基本维持。
马来西亚在 2025 年作为东盟主席国帮助促成和平努力，菲律宾在 2026 年继续这些努力。2027 年，新加坡将接管东盟观察员小组的领导权，负责监督停火。
高说，涉及两国外交部、国防部、武装部队和边境当局的双边机制应该投入运行，但“到目前为止……还没有发生太多事情”。
